title: Designing for Amplifying Voices-Supporting Bangladesh's Low-Income Ready-Made Garment Workers Through Technology Amid COVID-19 Pandemic: Interview Study Among Workers.
abstract: Background The ready-made garments (RMG) industry is a crucial component of Bangladesh's economy, using over 4 million workers from low-income backgrounds who often neglect their health care needs. Historically, this sector has faced criticism for labor exploitation, unsafe working conditions, and rights violations, as highlighted by tragic accidents resulting in loss of life. Compliant factories may uphold higher labor standards, but many noncompliant factories expose workers to poor conditions, increasing health risks. The COVID-19 pandemic intensified vulnerabilities, leading to widespread factory closures and job losses, increased health risks, and left millions of workers without wages. Although the government attempted to provide some relief, it fell short in offering job security, social protection, health services, and emergency assistance. Limited access to technology due to digital literacy gaps further hinders these workers, who primarily use basic mobile phones for communication rather than accessing health or emergency services. Thus, there is a pressing need to develop a sustainable system that capitalizes on their existing technological familiarity. Objective Our goal was to gain a deep understanding of RMG workers' experiences, focusing on their work environments, technological interactions related to health care management, and the impacts of COVID-19 on their circumstances. This understanding aims to inform the design of a technology-based framework that is both sustainable and contextual. Methods In phase 1, we conducted in-person interviews with 55 RMG workers, comprising 32 female and 23 male participants from urban and suburban areas of Dhaka and Gazipur, before the pandemic. Participants were aged between 18 and 40 years. In phase 2, we reconnect with 12 phase 1 participants during the pandemic and also consulted 3 stakeholders from RMG factories via phone. Each interview, conducted in Bengali, was recorded with consent, totaling 846 minutes of discussion that were translated and transcribed. Thematic analysis was used to analyze the results. Results Insights gathered revealed variations in working conditions, personal experiences, perceptions of health care, lifestyle choices, and technology use tied to factory compliance. Workers at compliant factories had better health care support and used technology more effectively than those in noncompliant settings. The pandemic drastically altered the landscape for all workers, heightening health and safety concerns and shortages of emergency assistance. The RMG sector faces significant challenges, highlighting the urgent need for targeted emergency relief and health services. Conclusions This research examined the challenges and technology use among RMG workers during the pandemic, with a focus on health care perspectives. Based on our findings, we proposed a technology-based framework called VOICE (Virtual Outlet for Integrated Community Engagement) that connects workers with service providers through a simplified interface. This aims to assist marginalized communities during emergencies and enhance their overall well-being.

title: Atendimentos e procedimentos em um serviço de urgência bucal antes, durante e após a pandemia de COVID-19: uma análise de séries temporais de 5 anos
abstract: Objective: To analyze and compare trends in visits and procedures performed at an Oral Emergency Service during the pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic periods of the COVID-19 pandemic. Method: Longitudinal study analyzing 76,530 records of dental visits and procedures performed at the Dental Emergency Service in the municipality of Piracicaba, São Paulo, Brazil, between January 2019 and October 2023. The time series were decomposed using LOESS to identify trends and seasonality. After adjusting the data for autocorrelation and removing the seasonal effect, control charts were constructed assuming a negative binomial distribution, and generalized additive mixed models (GAMMs) were fitted, also assuming a negative binomial distribution. The chi-square test was used to assess the association between procedure type and year. A significance level of 5% was adopted. Result: In April 2020, visits decreased by 30.2% compared with the previous month and by 39.7% compared with the same month of the previous year. Procedures decreased by 29.1% compared with the previous month and by 39.5% compared with the same month of the previous year. Tooth extractions were the most frequent procedure in all years, accounting for approximately 73% of procedures, followed by temporary sealing of pulpal cavities, accounting for approximately 16%. Conclusion: Demand for emergency dental services declined sharply during the COVID-19 pandemic, followed by a gradual recovery from 2021 onward.

title: The association between green space, socioeconomic deprivation, and COVID-19 infection: a population-based cross-sectional study
abstract: Objectives To assess the association between green space, socioeconomic deprivation, and infection with COVID-19 in Northern Ireland (NI). Methods This cross-sectional study included all NI individuals who were tested for COVID-19 in 2020 and 2021 (N = 519,005). Analyses were conducted using multilevel logistic regression models. The proportion of green space was measured within neighborhoods in 2020 and expressed as quintiles. Results Of the participants, 318,198 (61.31%) had records of testing positive for COVID-19. The results indicated that individuals living in areas with higher woodland cover had lower odds of reporting a positive COVID-19 test result (e.g., fifth quintile: OR = 0.939; 95% CI = 0.894, 0.987). However, individuals living in areas with higher grassland cover had higher odds of reporting a positive COVID-19 test result (e.g., fifth quintile: OR = 1.062; 95% CI = 1.018, 1.108). These associations were stronger in deprived neighborhoods. Conclusion Woodland may provide opportunities for safer social contact while attempting to balance the risk of viral transmission and the potential for positive health behaviors, particularly in more socioeconomically deprived areas. The government should work with urban planners and improve the availability of green spaces as part of future pandemic preparedness strategies.

title: The Role of Soluble Tumor Necrosis Factor Receptor II as a Prognostic Marker in Severe COVID-19
abstract: Objective: To investigate the clinical disease characteristics and standard laboratory parameters in relation to specific cytokine biomarkers associated with COVID-19 sequelae and to elucidate their correlations with disease severity, respiratory support requirements, and patient outcomes Study Design: Case control studyPlace and Duration of Study: This study was conducted at the Diyala, Iraq, from 1st December 2024 to 30th April 2025. Methods: Seventy four participants were enrolled and divided in two groups, patient group and control group. Patient group comprised 44 participants and control group consisting of thirty participants. The Iraqi Ministry of Health devised the COVID-19 severity protocol, and those steps were used to grade the patients. Results: There was a significant indicators of disease due to their relationship with COVID-19 and a high correlation between the severity of COVID-19 and inflammatory markers, including TNFRII, while blood cells,neutrophils and lymphocytes. There was a substantial rise in tumor necrosis factor receptor II levels (P<0.001) between the control and sick groups. Conclusion: The levels of tumor necrosis factor receptor II, white blood cells, neutrophils, and lymphocytes, all of which were consistent with the infection, were correlated with the severity of the COVID-19 infection.

title: Limited impact of ivermectin on immune response and transcriptional profiles in mild COVID-19
abstract: Ivermectin (IVM) was tested as a treatment for COVID-19 due to its in vitro antiviral activity and possible immunomodulatory properties. Here, we studied the immunomodulatory effects in a clinical trial involving 24 mild COVID-19 patients who received IVM within 72 h of symptoms onset by comprehensively analyzing immune responses over 28 days. The IVM group had statistically significant increased levels of IgG against the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid compared to the control group at days 4 and 7 post-treatment. IVM did not affect the kinetics of leukocyte subsets or SARS-CoV-2-specific T cells, despite a decrease in naïve CD4 + T cells, which was non-significant after adjusting for multiple comparisons. Although differential gene expression was not observed between IVM-treated and placebo groups, blood transcriptional module analysis revealed statistically significant decreases in innate and antiviral signatures and increases in adaptive signatures over time, with 10 modules upregulated (related to innate responses) and 15 modules downregulated (related to T cells and cell cycle) in the IVM-treated group compared to placebo. In conclusion, despite some weak differences in IVM treated participants, our detailed analyses do not support significant immunomodulatory effects that could benefit disease progression.

IVM did not affect the kinetics of leukocyte subsets or SARS-CoV-2-specific T cells, despite a decrease in naïve CD4 + T cells, which was non-significant after adjusting for multiple comparisons. Although differential gene expression was not observed between IVM-treated and placebo groups, blood transcriptional module analysis revealed statistically significant decreases in innate and antiviral signatures and increases in adaptive signatures over time, with 10 modules upregulated (related to innate responses) and 15 modules downregulated (related to T cells and cell cycle) in the IVM-treated group compared to placebo. In conclusion, despite some weak differences in IVM treated participants, our detailed analyses do not support significant immunomodulatory effects that could benefit disease progression.

title: Evaluating regional diversity in scientific communication: a comparative analysis of COVID-19 preprints and peer-reviewed publications
abstract: Background: The COVID-19 pandemic triggered extensive global research, leading to an unprecedented surge in both peer-reviewed publications and preprints. Despite their widespread use, the implications of preprints for global diversity in scientific communication remain underexplored. This study evaluates how preprints influenced regional diversity in COVID-19 research by analyzing international collaboration networks, social media engagement, and citation patterns compared to peer-reviewed publications.Methods: We conducted a comparative analysis of COVID-19-related peer-reviewed publications indexed in SCOPUS and preprints from MedRxiv (December 2019–November 2022). Regional diversity was evaluated using bibliometric metrics stratified by World Bank income classifications and geographic regions. International collaboration was quantified using network analysis metrics, while publication, dissemination, and social media engagement were assessed through relative ratios. Social media engagement was measured by quoted posts on X (formerly Twitter). Citation counts were compared between articles with preprint history versus those published directly in journals.Results: Authors from Sub-Saharan Africa, Latin America, and the Caribbean showed 3.9–4.5 times higher eigenvector centrality in preprints than in peer-reviewed papers, indicating greater integration into global research networks through preprint platforms. Low-income countries showed higher representation in preprints (P<0.001). Although overall engagement on X was similar for both formats, preprints exhibited higher relative ratios of quoted posts across all income groups. Peer-reviewed articles with preprint history received more citations (median=10, 25th-75th percentiles: 3–30) than those without (median=3, 25th-75th percentiles: 0–11, P<0.001), especially from low- and middle-income countries.Conclusions: Preprints significantly advanced regional diversity in scientific communication during the COVID-19 pandemic. Preprints enhanced international collaboration networks, particularly benefiting researchers from lower-income regions, facilitated broader social media engagement across all income groups, and conferred meaningful citation advantages for subsequent peer-reviewed publications. These results suggest that preprints represent an important mechanism for promoting more equitable participation in global scientific discourse.

title: Clinical characteristics, pathogen detection, and severity markers among children with acute respiratory infections during the COVID-19 restriction period: a retrospective hospital-based study
abstract: Background The epidemiology of pediatric acute respiratory infections (ARIs) changed substantially during the COVID-19 (coronavirus disease 2019) pandemic, largely because of school closures, masking, reduced travel, and other non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs). However, hospital-based data from the restriction period remain useful for describing pathogen detection patterns, clinical severity, and markers of adverse clinical course. Methods We conducted a retrospective hospital-based study of 62 children aged <18 years who were evaluated for ARI symptoms and underwent real-time fluorescent quantitative nucleic acid testing for common respiratory pathogens, including respiratory viruses and Mycoplasma pneumoniae . Demographic, clinical, laboratory, treatment, severity, and outcome variables were extracted from medical records. Continuous variables were summarized using medians and ranges, and group comparisons used non-parametric tests. Given the small sample size and sparse severe-outcome events, the study was not powered to detect small effect sizes, and regression findings were interpreted conservatively as hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory. Results The median age was 9 years (range, 1–17), and 33 patients (53.2%) were female. Most children had mild disease (37/62, 59.7%); 19 (30.6%) had moderate disease and 6 (9.7%) had severe disease. Intensive care unit (ICU) admission was recorded in 6 patients (9.7%), and mechanical ventilatory or noninvasive respiratory support in 9 (14.5%). Fever (43.5%) and cough (22.6%) were the most frequent presenting symptoms. Median oxygen saturation was 94.7% (range, 87.2–97.8). Respiratory virus detection was documented in 15 children (24.2%). Human rhinovirus was detected in 15 children (24.2%), human bocavirus in 9 (14.5%), and Mycoplasma pneumoniae in 10 (16.1%); co-detection was recorded in 14 children (22.6%). Lower SpO2 and longer symptom duration differed significantly across severity categories (both p < 0.001). In exploratory logistic regression, each additional day of symptoms was associated with higher odds of hospital admission/continued inpatient management [odds ratio [OR], 1.4; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.03–1.93; p = 0.022]. Sex was not significantly associated with clinical severity or laboratory parameters. Conclusions In this small hospital-based pediatric ARI cohort during the COVID-19 restriction period, severe disease was uncommon, and oxygen saturation and symptom duration were the most clinically coherent markers of greater severity. The observed pathogen detection pattern is compatible with pandemic-era disruption of respiratory pathogen circulation, but causal conclusions about NPIs require larger denominator-based studies with pre-pandemic and post-restriction comparison groups.

title: Changes in birth certificate-reported prevalence of congenital anomalies at live birth during the COVID-19 pandemic: a nationwide study of 26 million United States live births
abstract: Background Although the majority of studies have indicated that maternal severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection and coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) vaccination are not associated with neonatal birth defects, it is relevant to examine whether the disease burden changed during the COVID-19 pandemic, as other influencing factors may have also changed. We aimed to compare the birth certificate-reported prevalence of congenital anomalies at live birth before and during the pandemic. Methods Using public birth data, all live births from 2016 to 2022 in the United States of America (USA) were retrospectively included. The birth certificate-reported prevalence at live birth of selected congenital anomalies identified from the birth certificate, including anencephaly, meningomyelocele/spina bifida, cyanotic congenital heart disease (CCHD), congenital diaphragmatic hernia, omphalocele, gastroschisis, limb reduction defect, cleft lip, cleft palate, Down syndrome, chromosomal disorder, and hypospadias, was estimated and compared by calendar year of birth using logistic regression. Results A total of 26,345,765 live-born infants from 2016 to 2022 were included. The mean gestational age of the infants was 38.4 weeks (SD = 2.1 weeks), 48.9% were female babies, and 96.7% were singleton. The overall reported prevalence of congenital anomalies was highest in 2018 (3.51‰, 95%CI = 3.45‰–3.57‰) and has since shown a decreasing trend [3.38‰ (95%CI = 3.32‰–3.44‰) in 2019 and 3.35‰ (95%CI = 3.29‰–3.41‰) in 2022]. Using 2019 as a reference, it did not differ in 2020 and 2021 [odds ratio (OR) = 1.01 (0.98–1.03) and OR = 1.00 (0.98–1.03), respectively, after adjusting for maternal age, ethnicity/race, and socioeconomic status] and was slightly lower in 2022 [OR = 0.97 (0.95–0.99)]. For the majority of the congenital anomalies, the reported prevalence during the pandemic (2020–2022) remained unchanged or showed a decreasing trend (i.e., gastroschisis and Down syndrome) compared with that in 2019. The reported prevalence of CCHD was higher in 2021 and 2022 than in 2019. However, the increase had begun before the pandemic, and after correction for multiple comparisons, only the 2021 contrast remained significant. Segmented regression confirmed a significant pre-pandemic upward trend in CCHD with a level change dated to infants born in March 2020. When exposure was re-indexed by estimated year of conception, neither pandemic conception cohort differed from the 2019 conception cohort [2020: OR = 1.03 (0.97–1.09); 2021: OR = 1.02 (0.97–1.08)]. The direction of these results was consistent when stratified by gestational age (≥37 or <37 weeks), with wider intervals in the preterm stratum. Conclusions The birth certificate-reported prevalence of congenital anomalies at live birth did not increase during the COVID-19 pandemic in the USA and decreased for several specific anomalies. The higher reported prevalence of CCHD continues a trend that began before the pandemic and is null once exposure is aligned with organogenesis.

title: A Compartment Model and Deep Learning Approach for Simulating the Dynamic Transmission of Covid-19
abstract: This thesis develops and evaluates two approaches for modelling COVID-19 transmission. The first approach is an ODE-based compartmental model incorporating vaccination and mask usage. The model is analysed through stability analysis, sensitivity analysis, numerical simulation, and differential evolution optimisation. The results show good agreement with observed data. A hybrid CNN–LSTM model is also applied to forecast COVID-19 cases in Victoria and Western Australia, compared with ARIMA-based models.

title: A Sustainable, Quality-by-Design (QbD) Inspired Spectrofluorimetric Method for the Concurrent Analysis of Cetirizine and Montelukast in COVID-19 and Allergic Rhinitis Combination Therapy.
abstract: A novel direct spectrofluorimetric method was developed and validated for simultaneous determination of cetirizine hydrochloride (CTZ) and montelukast sodium (MKT), commonly used in COVID-19 combination therapy. Montelukast was determined using first derivative synchronous fluorescence at 422 nm, corresponding to a zero-crossing point for CTZ. Cetirizine was quantified using a newly applied ratio derivative synchronous fluorescence spectroscopy ( 1 DD-SFS) technique, using MKT (0.1 μg/mL) as a divisor, allowing CTZ measurement at 293 nm. Cetirizine and montelukast native fluorescence was significantly enhanced by micellar solubilization using cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB) and sulfuric acid. A two-level factorial design was employed for method optimization, with optimal conditions incorporating 0.5% w/v CTAB and 0.2-M sulfuric acid. Validation was performed according to ICH guidelines, proving the methods specificity, sensitivity, and robustness. title: Working Remotely from Home During and Post-COVID-19
abstract: Abstract The chapter reviews and analyzes the merits and challenges of people with disabilities in the United Kingdom and United States regarding working from home in the post-pandemic period when a return to office was mandated by both governments. Both countries had similar legislation regarding reasonable accommodations for people with disabilities. The Equality Act 2010 in the United Kingdom was comprehensive, covering disability as one of nine “protected characteristics.” The US ADA Title I focused exclusively on the employment of people with disability. The UK policy showed much more willingness to regulate the labor market during the pandemic and the post-pandemic period and allowed remote working. The US policy demonstrated less interference in the labor market during the pandemic and post-pandemic. The UK government was concerned with employer pushback on remote working and tended to disproportionally affect workers with disability regarding flexible arrangements. The UK policy recognized the right to flexible work, and employees with disabilities still had stronger protection under the “reasonable adjustment” framework. The US federal policy-imposed return-to-office mandate led to a rise in ADA lawsuits regarding the denial of remote work as a reasonable accommodation. The United States carried out the “essesntial functions” test, meaning the key legal question in many US cases was whether remote work eliminated an “essential function” of the job. Although courts aligned with employers vis-à-vis employees’ claims for working remotely, judges in some circuits started considering an employee’s remote work after the pandemic.
journal: Prospects for Employment of Persons with Disabilities in the Post-COVID-19 Era

title: UK and US Policies Regarding Employees with Disabilities During and Post-COVID-19 Pandemic and in a Few Low-Middle-Income-Countries
abstract: Abstract During the COVID-19 pandemic, the United Kingdom and United States prioritized flexible working arrangements and adjustments for employees with disabilities, particularly those at higher risk. In the post-pandemic period, both nations have focused on solidifying these flexible arrangements but have also faced criticism over potentially regressive policies related to disability benefits. The UK approach focused on the expansion of access to work. However, the UK government proposed significant welfare reforms aimed at pushing more people into work. The United States prioritized post-pandemic Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) guidance that solidified the legal precedent for remote work as a reasonable accommodation under the ADA. Employers were required to evaluate renewed requests for remote work based on individual circumstances rather than reverting to pre-pandemic policies. Employers were expected to ensure a safe return-to-office (RTO) process but were not required to eliminate essential job functions to accommodate remote work. Finally, case law in the United States continued to evolve regarding what constituted an “undue hardship” for employers denying remote work, often referencing the successful remote work period during the pandemic. The COVID-19 pandemic disproportionately affected employees with disabilities in Low-Middle-Income-Countries (LMICs), exacerbating preexisting inequalities in employment, income, and access to services. Post-pandemic policies required a more comprehensive and systematic approach to address the deeper structural barriers to inclusion.
journal: Prospects for Employment of Persons with Disabilities in the Post-COVID-19 Era

title: Analisis Perbandingan Biaya Operasional dan Kinerja Keuangan pada Saat Pandemi COVID-19 dan Setelah Pandemi COVID-19 pada Perusahaan Food and Beverage yang Terdaftar di BEI
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic placed considerable pressure on economic activity, including the food and beverage (F&B) industry listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX). This study analyzes differences in operating costs and financial performance of F&B companies during the pandemic (2019–2021) and after the pandemic (2022–2024). Operating costs are measured using the Operating Expense Ratio (OER), while financial performance is assessed through Net Profit Margin (NPM), Current Ratio (CR), and Debt to Equity Ratio (DER). Using a comparative quantitative approach, this study analyzes secondary data from annual financial reports of 15 F&B companies selected through purposive sampling based on complete financial statements and consistent profits during 2019–2024. Normality was tested using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, followed by the Wilcoxon Signed Rank Test at a 5% significance level because the data were not normally distributed. The results show no significant differences in OER (Sig. 0.977), or DER (Sig. 0.252) between the two periods. Descriptively, OER decreased from 26% to 25%, NPM from 7% to 6%, while CR increased from 2.95 to 3.02 times and DER from 0.72 to 0.82. These findings indicate relatively stable operating costs and financial performance among F&B companies despite the pandemic.
journal: Inisiatif: Jurnal Ekonomi, Akuntansi dan Manajemen

title: Frequency of Thrombocytopenia in Patients with COVID-19
abstract: Objective: To determine the frequency of thrombocytopenia in patients with COVID-19. Study Design: Cross sectional study. Place and Duration of Study: Combined Military Hospital, Quetta Pakistan, from Apr 2021 to Mar 2022. Methodology: A total of 225 patients with COVID-19 were selected using non-probability, consecutive sampling. After ethical approval, informed consent platelet count was studied in 2 weeks of hospital admission fulfilling inclusion and exclusion criteria. Results: Two hundred and twenty-five patients, with age ranging from 30 to 60 years and mean 44.89±5.42 years were included in this study, in which 95 patients were COVID-19 survivors and 130 were non-survivors. Blood samples of all patients was collected, and platelet count was studied and categorized into [0-50], [50-100], [100-150], and 150 or more by using unit (×109/L). 2321 tests of platelet count were done, that shows 50×109/L was the lower limit of normal range of platelets. Overall mortality rate per 1000 is 77 out of which was survival rate is 93.4% and death rate (6.6%), moreover mortality rate in patient with platelet [0-50]is (38.80%), [50-100] (25.70%), [100-150] (23.60%), and >150 group (11.70%) respectively. Conclusion: Thrombocytopenia was common in patients with corona virus and platelet count was relatively lower in severe COVID-19 infection and analyzing the gradual decrease in platelet counts may be useful in the prognosis of patients with COVID-19.

title: Public Interest in Stress-Induced Dermatologic Conditions and Psychodermatologic Disorders Before, During, and After the COVID-19 Pandemic: Segmented Regression Analysis.
abstract: Background Psychological stress is known to exacerbate dermatologic conditions such as acne, eczema, and compulsive skin behaviors. The COVID-19 pandemic introduced a global stressor with widely experienced psychosocial effects and potential impacts on skin health. This study analyzes US public interest in stress-induced dermatologic conditions and psychodermatologic disorders to test for pandemic-associated shifts in 6 search terms. Objective This study aimed to assess whether the onset and resolution of the COVID-19 pandemic were associated with changes in Google Search interest in psychodermatologic and stress-related skin conditions in the United States. Methods Monthly relative search volume (RSV; 0-100 scale) for 6 terms ("skin picking," "trichotillomania," "stress rash," "eczema flare up," "dermatillomania," and "anxiety skin picking") was obtained from Google Trends for January 2018 through December 2024 (n=84 monthly observations per term); the 6 primary and 4 secondary exploratory terms were extracted in April 2025 and the 5 synonymic terms in July 2026, using the identical query window. A segmented regression model with break points at the World Health Organization's (WHO) pandemic timeline (March 2020 declaration; May 2023 end of concern) tested for level and slope changes at pandemic onset and post pandemic. Newey-West (heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation consistent) SEs corrected for residual autocorrelation, and joint F tests with Bonferroni and Benjamini-Hochberg (false discovery rate [FDR]) corrections assessed whether each period differed from the prior trend. A sensitivity analysis applied the identical model to 5 synonymic terms, each paired with 1 primary term, and to 4 unpaired, secondary, exploratory terms ("acne," "stress acne," "stress hives," and "hair loss from stress"). Results A total of 2 of the 6 terms showed a statistically significant pandemic-onset effect after correction: "dermatillomania" (level shift +15.20 RSV points; Bonferroni P =.007; FDR P =.007) and "anxiety skin picking" (slope change +0.70 RSV points/month; Bonferroni P =.02; FDR P =.01). "Stress rash," "skin picking," and "eczema flare up" reached significance under FDR correction only ( P =.04, .04, and .03, respectively); "trichotillomania" showed no effect under either correction (FDR P =.08). "Anxiety skin picking," "trichotillomania," and "stress rash" showed postpandemic reversals robust to both corrections. The synonymic sensitivity analysis showed weaker, inconsistent support: only 1 of 5 pairs ("dermatillomania"/"excoriation disorder") showed partial agreement under FDR correction, while the remaining 4 diverged, indicating sensitivity to search-term phrasing. The secondary exploratory analysis found no pandemic-onset effects under either correction. Conclusions Public search interest in a subset of psychodermatologic conditions, specifically "dermatillomania" and "anxiety skin picking," showed statistically significant shifts temporally coinciding with COVID-19 pandemic onset. A sensitivity analysis using synonym terms did not consistently reproduce these findings, indicating sensitivity to both analytic choices and search-term phrasing. These results support further research into psychodermatology and illustrate how public search behavior can reflect societal stress, though causal interpretation is unwarranted from search-volume data alone.

title: A-380 Comparative Analytical Evaluation of Point-of-Care and Centralized Respiratory Assays For Detection of SARS-CoV-2, Influenza, and RSV
abstract: Abstract Background The clinical and operational pressure to provide rapid, accurate respiratory diagnostics demands a strategy that leverages point-of-care and high-throughput assays/systems across the continuum of care. A central tenet of defining any co-existence strategy is to understand the comparative performance characteristics of the chosen assays/systems to be deployed within a diagnostic algorithm. This study compared the ability of two CLIA-waived and two moderate complexity multiplex respiratory assays to detect quantified viral samples at a range of low viral titers. Methods A two-phase study, inclusive of a range-finding and confirmation arm, was conducted using a quantified control material for viral respiratory targets diluted into viral transport media. A 10-fold serial dilution was performed, and replicates (6 for range-finding, 20 for confirmation) of each concentration were evaluated on four multiplex respiratory assays: cobas® liat SARS-CoV-2 & Influenza A/B assay, cobas® liat SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A/B, & RSV assay, cobas® SARS-CoV-2, & Influenza A/B v2 assay, and the cobas® Respiratory 4-flex assay. Analyte detection rates and Ct values were compared across assays. Results Preliminary data indicates that the assays evaluated in this study have similar performance for low titer samples. Similar detection rates were observed for all assays across all concentrations tested Conclusion These findings demonstrate that respiratory assays performed on the cobas® liat and cobas® x800 systems provide similar detections at low viral concentrations. This data validates the use of highly sensitive point-of-care tools alongside centralized systems, ensuring that a multifaceted testing strategy delivers consistent and accurate results regardless of the platform used.

title: Inflammasomes and interferons: new insights into the innate immune response to RSV and SARS-CoV-2 infection in airway epithelial cells
abstract: Respiratory viruses like RSV and SARS-CoV-2 pose significant public health threats, particularly to the young and elderly. Both viruses infect the airway epithelium, with severe disease associated with enhanced highly inflammatory immune responses. To develop novel therapeutics there is an urgent need to understand how specific innate immune responses are activated and regulated by RSV and SARS-CoV-2. Inflammasomes are cytosolic protein complexes that mediate the maturation and release of the pro-inflammatory cytokines interleukin (IL)-1β and IL-18 and pyroptotic cell death. Given inflammasomes trigger potent inflammation that correlates with disease severity, we hypothesised that inflammasome activation may be critical. Inflammasome research has focused primarily on myeloid cells and NLRP3, herein we investigated inflammasome signalling within the airway epithelium using physiologically relevant well-differentiated primary airway epithelial cell cultures (WD-PAECs). We found that although the canonical inflammasome NLRP1 is constitutively expressed and infection upregulates inflammasome-related genes, direct infection-induced activation is minimal. However, crosstalk between epithelial and immune cells significantly potentiates this response. Despite dysregulated inflammasome activation being associated with disease severity, inflammasome activation, in addition to the interferon response was shown to play an important role in cell intrinsic antiviral responses. We demonstrated that IL-1β, bolstered by epithelial-myeloid interactions, plays a crucial role in early antiviral defence against RSV, making inflammasome activation a double-edged sword. Given co-infections account for >30% of all respiratory viral infections, we explored the interactions between RSV and SARS-CoV-2. Our findings revealed bi-directional viral interference patterns, driven by time-dependent induction of type I interferons (IFNs), highlighting their underappreciated role in the airway epithelium's innate armoury. By utilizing primary cell models, this work provides new insights into how the airway epithelium regulates innate immunity and highlights the complex balance between protective antiviral signalling and harmful inflammation during viral infection and co-infection. Thesis is embargoed until 31 July 2027.

title: Communicating Compliance During COVID-19: A Case Study of Police Messaging, Public Health Restrictions, and Mobility Control, 2020–2021
abstract: In New Zealand’s COVID-19 response, the New Zealand Police played a central role in translating public health restrictions into everyday expectations about movement, responsibility and conduct. This article examines 84 news releases and official statements issued between March 2020 and December 2021 using a qualitative single-case design and theory-informed directed content analysis. Releases from the first national lockdown mainly explained unfamiliar rules and appealed to collective responsibility. During the Delta period, education-first language continued, but routine boundary checks and cumulative compliance statistics became more prominent. The corpus shows no simple shift from persuasion to punishment. Police presented extensive monitoring as restrained by placing engagement, warnings and majority cooperation before prosecution or arrest. Read through Foucault’s concepts of disciplinary power, biopolitics and governmentality, the releases formed part of pandemic governance: they defined legitimate movement, established the compliant majority as a norm and made institutional reach publicly visible. The study also brings institutions into the psychosocial account of the pandemic, showing how official messages linked acceptable conduct to collective responsibility and reassurance. The findings highlight a practical issue for pandemic preparedness: agencies that enforce emergency restrictions also explain them, and their communication helps shape the balance between voluntary cooperation and sanction.

title: Cell therapy for Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome and COVID-19
abstract: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) is characterised by acute hypoxaemic respiratory failure and bilateral infiltrates on chest imaging resulting from immune mediated destruction of the alveolar epithelial-endothelial barrier. Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) are a potential therapeutic strategy due to their pleiotropic immunomodulatory, reparative and antimicrobial effects. The aim of this thesis was to explore the role of MSCs in ARDS and COVID-19. Written under the ‘Thesis with Publications’ submission style, it includes reviews of ARDS and MSC therapy, and publications relating to the REALIST (Repair of ARDS with Stromal Cell Administration) trial. REALIST investigated a novel MSC product (ORBCEL-CTM , a population of CD362 enriched allogeneic umbilical cord derived MSCs) in patients with moderate to severe ARDS defined by the Berlin criteria. Phase 1 investigated a single intravenous infusion of ORBCEL-CTM MSCs in a 3+3 open-label dose-escalation study (3 dose cohorts of 3 patients with ARDS receiving either 100, 200 or 400 million cells), establishing that 400 million cells was a safe dose for a phase 2 trial. Phase 2 recruited a cohort of patients with ARDS due to COVID-19. In this sixty-patient, randomised, triple blind placebo-controlled clinical trial a single intravenous infusion of 400 million ORBCEL-CTM MSCs was found to be safe (primary safety outcome serious adverse events up to day 90) but there was no difference in the primary efficacy outcome (oxygenation index at day 7) nor in a range of secondary surrogate outcomes of systemic and pulmonary organ function. Long term follow up to 2 years also found ORBCEL-CTM MSCs to be safe. The final chapter in this thesis presents a critical appraisal of available evidence to explore 1) the feasibility of delivering cell-based therapy for critically ill patients within the UK national health service, 2) the safety and long-term outcomes of MSCs in ARDS and COVID-19, 3) efficacy of MSCs in ARDS and COVID-19, and 4) mechanistic insights regarding MSCs in ARDS and COVID-19.

title: COVID-19 in children: a prospective study investigating host response to SARS-CoV-2.
abstract: This thesis explores the clinical features, immunology, and outcomes of Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C), a severe post COVID-19 condition identified during the early waves of the pandemic. Initially, MIS-C cases required intensive care, with multiple organs affected, particularly the heart and vasculature. The cause and long-term outcomes of MIS-C were unclear, and no diagnostic tests were available.The first part of this thesis reports on the clinical characteristics and potential risk factors for severe disease in a cohort of MIS-C cases from Northern Ireland, providing one of the first studies on long-term outcomes following discharge.The second part applies discovery proteomics to investigate the proteome of children with MIS-C, identifying biological pathways driving the disease, such as chemokine signalling, platelet activation, and complement activation. Comparison with healthy children post-SARS-CoV-2 infection and febrile controls revealed distinct proteomic differences, highlighting pathways uniquely involved in MIS-C, including IFN-γ activation and extracellular matrix organization. Candidate diagnostic biomarkers for MIS-C were identified from proteomic data and verified in the MIS-C cohort, showing potential for distinguishing MIS-C from other febrile illnesses.Finally, the leading hypothesis that increased intestinal permeability allows persistent SARS-CoV-2 spike protein translocation, triggering a superantigenic response, was tested. Although markers of intestinal permeability were elevated in MIS-C, they were also raised in other febrile conditions, and the hypothesis of spike protein superantigenicity was not supported.In summary, this thesis provides new insights into the clinical features, proteomic profile, and outcomes of MIS-C, identifies candidate diagnostic biomarkers, and challenges current hypotheses regarding the condition’s pathogenesis. Thesis embargoed until 31st December 2029

title: The Effect of Antioxidants on COVID-19 Pneumonia: Managements and Future Strategies
abstract: The outbreak of pneumonia caused by the novel coronavirus-2 (nCoV/SARS-CoV-2 2019), which was first reported in Wuhan, China, in late 2019, caused widespread panic among people around the world. But now, more than three years have passed since the outbreak of COVID-19, and the initial panic due to the unknown and rapid spread of this viral infectious disease has today given way to relative calm. There is currently no fully effective drug for this virus, but during the COVID-19 epidemic, some reports indicated that antioxidant compounds were good options for reducing symptoms in hospitalized patients. The aim of this mini-review is to analyze the current knowledge about the relationship between nutrition and antioxidants and the supportive role of these compounds on the immune system, and COVID-19 infection in order to develop appropriate dietary and nutritional programs to prevent infection with other new variants of this virus in the future. Although many review articles have been written about the role of antioxidants on COVID-19 infection, due to sometimes contradictory clinical and nutritional information in different articles, there is still uncertainty about whether antioxidant compounds really play a major role in reducing COVID-19 infections. Can these compounds be used definitively to treat coronavirus infections? If the world were to be hit by such a dangerous epidemic again, how helpful would the results of studies conducted so far on antioxidant compounds be? Since no definitive treatment has been found for COVID-19 yet, proper nutritional selection through balanced meals and the use of proper hygiene methods in selecting, preparing, and storing food could likely be one of the most useful approaches to managing this disease or other pathogenic variants of this virus in the future. In a general conclusion, it can be stated that optimizing public health worldwide is a very urgent matter that must be considered in all circumstances. Public health management and control, even in situations other than dangerous viral epidemics, requires not only knowledge of medical and biological sciences but also all sciences related to lifestyle, social, and behavioral studies, including dietary habits and lifestyle. Changing your eating habits and choosing a healthy diet rich in nutrients, including antioxidants, can help strengthen your immune system and help you overcome diseases.

title: Pan-Coronavirus Protease Engagement and Differentiated Pharmacology of Antiviral Candidate CMX990
abstract: COVID-19 highlighted the need for antivirals that can be rapidly deployed against both current and future coronavirus threats. CMX990 is a clinical stage coronavirus main protease (Mpro) inhibitor bearing a unique trifluoromethoxymethyl ketone warhead. Here, we broadly evaluate its pan-coronavirus target engagement, antiviral breadth, and pharmacologic differentiation. Across a reporter panel of 24 Mpro enzymes spanning alpha-, beta-, delta-, and gamma-coronaviruses, CMX990 retained robust potent activity, including against nirmatrelvir-resistant SARS-CoV-2 variants. In direct comparison, nirmatrelvir and ensitrelvir showed diminished potency against non-SARS-CoV-2 coronaviruses. Live-virus assays corroborated this breadth, with potent, selective activity against SARS-CoV-2, SARS-CoV-1, MERS-CoV, and additional human coronaviruses. Structural studies revealed a conserved covalent binding mode centered on the catalytic Cys of coronavirus Mpro. In serial-passage studies, resistance emerged only after approximately twice as many serial passages under CMX990 selection as under nirmatrelvir selection, without selecting for the canonical nirmatrelvir-resistance substitution E166V. Extracellular washout experiments revealed superior persistence of antiviral activity relative to nirmatrelvir, consistent with durable target engagement. In a murine SARS-CoV-2 infection model, once-daily CMX990 protected against weight loss and reduced lung viral titers to near baseline levels. Collectively, these findings identify CMX990 as a structurally and functionally validated pan-coronavirus protease inhibitor supporting its potential as a pandemic-ready antiviral candidate.

title: Immune Thrombocytopenia Following COVID-19 Vaccination in a Pediatric Patient
abstract: Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) is the most common acquired bleeding disorder in children, with further delineation into primary and secondary causes; it is immune-mediated and typically self-limited.Primary ITP is often seen in children with a history of a preceding infection that has subsequently resolved.Additionally, ITP can be seen in children within six weeks of vaccination with measles-mumps-rubella and varicella, and in adults, ITP has developed following messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccination.We present the case of a three-year-old boy who presented with petechiae and purpura eight days after Moderna COVID-19 vaccination and was found to have severe thrombocytopenia with a platelet count of 3,000/mm3.He was thought to have secondary ITP from COVID-19 vaccination.To date, there have been no published reports of ITP presenting in children following mRNA COVID-19 vaccination.This case brings to attention the possible complication of ITP after COVID-19 vaccination with spontaneous resolution without medical intervention and the need for further clinical monitoring of symptoms after COVID-19 vaccination.

media_mentions.content_title: Immune Thrombocytopenia Following COVID-19 Vaccination in a Pediatric Patient
media_mentions.content: Abstract Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) is the most common acquired bleeding disorder in children, with further delineation into primary and secondary causes; it is immune-mediated and typically self-limited. Primary ITP is often seen in children with a history of a preceding infection that has subsequently resolved. Additionally, ITP can be seen in children within six weeks of vaccination with measles-mumps-rubella and varicella, and in adults, ITP has developed following messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccination. We present the case of a three-year-old boy who presented with petechiae and purpura eight days after Moderna COVID-19 vaccination and was found to have severe thrombocytopenia with a platelet count of 3,000/mm3. He was thought to have secondary ITP from COVID-19 vaccination. To date, there have been no published reports of ITP presenting in children following mRNA COVID-19 vaccination. This case brings to attention the possible complication of ITP after COVID-19 vaccination with spontaneous resolution without medical intervention and the need for further clinical monitoring of symptoms after COVID-19 vaccination. Introduction Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) is the most common acquired bleeding disorder in children and is characterized by isolated thrombocytopenia of <100 × 109/L platelets (normal range for platelets is 150,000-450,000/mm3) [1]. ITP is often seen in children with a history of a preceding viral or acute gastrointestinal infection and presents with signs of mucocutaneous bleeding such as petechiae, purpura, ecchymosis, or epistaxis. ITP has a peak incidence between two and six years of age [2]. Primary ITP is typical in pediatric patients and often benign and self-limited, with spontaneous recovery of platelet counts in three to six months. Secondary ITP can be caused by an underlying autoimmune condition, drugs, malignancy, infections, or immunodeficiency. Vaccination can trigger autoimmunity, with reports of ITP occurring in children after routine vaccination with measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) and varicella, and reports of ITP presenting in adults following messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccination [3]. A causal association between MMR and ITP has been reported with an incidence of 0.087-4 per 100,000 doses seen in children [4]. In May 2025, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Moderna’s next-generation mRNA COVID-19 vaccine for children ages six months through eleven years with at least one underlying condition putting them at high risk for severe outcomes from COVID-19. In adults, thrombocytopenia induced by COVID-19 vaccination showed an incidence of 0.80 to 11.3 per million doses [4]. However, there are currently no published reports of ITP presenting in children following mRNA vaccination. In this case, we present the case of a pediatric patient with ITP after receiving their first dose of the Moderna COVID-19 mRNA vaccine. Consent to present this case was obtained from the parents of this patient. This rare occurrence after COVID-19 vaccination suggests that further surveillance is required. Case Presentation A three-year-old boy presented to the emergency department with new-onset bruising for two days. The day before presentation, his family had noted bruising on his lower extremities and called his pediatrician, who attributed the bruising to falling off his toddler bed. On the day he presented to the emergency department, the family noted new bruising on his left shoulder and worsening of the initial bruising on his shins. The family again called the pediatrician, who referred them to the emergency department for further evaluation. In the emergency department, the family denied fevers, epistaxis, gum bleeding, hematuria, bleeding into joints, weight loss, and decreased appetite. The patient had received his first Moderna COVID-19 vaccine eight days before onset of symptoms. He had non-bloody diarrhea for two to three days after receiving his vaccine but denied any recent rhinorrhea and nasal congestion. His only medication was daily Flovent for asthma, and he reported no other medical history. He also reported being fully vaccinated, including against influenza, with none given in the past 11 months. There was no known family history of autoimmune conditions or bleeding disorders. On examination, he was afebrile, with other vital signs within normal limits for age. His physical examination was notable for ecchymosis on his left shoulder (Figure 1), and multiple petechiae, purpura, and ecchymoses were identified on his bilateral shins (Figure 2). Family consented to the photos taken for this case. At this initial presentation, there was no mucosal bleeding noted. The remainder of his physical examination was normal for age. Laboratory testing revealed normal basic metabolic panel and liver function testing. Complete blood count demonstrated severe thrombocytopenia (platelets 3,000/mm3) and a normal white blood cell count and hemoglobin (12.8 g/dL). The partial thromboplastin time was 44.2 seconds (reference range: 27-38 seconds), and prothrombin time was 11.2 seconds with an international normalized ratio of 0.9. He tested negative for COVID-19 (Table 1). The patient was discharged home with bleeding precautions, and an outpatient follow-up with Pediatric Hematology was scheduled for two days later. On the day after discharge, his family noted slight mucosal bleeding along his gum line. He was seen in Pediatric Hematology clinic with resolution of gum bleeding and no new bruising. A follow-up complete blood count on that day showed continued severe thrombocytopenia (platelets: 5,000/mm3). Immunoglobulin A was 37 mg/dL (reference range: 14-212 mg/dL), and immunoglobulin G was 421 mg/dL (reference range: 485-1,160 mg/dL). The decision was made to defer medical treatment for ITP given no new bleeding and capacity for close outpatient monitoring. Over the next 10 days, ecchymoses resolved and the child remained without new symptoms. His repeat complete blood count showed a platelet count of 28,000/mm3 (Table 2). Discussion ITP is an acquired thrombocytopenia due to antibodies against platelet antigens and is the most common acquired thrombocytopenia in children [1]. Primary ITP is defined as a platelet count <100 × 109/L not due to any specific etiology [1]. Secondary ITP is thrombocytopenia due to an underlying disorder such as a viral illness, autoimmune disorders, or immunodeficiency [1]. Certain vaccines such as MMR, Haemophilus influenzae type b, and hepatitis B have been implicated in vaccine-associated ITP, with an incidence of 1% of all ITP cases [3]. Because the incidence of acute ITP in children shows a peak between the ages of two to six years [2], it may become more common to see ITP after vaccination for COVID-19 in the younger population, who are still only recently eligible for vaccination under emergency use authorization. In a review of 20 case reports, new-onset thrombocytopenia occurred within two weeks of mRNA vaccination, with ages ranging from 22-73 years, and predominantly in females [5]. Causes of thrombocytopenia in these cases include secondary ITP due to mRNA vaccination, primary ITP occurring around the time of vaccine administration, or worsening of undiagnosed ITP [5]. Overall, it remains unclear what would trigger ITP after COVID-19 vaccination, although one theoretical mechanism involves antibodies against a novel antigen, the outer lipid layer of nanoparticles attached to platelets, as there have been antibodies detected post-COVID-19 infection that led to an ITP picture [5]. It is unclear if these antibodies act in the same way after COVID-19 vaccination. A better understanding of ITP as related to COVID-19 vaccination will likely emerge as the vaccine is more widely utilized. The case described herein is, to the authors’ knowledge, the first published report of secondary ITP following immunization with the Moderna COVID-19 vaccine. In reviewing the FDA’s full emergency use authorizations for both Pfizer and Moderna COVID-19 vaccines in prevention of COVID-19 for children six months through four years of age, no adverse bleeding events were listed in clinical trials or post-authorization experience [6,7]. However, it is important to note that early studies and early post-authorization experience may miss rare events such as myocarditis or ITP, where the number of occurrences is below the threshold of detection by these studies (events that occur in the 1/100,000 rate or higher). Because these events require larger populations exposed to the vaccine to become statistically significant, it will be important to follow case reports to help guide providers in management both pre- and post-vaccine administration. Both Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccines for individuals six months through four years of age have been available under emergency use authorization since June 2022, and adverse events have been submitted to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Vaccine Adverse Events Reporting System (VAERS) by healthcare providers and consumers. Reviewing VAERS showed 15 submissions of “petechiae” in children five years old and younger after mRNA vaccination [8]. However, several submissions suggest alternate causes, such as petechiae occurring minutes after vaccination or a vasculitis occurring around the time of vaccination. Three submissions include the diagnosis of ITP with thrombocytopenia or low platelet count occurring weeks after COVID-19 vaccination [8]. Regarding our case, secondary ITP following viral illness such as enterovirus is certainly a possibility, especially with the history of non-bloody diarrhea presenting in the days after vaccination. However, the clinical presentation is suggestive of secondary ITP after COVID-19 vaccination given the occurrence of acute isolated thrombocytopenia within two weeks of immunization, correspondence with peak age incidence for ITP, lack of clear specific viral syndrome, no further bruising or bleeding, and lack of additional symptoms. In terms of management, our patient was observed without initiation of treatment, as he had no bleeding or new bruising. In the American Society of Hematology 2011 evidence-based practice guideline for immune thrombocytopenia, children with no bleeding or mild bleeding (defined as skin manifestations only) can be managed with observation alone regardless of platelet count [9]. Conclusions As more children under five years of age are vaccinated for COVID-19, providers should be made aware of complications, including secondary ITP, given its relatively high incidence in this age group. This case may help provide awareness for physicians, with a potential need for further medical management to prevent serious bleeding events. However, this case alone does not prove causality but provides more awareness toward complications and the need for further surveillance and reporting. Additionally, the decision to offer subsequent COVID-19 vaccination after secondary ITP from initial vaccination depends on individual risk assessment and should be made in consultation with a hematologist, which could include guidance on laboratory monitoring before and after vaccination. Increased awareness by providers will also help with identification and reporting of any future events to VAERS and demonstrate a need for larger studies to determine the true incidence. In turn, this may support future investigations of potential risk factors for developing ITP after COVID-19 vaccination. title: Attitude, Educational Needs, and Challenges Faced by Physicians in Managing End-of-Life Care for Critically Ill COVID-19 Patients in Critical Care Settings During the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: INTRODUCTION: End-of-life (EOL) decision-making is particularly sensitive and complex, especially during the COVID-19 pandemic. This study aimed to assess the attitudes, educational needs, and challenges faced by doctors working in critical care settings in providing EOL care for critically ill COVID-19 patients during the pandemic. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A structured questionnaire comprising four sections was utilized to assess the attitudes of critical care unit doctors at the Hospital Universiti Sains Malaysia and Hospital Selayang, Malaysia. The questionnaire captured responses related to the attitudes, educational needs, and challenges of the physicians in the management of critically ill COVID-19 patients. RESULTS: The respondents generally agreed that EOL care is an essential clinical competency during the pandemic, with a mean score of 3.44 ± 0.87. There was strong recognition of diverse educational needs related to EOL care, encompassing both clinical and ethical aspects, with average mean scores exceeding 3 across relevant items. The physicians also identified several significant barriers to delivering effective EOL care, including the absence of standardized protocols or dedicated services (p=0.001), insufficient training (p=0.006), and time constraints (p=0.007). CONCLUSION: Overall, doctors in critical care settings demonstrated a positive attitude toward the role of EOL care for critically ill COVID-19 patients during the pandemic. A clearer understanding of their attitudes, challenges, and educational needs can help inform strategies to enhance the development and integration of EOL care in critical care settings moving forward.

title: Mechanistic reconstruction as complementary evidence for reported ancestral-lineage SARS-CoV-2 long-distance airborne outbreaks
abstract: Several short-duration indoor SARS-CoV-2 outbreaks before Alpha were interpreted as consistent with transmission beyond 2 m, but retrospective evidence cannot distinguish shared-air exposure from close contact. I developed a size-resolved framework to test how demanding pure long-distance airborne transmission is, using literature-derived source-to-deposition distributions, restricted to ancestral/pre-VOC conditions between January and September 2020. Four events were analysed: the Skagit and Wihr-au-Val choir rehearsals, the Hunan bus journey, and the Vaud courtroom hearing. Activity-matched particle and RNA emission rates for breathing, speaking, and singing were first compared against measurement to establish baseline source coverage and its dependence on the assumed source population. For each event, 100,000 realizations were evaluated across a scenario grid combining viral-load priors, RNA-to-TCID50 conversion scenarios, and deposition mechanisms, alongside a separate analysis retaining empirically paired RNA and FFU measurements. Compatibility required at least the reported number of susceptible occupants to deposit one or more infectious-unit equivalents (IUE), TCID50- or FFU-derived. No dose-response model was applied, as no validated function links deposited ancestral SARS-CoV-2 dose to infection. Compatibility under the RNA-TCID50 framework was consistently low under the RNA-positive viral-load priors, reaching at most 1.14% for Skagit, 0.61% for Wihr, 0.02% for Hunan, and 0.04% for Vaud. It was approximately an order of magnitude higher under the culture-positive prior, though the highest single scenario cell reached only 22.7% even under this upper-bound scenario. The matched RNA-FFU analysis was substantially lower, remaining below 0.01% in every cell, underscoring the model's high sensitivity to the choice of infectious-unit conversion basis. For the outbreaks that were reproduced as compatible, the pure long-distance airborne hypothesis required more than poor ventilation and elevated aerosol-generating activity: it also required an unusual draw from the upper tail of the viral-load distribution and, to a lesser extent, emitted liquid volume and infectious fraction. The proposed route is physically possible but demands an unusual conjunction of source and exposure conditions. This small compatible region supports caution in attributing these outbreaks to pure long-distance transmission, since unreported short-range exposure, additional infectious sources, and other unmeasured contributors remain plausible.

title: Single-cell B-cell receptor repertoires associated with SARS-CoV-2 immune imprinting
abstract: This project contains 10x Genomics single-cell V(D)J sequencing data from JN.1 RBD-reactive memory B cells collected from Chinese adult cohorts with distinct levels of ancestral SARS-CoV-2 immune imprinting. The dataset supports analyses of immunoglobulin gene usage, B-cell clonotypes, and antibody repertoire features associated with the severity of immune imprinting and neutralization of the BA.3.2.2 variant.

title: Retorno a la presencialidad: Percepción de riesgo del COVID-19 y salud mental en universitarios chilenos Return to in-person learning: Perception of the risk of COVID-19 and mental health among Chilean university students
abstract: Objetivo: Analizar la relación entre la percepción de riesgo de contagio del COVID-19 e indicadores de salud mental considerando variables sociodemográficas y estilo de vida asociados a la pandemia en universitarios chilenos, ante el retorno a las clases presenciales. Método: Estudio de diseño transversal, descriptivo, correlacional. Participaron 530 estudiantes de una universidad regional estatal de Chile entre los 18 y 41 años. Se utilizaron los cuestionarios de Percepción de Riesgo de Contagio COVID-19 (PCR-CV19), la Escala de Depresión, Ansiedad y Estrés (DASS-21) y una ficha sociodemográfica. Los análisis estadísticos fueron descriptivos y correlacionales, empleando pruebas de Kruskal–Wallis, tamaños de efecto d de Cohen, η2 parcial y modelos de regresión lineal múltiple jerárquica. El análisis de datos se realizó en R (4.4.1) y Jamovi (2.3.28). Resultados: Se hallaron correlaciones significativas entre las dimensiones de percepción de riesgo (vulnerabilidad cognitiva, vulnerabilidad emocional y gravedad) e indicadores de salud mental (estrés, ansiedad y depresión). Se identificó que la vulnerabilidad emocional, el de diagnóstico COVID-19 en el entorno cercano y la edad contribuyen significativamente a la varianza de la sintomatología. Conclusión: La crisis sanitaria derivada de la COVID-19 afectó la salud física y la salud mental de la población universitaria. El estudio aporta evidencia empírica que permite comprender la percepción de riesgo de contagio, no como una evaluación cognitiva, sino como una configuración emocional, donde la vulnerabilidad del individuo y sus variables sociodemográficas inciden de manera significativa en la respuesta psicológica.

title: Bhutan-focused COVID-19 publications, 2020-2024: A Scopus-based bibliometric analysis
abstract: Background: The COVID-19 pandemic stimulated unprecedented global research activity. Bhutan, despite its small population and limited research infrastructure, contributed to the COVID-19 related literature. This study aimed to analyse Bhutan-focused COVID-19 research productivity and scholarly publications using bibliometric analysis. Methods: Publications published between 2020 and 2024 were retrieved from Scopus and analysed using Microsoft Excel 2019 and VOSviewer version 1.6.20. Results: A total of 60 publications were identified. Research output increased significantly over time, from 6 publications (10%) in 2020 to 18 publications (30%) in 2021, reflecting heightened research engagement during the early phase of the pandemic. The Asia-Pacific Journal of Public Health published the highest number of publications. 18 publications (30%) remained uncited, and 9 publications (15%) received 10 or more citations. Bhutan-focused COVID-19 publications emphasised how Gross National Happiness principles and cultural values guided the country’s public health response to the pandemic. Conclusion: Bhutan-focused COVID-19 publications demonstrated a timely and collaborative research response to the pandemic. While the publication output and uptake of open-access publishing were encouraging, citation impact remained modest. Increasing research visibility, dissemination, and the inclusion in database indexes may help strengthen the impact of Bhutan-focused research in the future.

title: The Role of Chemical Metals in SARS-CoV-2 Infection
abstract: This chapter examines the complex roles of essential, trace, and potentially toxic chemical elements in SARS-CoV-2 infection and COVID-19 pathogenesis. Particular attention is given to zinc, copper, iron, selenium, magnesium, and calcium, which contribute to viral protein stability, enzymatic activity, replication, cellular entry, redox regulation, and host immune responses. The chapter also discusses how disturbances in metal homeostasis may promote oxidative stress, inflammation, immune dysfunction, and increased disease severity. Conversely, toxic elements such as cadmium, lead, mercury, and arsenic may exacerbate adverse clinical outcomes by impairing essential biological and immunological processes. By integrating current knowledge from virology, immunology, metallomics, and bioinorganic chemistry, the chapter highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic potential of monitoring and modulating metal levels in COVID-19. Remaining analytical challenges and the possible implications of persistent elemental dysregulation in long COVID are also considered.

title: Effect of Prenatal Maternal COVID-19 Vaccine on Pregnancy Outcomes
abstract: Objective: The aim of this study is to compare the pregnancy results of prenatal COVID-19 vaccinated and unvaccinated pregnant women who gave birth in our clinic and to present the statistical analyses of the obtained data.Methods: We retrospectively scanned and compared 301 vaccinated and 653 unvaccinated total 954 pregnant data who gave birth between August 2021 and January 2023 in a tertiary university hospital, gynecology and obstetrics clinic in the statistical evaluation, skewness/kurtosis tests were used to assess normality; Student's t-test was applied for parametric data, the Mann–Whitney U test for non-parametric data, and the Paired t-test for comparing 1st and 5th minute APGAR scores.Results: No significant difference was found between the vaccinated and unvaccinated groups in terms of weeks of birth and birth weights. There was no difference between the two groups in terms of blood pH values and 1st/ 5th minute APGAR scores in newborns. The rates of delivery patterns, abortions, presence of complications, and preterm birth were found to have similar frequencies in the two groups. Conclusions: Our study found that the administration of the maternal COVID-19 vaccine during pregnancy is not related to adverse prenatal outcomes. It was determined that only the placental abruption ratio was seen more frequently in the unvaccinated group.

title: Citizen Behaviour During COVID-19: Determinants of Preventive and Maladaptive Responses in Kazakhstan
abstract: This study intends to understand the predictors of preventive and maladaptive practices during the COVID-19 pandemic. The association between risk perception, behaviour, knowledge, trusted sources of information, attitudes toward the COVID-19 pandemic, response initiative, and other variables from June to September 2020, and people’s behaviour to inform COVID-19 outbreak responses was assessed. Four samples, composed of about 1,000 respondents aged 18 years and above, were interviewed online or via telephone in four rounds every two weeks from June to September 2020. Descriptive and inferential analyses of the data were conducted using Stata 18. Multivariate regression analyses, including logistic and linear regression models, were used to identify predictors of preventive and maladaptive behaviours. The study findings revealed distinct factors associated with both preventive and maladaptive measures. These findings are significant as they provide a deeper understanding of the predictors of preventive and maladaptive practices. The existence of different predictors in favour of maladaptive behaviour calls for policy intervention to increase the uptake of preventive behaviour rather than maladaptive behaviour. Therefore, consideration of all people, regardless of their place of residence, level of education, and health status, is needed through increased exposure to the right information and undertaking measures that will increase trust in the disseminated information. Policy interventions should focus on increasing exposure to accurate information to encourage preventive behaviours. Keywords: COVID-19, Kazakhstan, maladaptive behaviour, preventive behaviour, attitude.

title: A retrospective assessment of short-horizon real-time COVID-19 projections in Tokyo
abstract: We examine the features of five real-time COVID-19 infection projections in Tokyo. We find that these projections tended to (i) overpredict subsequently reported infections, (ii) be less accurate when issued during the fifth infection wave, and (iii) underpredict subsequently reported infections when issued during the rising phase but overpredict them when issued during the peak and falling phases. If policymakers and the public were to utilize real-time projections in future pandemics, it would be useful for them to be aware of the possibility that real-time projections may have systematic patterns.

title: Forecasting the Spread of COVID-19 Pandemic in Yemen using Prophet Machine Learning Model
abstract: The spread of COVID-19 has caused it to be a pandemic. This has caused massive disruption to our daily lives, both directly and indirectly. In the healthcare industry, there is much evidence that Artificial Intelligence (AI) and machine learning algorithms can provide effective models that solve problems in order to predict confirmed and death cases. Thus, early prediction of the COVID-19 spread can facilitate the planning of necessary actions from the government and people. In this paper, a forecasting the spread of COVID-19 pandemic in Yemen using prophet machine learning model is proposed. The proposed model is tested and validated to forecast confirmed and death cases at any specific period of time using COVID-19-Yemen dataset in the period of January 2020 till the end of August 2024. The proposed model is trained on 80% of the data and tested on the remaining 20%. The obtained results are evaluated using some common evaluation measures such as Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and Coefficient of determination (R2). The obtained results are promising, as the proposed model achieves high ability in forecasting confirmed and death cases using COVID-19-Yemen dataset. The performance of the proposed model is compared with other related models such as decision tree regression and polynomial regression. The comparative study confirms that the proposed model has less forecasting error with high accuracy, so it outperforms other models as it scores 1.28 in MAE, 4.41 in RMSE and 0.99 in R2 for confirmed cases. Furthermore, for death cases, the proposed model scores 0.40, 1.59, and 0.95 for MAE, RMSE and R2 respectively. The findings have yielded a realistic picture of the disease direction and provide useful insights for decision makers so as to be prepared for the future evolution of the pandemic.

title: Recovery and resilience of public transportation in Istanbul after COVID-19
abstract: The pandemic's lasting impact on public transportation raises concerns about permanent decline. There is a lack of research on the long-term effects of different modes of public transport in developing countries and adaptation to future crises. Therefore, the research questions whether and how COVID-19 has permanently changed the demand for different modes of public transportation. Secondly, whether the lessons learned from the crisis led to a policy document for resilience for future crises is questioned. The first part of the research is focused on comparative time series analysis covering the period from 2017 to 2022 to demonstrate the change in the number of passengers of each mode of public transportation in Istanbul. In the second part of the research, semi-structured interviews with decision-makers are conducted to inquire about resiliency in policy responses to future crises. The key findings indicate the fastest recovery in the urban rail system, with a 16% increase in ridership in 2022 compared to the ridership level in 2019. However, maritime public transit modes in 2022 are the most vulnerable modes, which remain approximately 17% below 2019. The results of the semi-structured interviews show that the pandemic has led to awareness about resilience in transport practice.

title: Potencial diabetogênico do SARS-CoV-2
abstract: Objetivo: Sintetizar as evidências epidemiológicas e os mecanismos fisiopatológicos associados ao desenvolvimento de diabetes mellitus (DM) após infecção por SARS-CoV-2. Métodos: Revisão integrativa orientada pela estratégia PECO. As buscas ocorreram nas bases PubMed, Scopus, SciFinder e LILACS até março de 2026, com triagem na plataforma Rayyan. Incluíram-se artigos originais (2021–2026) em português, inglês e espanhol. A seleção seguiu a estrutura do PRISMA e o nível de evidência foi categorizado por Melnyk e Fineout-Overholt. Resultados: Selecionaram-se 20 estudos, com predomínio de coortes (70%). Observou-se maior risco de DM incidente e alterações glicometabólicas persistentes em pacientes acometidos por COVID-19, sobretudo em casos graves e hospitalizados. Os mecanismos fisiopatológicos incluem disfunção e transdiferenciação das células beta via ACE2, resposta inflamatória sistêmica com estresse oxidativo, resistência à insulina (via IRF1 e bloqueio da via PI3K/Akt), mimetismo molecular e distúrbios metabólicos no tecido adiposo e hepático. Considerações finais: A associação entre COVID-19 e alterações glicêmicas pós-agudas é plausível. Contudo, a heterogeneidade metodológica e a dificuldade de diferenciar DM de início recente de hiperglicemia transitória limitam inferências causais definitivas.

Observou-se maior risco de DM incidente e alterações glicometabólicas persistentes em pacientes acometidos por COVID-19, sobretudo em casos graves e hospitalizados. Considerações finais: A associação entre COVID-19 e alterações glicêmicas pós-agudas é plausível. Contudo, a heterogeneidade metodológica e a dificuldade de diferenciar DM de início recente de hiperglicemia transitória limitam inferências causais definitivas.

title: No detectable differences in peripheral blood immune profiles between patients with prolonged severe long COVID and convalescent controls
abstract: Abstract Long COVID (LC) is characterized by persistent symptoms following acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. Common symptoms include post-exertional malaise (PEM), fatigue, cognitive impairments, and orthostatic intolerance. The underlying pathophysiological mechanism of LC remains poorly understood and studies involving patients affected for several years remain scarce. We analyzed a comprehensive panel of inflammation-associated immune markers and clinical features in LC patients with a median disease duration of three years, and compared them with convalescent controls (CC). LC was characterized using patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs), including assessments of recovery, symptoms, PEM, fatigue, cognitive failures, orthostatic intolerance, and health-related quality of life. Peripheral blood was analyzed for immune cell distributions, systemic interferon (IFN) pathway activation, monocyte transcriptional signatures, and circulating cytokine levels in serum. Immunologically, absolute numbers and frequencies of immune subsets did not differ significantly between LC and CC groups. Similarly, after correction for multiple testing, no significant differences were observed between patients with LC and CC in the expression of monocyte-associated genes, cytokine levels, or systemic IFN pathway activation. In the LC group, immunological markers were not significantly associated with illness duration or PROMs. Our findings contrast with earlier reports, predominantly conducted earlier in the disease course, describing subtle inflammatory differences in LC. In this study, we observed no detectable differences in the assessed immune markers in peripheral blood between patients with LC and controls under resting conditions. Consequently, these markers may have limited utility for diagnosis or stratification in long-term LC.
