title: Неврологічні прояви постковідного синдрому: клінічні фенотипи, прогностичні маркери та фактори ризику
abstract: Post-COVID-19 condition (Long COVID) is a heterogeneous multisystem disorder in which neurological symptoms may persist for months after acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. The diversity of clinical manifestations and absence of a validated diagnostic biomarker complicate diagnosis and prognosis. To summarize current evidence on neurological phenotypes, pathogenetic mechanisms, prognostic markers, risk factors, diagnosis, and management of post-COVID-19 condition. A narrative review of systematic reviews, meta-analyses, cohort, neuroimaging and neuroimmunological studies was performed, prioritizing publications from 2022–2025. Common manifestations include fatigue, cognitive impairment, sleep disorders, headache, dizziness, sensory disturbances, and dysautonomia. Proposed mechanisms involve neuroinflammation, microglial dysfunction, endothelial and microvascular injury, blood–brain barrier disruption, immune dysregulation, and altered neurotransmission. Potential prognostic biomarkers include markers of systemic inflammation (CRP, IL-6, NLR, SII), endothelial and coagulation dysfunction, immune activation (CCL2), and neuronal and glial injury (NfL, GFAP); however, their predictive value for Long COVID requires further prospective validation. Female sex, severe acute disease, lack of vaccination, pre-Omicron infection, and comorbidities are associated with a higher risk of Long COVID. Neurological post-COVID syndrome requires phenotype-oriented assessment, exclusion of alternative causes, and targeted additional investigations. Further studies should focus on standardized phenotyping, validation of prognostic biomarkers, and evaluation of phenotype-oriented interventions.

title: Assessment of the Association between Myocarditis (New-onset Heart Failure) and COVID-19 and COVID-19 Vaccination
abstract: Introduction: Myocarditis is a rare but significant cardiovascular complication that may occur after receiving COVID-19 vaccines, particularly in younger individuals. The majority of cases have been reported after receiving mRNA-based vaccines, while inactivated and viral vector-based vaccines have been associated with fewer occurrences. Despite this, myocarditis is much more common and results in a poorer prognosis following COVID-19 infection. However, the relationship between myocarditis post-vaccination and its potential mechanisms remains unclear due to limited information. Methods: This study investigated patients with myocarditis (new-onset heart failure) who had received the COVID-19 vaccine and those who had been infected with COVID-19 between March 2021 and March 2023 in Farshchian Cardiovascular Hospital in Hamedan. The data was analyzed using Stata version 14 software and Python. Results: Among 146 myocarditis patients, unvaccinated individuals had higher rates of hypertension, diabetes, obstructive pulmonary disease, and substance abuse, and exhibited more severe cardiac issues like mitral regurgitation and ventricular dysfunction. Vaccinated patients had better lab results and fewer severe symptoms. A model identified advanced age and cardiovascular dysfunction as key mortality risks, suggesting vaccination may mitigate severe cardiac complications and improve outcomes. Conclusion: The findings of this study show that although there is a risk of myocarditis as a side effect following the COVID-19 vaccination, its severity is far less than the occurrence following the COVID-19 infection, with fewer complications and a better prognosis. However, more studies are still necessary to complete the existing findings and clarify their unknown aspects.

title: Role of proteases and alpha-1-proteinase inhibitor in the development of respiratory failure in SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia in patients with type 2 diabetes
abstract: BACKGROUND: SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is linked to severe disease and high mortality. The role of alpha-1 protease inhibitor (α1-PI) in regulating proteolytic activity in this population during COVID-19 remains poorly understood. AIM: To evaluate the activity of alpha-1 protease inhibitor (α1-PI), elastase-like proteases (ELP), and trypsin-like proteases (TLP) in the plasma of patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) infected with SARS-CoV-2, and to develop a prognostic model for the risk of respiratory failure (RF). MATERIALS AND METHODS: A prospective observational study included 172 participants divided into four groups: SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia without T2DM (n=70), T2DM without infection (n=32), T2DM with pneumonia (n=15), and healthy controls (n=30). Plasma levels of α1-PI, elastase- and trypsin-like proteases (ELP, TLP), ACE, PAR-4, CRP, glucose, C-peptide, and TBARS were measured. Data were analyzed using non-parametric tests, Spearman’s correlation, and binary logistic regression. RESULTS: In patients without T2DM and severe pneumonia, α1-PI activity was reduced by 21% (23.7 IU/mL [15.1; 33.2] vs. 30.0 in controls; p=0.008), with moderate increases in ELP and TLP. In contrast, T2DM patients with COVID-19 showed a 41% rise in α1-PI (42.4 IU/mL [31.8; 53.4]; p=0.023) alongside marked activation of TLP (10.9-fold; p 0.05). CONCLUSION: In patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and COVID-19, a more pronounced protease activation and a dual response of α1-protease inhibitor (α1-PI) are observed, indicating an ineffective anti-inflammatory response. Decreased PAR-4 levels correlate with the severity of respiratory failure (RF). The prognostic model enables risk stratification for RF in T2DM patients.

Method:The patients admitted between November 2020-November 2021 due to quantitative and/or qualitative disorders of sense of smell and taste were included in the study.The course of sensory disorders of study patients were gathered from the medical records and evaluated retrospectively.Results: Fifteen patients were admitted for taste and/or smell disorders with or without a history of symptomatic title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of COVID-19 Cases in 75 Countries Using Google Trends: A Retrospective Study
abstract: Few studies have systematically examined the predictive capacity of digital search data for forecasting COVID-19 cases on a global scale, particularly in terms of search queries in different languages. Additionally, limited research has explored the correlations and temporal dynamics between digital search data in different languages and clinical cases. Therefore, this study employed Google Trends using COVID-19-related search terms in English and local languages to predict World Health Organization reported cases across 75 countries, spanning Africa, the Americas, Asia and Oceania, and Europe. Correlations between Google Trends and clinical case data were evaluated, and time-lagged cross-correlation analysis was employed to estimate the temporal dynamics of search data relative to cases. We also developed a machine learning-based random forest model to predict clinical cases using combined English and local language Google Trends. Our results identified leading time lags in most countries, suggesting that Google Trends can provide early warnings of reported clinical case surges. Furthermore, our random forest model successfully predicted COVID-19 cases using combined English and local language search data in a retrospective analysis, with identified relative contributions of English versus local-language searches. This study demonstrates that digital search data provide an openly accessible source of information that may assist forecasting of infectious disease outbreak surges prior to clinical data reporting. Digital epidemiology-based approaches could support public health decision-making by potentially complementing existing clinical and wastewater surveillance systems for infectious diseases. This work directly contributes to the United Nations sustainable development goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-Being) and SDG 11 (Sustainable and Resilient Cities and Communities).

title: GPs behind open doors: a case study during the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Background and Purpose Prior to the COVID-19 pandemic, general practice was in crisis with an increasingly older co-morbid population coupled with the perfect storm of dwindling workforce due to recruitment and retirement. Suddenly in March 2020, general practice faced a further crisis in the form of the COVID-19 pandemic. This brought a seismic shift overnight in how General Practitioners (GPs) provided patient care. This is a case study of how GPs in Northern Ireland adapted and changed their practice during the COVID-19 pandemic. Methodology GPs were recruited to the study via a restricted Facebook page ‘GP Survival Northern Ireland’ and through snowballing. Eight participants were recruited and interviews occurred remotely via Microsoft Teams or telephone call utilising a semi structured interview template derived from a scoping review of the literature. The data was transcribed and analysed by the research team, using a Case Study approach as described by Crowe et al. Key findings were extracted from the data. Results Participants ranged widely in age and geographical location of practices, with list sizes up to 10000 patients. There were three key findings identified from the Case Study: 1. Layers of communication: GPs described communication on multiple levels, using new and not so new ways to update and disseminate information to their staff, colleagues and their patients. Rapid change, practice continues: Despite the rapid change occurring, the normal day to day work of general practice had to carry on; patients’ needs continued to have to be met. 3) Resetting and redefining the work of general practice: general practice has grappled with its own identity using this opportunity to reset and continue to redefine its identity. Discussion and Conclusions General practice has changed during the COVID-19 pandemic. There have been several ways in which GPs have had to consider the best way to communicate incorporating new and not so new modes however patient access remains an important element to the tenet of GPs. The element of stress and risk has been brought into sharp focus with GPs having to be cognisant of the increased risk during the COVID-19 pandemic. General practice was evolving pre COVID-19 and continues to evolve. It is unclear as to its exact shape in the future.

Methodology GPs were recruited to the study via a restricted Facebook page ‘GP Survival Northern Ireland’ and through snowballing. Eight participants were recruited and interviews occurred remotely via Microsoft Teams or telephone call utilising a semi structured interview template derived from a scoping review of the literature. The data was transcribed and analysed by the research team, using a Case Study approach as described by Crowe et al. Key findings were extracted from the data. Results Participants ranged widely in age and geographical location of practices, with list sizes up to 10000 patients. There were three key findings identified from the Case Study: 1. Layers of communication: GPs described communication on multiple levels, using new and not so new ways to update and disseminate information to their staff, colleagues and their patients. Rapid change, practice continues: Despite the rapid change occurring, the normal day to day work of general practice had to carry on; patients’ needs continued to have to be met. 3) Resetting and redefining the work of general practice: general practice has grappled with its own identity using this opportunity to reset and continue to redefine its identity. Discussion and Conclusions General practice has changed during the COVID-19 pandemic. There have been several ways in which GPs have had to consider the best way to communicate incorporating new and not so new modes however patient access remains an important element to the tenet of GPs. The element of stress and risk has been brought into sharp focus with GPs having to be cognisant of the increased risk during the COVID-19 pandemic. General practice was evolving pre COVID-19 and continues to evolve. It is unclear as to its exact shape in the future.

title: Bioinformatic evidence of spike-olfactory receptor mimicry: a potential mechanism for anosmia after SARS-CoV-2 infection and vaccination
abstract: Anosmia is one of the most common neurological symptoms to occur following infection with SARS-CoV-2, whilst olfactory disorders are rare following vaccination. The immune-mediated response against the olfactory structures could have broad implications for the proper functioning of the central nervous system, as the sense of smell is not only important for the perception of odors but is also closely interconnected with the gustatory, limbic and cognitive circuits. Molecular mimicry between viral and host proteins is one of the plausible mechanisms underlying these effects. In light of this, we carried out a systematic bioinformatic analysis to identify potential linear peptide matches between the human olfactory receptor proteome and SARS-CoV-2 proteins, focusing on the spike glycoprotein. We found multiple peptide matches between olfactory receptors and SARS-CoV-2 proteins, but only OR5H14 shared an identical hexapeptide (ISVTTE) with the spike glycoprotein, suggesting a possible mechanism underlying the rare spike-mediated post-vaccination olfactory dysfunction. This also explains why, by contrast, greater viral exposure during infection leads to a higher prevalence of anosmia. Furthermore, the shared amino acid sequence segment demonstrated antigenic-immunogenic potential. These findings support a potential role for molecular mimicry between the spike protein and OR5H14 in post-vaccination anosmia, with implications for the sensory and cognitive pathways of the central nervous system, laying the foundations for future immunological studies.

title: Evaluation of the Effect of Vaccination Status on Lung Involvement and Hospitalization in COVID-19 Patients
abstract: Background: The spectrum of COVID-19 in adults ranges from asymptomatic infection to mild respiratory tract symptoms to severe pneumonia with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and multiorgan dysfunction. In our study, it was aimed to investigate the effects of COVID- 19 vaccine on lung involvement and hospitalization. Materials and Methods: Cases over the age of 18, who had a history of contact with cases infected with COVID-19 or had clinical findings suggestive of COVID-19, who applied to the emergency department and who were diagnosed with COVID-19 by reverse-transcriptase-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) were included in the study. Age, gender, comorbid diseases, hospitalization status, thorax tomography findings, and vaccination status in the last 3 months of the patients included in the study were obtained by examining the hospital information system and patient files. Results: Our study included 496 patients. One hundred eighty-three of the cases were vaccinated and 42.6% (n = 78) of the vaccinated patients were male. Of the 313 unvaccinated patients, 36% (n = 113) were male. Comorbid disease was observed in 55.2% (n = 101) of the vaccinated patients and 38.7% (n = 121) of the unvaccinated patients. Of the 313 unvaccinated patients, 72.2% (n = 226) were discharged from the emergency department, 19.8% (n = 62) were admitted to the service, and 8% (n = 25) were admitted to the intensive care unit. Of the 183 vaccinated patients, 78.1% (n = 143) were discharged from the emergency department, 16.4% (n = 30) were admitted to the service, and 5.5% (n = 10) were admitted to the intensive care unit. In the vaccinated patient group, both the service admission rate and the intensive care hospitalization rate were found to be significantly lower than the non-vaccinated patient group (p Conclusion: In our study, it was found that vaccination significantly reduced hospitalization in COVID-19 patients. Although the mean age was higher in the vaccinated patient group, both the service admission rate and the intensive care admission rate were found to be lower.

title: Uluslararası Sağlık Turizmi: Kayıt Dışı Riskler, COVID-19 Sonrası Dalgalanmalar ve İtibar Yönetimi (2017–2025) – Sistematik Derleme (International Health Tourism: Unregistered Risks, Post-COVID-19 Fluctuations, and Reputation Management (2017–2025) – Systematic Review)
abstract: This review synthesises the international health tourism literature published between 2017 and 2025 along three thematic axes — the sectoral impacts of COVID-19, the informality–accreditation–intermediary ecosystem, and reputation management–electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM)–destination image — maps the intersections between them and establishes empirically the absence of integrated designs. Searches in Web of Science, Scopus and PubMed up to 15 September 2025 returned 724 records; following PRISMA 2020, 214 studies were included. The evidence base is dominated by survey-based quantitative studies, qualitative inquiries and text-mining/eWOM analyses. Reputation and eWOM predominate (132 studies); work on COVID-19 effects has grown rapidly (70 studies), while research on accreditation and intermediary dynamics remains limited (47 studies). No single study addresses all three themes together. Crisis and risk communication and hygiene protocols emerged as decisive for destination image and travel intention. The review recommends strengthening accreditation transparency, regulating intermediaries, reporting complication data and proactive multilingual risk communication, and points to the need for multi-source, causal designs.

title: Comparative Evaluation of the Inactivation of SARS-CoV-2 and Human Coronavirus 229E against Sodium Hypochlorite
abstract: Introduction: Surface disinfection is one of the important non-pharmaceutical intervention measures that help prevent the spread of Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). Disinfectants with an efficacy claim against Human Coronavirus strain 229E (HCoV-229E) have been used for the disinfection of SARS-CoV-2; however, the comparative susceptibility of these two viruses to chemical disinfection has not been well defined. To address this, laboratory data were generated to compare the level of inactivation of human coronaviruses HCoV-229E and SARS-CoV-2 to a common antimicrobial agent, sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl), on a hard non-porous surface. Methods: A hard surface-based Quantitative Method (QM) was used to evaluate the viral inactivation efficacy by three treatments of NaOCl against HCoV-229E and SARS-CoV-2. For each treatment, viral inoculum containing soil load was applied onto a stainless steel carrier and dried. The inoculated carrier was exposed to NaOCl or a control fluid and held for five minutes. Following the exposure time, a neutralizer was added, and the sample was serially diluted and inoculated onto host cells to determine the number of infective units. The resulting Log10 of the density for control and treated carriers was used to generate Log10 reduction (LR) values for comparative statistical evaluation. Results: The mean LR ± standard error (SE) for HCoV-229E was 0.96 ± 0.09 (n=10) at 500 ppm NaOCl, 2.41 ± 0.15 (n=10) at 1,000 ppm NaOCl, and 4.54 ± 0.13 (n=10) at 1,500 ppm NaOCl. The mean LR ± SE for SARS-CoV-2 was 0.91 ± 0.24 (n=4) at 500 ppm NaOCl, 1.96 ± 0.26 (n=4) at 1,000 ppm NaOCl, and 4.23 ± 0.16 (n=4) at 1,500 ppm NaOCl. Both viruses were significantly responsive to the increasing concentrations of NaOCl. HCoV-229E had slightly higher mean LRs compared to SARS-CoV-2 at each NaOCl concentration; however, these differences were not statistically significant (p ≥ 0.067). Regression analysis using a linear mixed effects model (LMM) also indicates that the susceptibility of HCoV-229E and SARS-CoV-2 to NaOCl is comparable. Discussion: Understanding the antimicrobial tolerance of viruses can enhance public health response to viral infections. By determining the tolerance, the most appropriate antimicrobial agent can be chosen to disinfect surfaces contaminated with viral particles. Disinfection of highcontact surfaces can reduce the amount of fomite transmission and limit outbreaks. Conclusion: The data suggest that HCoV-229E and SARS-CoV-2 are statistically comparable in their susceptibility to NaOCl treatments.

title: Potential Predictive Value of Netrin-1 and Hematological Biomarkers in COVID-19-Associated Immune Dysregulation
abstract: This study intended to evaluate levels of Netrin-1, glycated hemoglobin, and some hematological parameters in COVID-19 patients by comparing them with the control or healthy group to investigate the potential effects of infection. The biochemical tests studied included of Netrin-1 protein level, random blood sugar (RBS), HbA1c, C-reactive protein levels, and concentrations of some hematological parameters (RBC, WBC, Platelets, and Hemoglobin). The study was applied on 40 patients (20 males and 20 females) with COVID-19 at Samarra Hospital and some outpatient clinics in Samarra city, in addition to 30 healthy individuals (15 males and 15 females) as a control group, for the period from the beginning of October 2022 to the end of January 2023. They were in four groups of males and females aged between 20 and 50 years. The results showed significant sex-dependent changes in Netrin-1 levels. Netrin-1 concentrations were considerably lower in COVID-19 male patients compared to healthy men, whereas female patients had significantly higher levels compared to female controls (P < 0.001). CRP and RBS levels were significantly elevated in both male and female patients (P <0.001). Male patients had significantly higher HbA1c levels (P = 0.003) whereas females had a non-significant rise (P = 0.072). Hematological investigations indicated significant leukocytosis, lymphopenia and thrombocytopenia in both sexes. In female patients, there was also a substantial decrease in hemoglobin levels while in male patients there was a large increase in RBC count and PCV levels. Correlation study showed substantial inverse connection between Netrin-1 and both CRP and HbA1c levels confirming the link between changed Netrin-1 expression and inflammatory dysregulation in COVID-19 patients . ROC curve research revealed promising predictive and diagnostic values of CRP, lymphocyte percentage, Netrin-1 and platelet count for immunological changes related with COVID-19. In conclusion, COVID-19 infection is associated with severe inflammatory and hematological abnormalities that are linked to sex-dependent changes in Netrin-1 levels. These data imply that Netrin-1 may be a promising prognostic biomarker related to immunological dysregulation in COVID-19 patients.

title: Immune transcriptomic differences in paediatric patients with SARS-CoV-2 compared to other lower respiratory tract infections
abstract: Abstract Background The clinical severity of SARS-CoV-2 infection in children varies, with asymptomatic or mild illness predominating and a minority developing severe disease. However, studies of the transcriptional responses to SARS-CoV-2 infection in children are limited. Understanding the immunological responses that underlie severity of disease may guide future development of preventive or therapeutic interventions. Methods Whole blood transcriptomes of healthy children ( N = 127) were compared to children with mild/asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection ( N = 71) and to children hospitalised with severe SARS-CoV-2 ( N = 41), lower respiratory tract illness (LRTI), LRTI due to Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV-LRTI) ( N = 47), or Pulmonary Tuberculosis (PTB) ( N = 47). Results We identified > 5000 differentially expressed genes including: OLFM4 , IFI27 , CBX7 , IGF2BP3 , OTOF for severe SARS-CoV-2; IFI27 , OTOF , SIGLEC1 , IFI44L and USP18 for RSV-LRTI, and MMP8 , LTF , IGF2BP3 , GPR84 , CD177 , C1QC and DEFA4 for PTB, at false discovery rate (FDR) < 0.05. Pathway analysis identified enrichment for neutrophil degranulation, interferon gamma signalling, overexpression of ribosomal proteins and depletion of immune response in severe SARS-CoV-2 compared to healthy (SAR-CoV-2 uninfected) children. Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis ( WGCNA ) identified 10 correlated gene modules shared between LRTIs showing similar underlying response mechanisms. Cellular decomposition analysis identified the depletion of 22 cell types in severe SARS-CoV-2, 16 for RSV-LRTI and 21 for PTB compared to healthy children. Conclusion Severe COVID-19 in children exhibits a similar cellular response as previously reported in adults. We identified genes important for discriminating asymptomatic/mild from severe SARS-CoV-2, healthy children from severe SARS-CoV-2, RSV-LRTI and PTB, highlighting future therapeutic targets.

title: Cross talk between SARS-CoV-2 and the angiotensin system: clinical implications
abstract: This study characterizes the interaction between the angiotensin system and angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2)/spike proteins and its significance for coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) severity. Using a cell-to-cell fusion assay and angiotensin 1 receptor (AT1R) activation assessment via the AT1R-Tango approach, we reveal a crucial role of ACE2 in attenuating AT1R activation. Furthermore, the data indicate that the spike protein indirectly amplifies AT1R activation. In addition, angiotensin 1–7 (Ang 1–7) was identified to act not only as Mas receptor (MasR) agonist, but also as a biased agonist for AT1R.

title: In silico Identification of Antiviral Polyphenols from Phoenix dactylifera Targeting SARS-CoV-2 Main Protease
abstract: COVID-19, caused by SARS-CoV-2, depends on its main protease (Mpro) for viral replication. This study evaluated the potential of polyphenolic compounds from Phoenix dactylifera as Mpro inhibitors using molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and ADMET profiling. Three ligands - flavoxanthin, violaxanthin, and neoxanthin, demonstrated the strongest binding affinities to Mpro, although still lower than tipranavir. MD simulations indicated that all three ligands maintained stable interactions with Mpro, while PCA revealed no major structural deviations in the complex. ADMET screening identified 18 compounds with acceptable pharmacokinetic properties. Overall, the top three ligands exhibited favorable binding energies and stability, supporting their potential as Mpro inhibitors. Further in vitro and in vivo validation is needed to support this hypothesis.

source_records.title: In silico Identification of Antiviral Polyphenols from Phoenix dactylifera Targeting SARS-CoV-2 Main Protease
source_records.abstract: COVID-19, caused by SARS-CoV-2, depends on its main protease (Mpro) for viral replication. This study evaluated the potential of polyphenolic compounds from Phoenix dactylifera as Mpro inhibitors using molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and ADMET profiling. Three ligands - flavoxanthin, violaxanthin, and neoxanthin, demonstrated the strongest binding affinities to Mpro, although still lower than tipranavir. MD simulations indicated that all three ligands maintained stable interactions with Mpro, while PCA revealed no major structural deviations in the complex. ADMET screening identified 18 compounds with acceptable pharmacokinetic properties. Overall, the top three ligands exhibited favorable binding energies and stability, supporting their potential as Mpro inhibitors. Further in vitro and in vivo validation is needed to support this hypothesis.

title: Cold agglutinin syndrome as a complication of Covid-19 in two cases.
abstract: Cold agglutinins are autoantibodies against RBC antigens, leading to hemolysis at less-than-physiological temperatures through complement fixation. Production can be triggered by infections, resulting in secondary cold agglutinin syndrome (CAS). This syndrome has been classically described in the setting of Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection, as well as with several viral pathogens.Here, we present two cases of cold agglutinins identified in the context of Covid-19 in critically ill patients treated at our institution. Each case was characterized by little in-vivo hemolysis, but these antibodies complicated laboratory assessment and renal replacement therapy. Management included anticoagulation and warming of dialysis circuit.Despite minimal in-vivo hemolysis, these antibodies are of clinical significance given their implications for laboratory assessment and renal replacement therapy, particularly with the frequency of multi-organ system dysfunction associated with severe Covid-19.

title: Knowledge, Attitude and Perception of Covid-19 Vaccine Among Older Adults in Ikwerre LGA, in Rivers State
abstract: Background: Older adults remain at increased risk of severe illness, hospitalization, and mortality from COVID-19, yet vaccine hesitancy persists in many low- and middle-income countries like Nigeria. Lack of knowledge, attitude, and perception toward the COVID-19 vaccine contribute significantly to vaccine refusal in older populations. This study assessed the knowledge, attitude, and perception (KAP) of older adults toward the COVID-19 vaccine in Ikwerre Local Government Area (LGA), Rivers State, Nigeria. Methodology: A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 423 older adults aged 60 years and above residing in Ikwerre LGA from August 8th to September 24th 2024, using a well-structured questionnaire and analysed using Stata version 16. Descriptive statistics was used to summarize socio-demographic characteristics and analysis of variance (ANOVA) test The ANOVA test was used to test for the association between KAP and socio demographic factors and statistical significance was set at p-value ≤0.05. Results: The mean age of the respondents was 68.5 ± 5.4. The study found that half of the respondents (50.6%) had low knowledge of the COVID-19 vaccine, while (30.3%) demonstrated high knowledge. About two-thirds (70.7%) of the respondents had good attitude, while more than half (66.7%) had positive perceptions of the vaccine. The primary source of vaccine information was children (57%) followed by relatives (44.9%) and friends (40.0%).. Knowledge was significantly associated with education, occupation, and income (p<0.001), while marital status, living arrangement, income, and healthcare access were significantly associated with attitude and perception. Conclusion: The study revealed that most respondents expressed positive attitudes and perceptions toward COVID-19 vaccination, knowledge levels were generally low influenced by socio-demographic factors. Targeted health education and improved access to reliable vaccine information are essential to strengthen vaccine literacy and sustain positive attitudes, ultimately enhancing vaccine uptake among older adults in Nigeria.
journal: International Journal of Health and Pharmaceutical Research

title: Intensive care unit and hospital mortality for patients with COVID-19 compared with patients with community-acquired pneumonia during the COVID-19 pandemic in Alberta hospitals: Retrospective observational cohort study
abstract: RATIONALE Mortality among hospitalized patients with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) ranges from 10% to 12%, increasing to approximately 30% in those requiring mechanical ventilation (IMV). During COVID-19, it remained unclear whether critically ill COVID-19 patients experienced different outcomes compared with CAP patients. This study compared ICU and hospital mortality between these groups.OBJECTIVES The objective of this study was to compare demographics, clinical characteristics, and outcomes of adults with COVID-19 admitted to intensive care units (ICUs) in Alberta during the pandemic versus CAP patients.METHODS This retrospective population-based cohort study included adults admitted to 19 medical–surgical ICUs in Alberta, Canada, from March 2020 to March 2023. Data were obtained from Alberta Health Services databases. Multinomial regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (ORs) for co-primary outcomes (ICU and hospital mortality) and secondary outcomes (ICU and hospital readmission).RESULTS A total of 5138 COVID-19 and 5154 CAP ICU admissions were analyzed. CAP admissions were steady, while COVID-19 admissions occurred in four waves. COVID-19 patients had higher ICU mortality (OR 1.20, 95% CI 1.09–1.32; p < 0.001) and ICU readmission (OR 1.32, 95% CI 1.00–1.75; p = 0.048). ICU length of stay and hospital mortality were similar. COVID-19 patients had lower IMV use, shorter hospital length of stay, and lower hospital readmission. Hospital mortality declined more over time among COVID-19 patients (interaction OR 0.984; p < 0.001).CONCLUSIONS COVID-19 was associated with higher ICU mortality, whereas CAP was associated with longer hospitalization. The ICU mortality among mechanically ventilated patients with COVID-19 declined following the RECOVERY trial. However, other evolving therapies, virological, and immunological factors likely contributed to the progressive improvement in survival.
journal: Canadian Journal of Respiratory Critical Care and Sleep Medicine

title: Health Point Prevalence of TB Among Sars Cov-2 Positive Patients in Delta State
abstract: COVID-19 and tuberculosis (TB) overlap in clinical presentation, complicating diagnosis in TB endemic regions. Data on TB prevalence among SARS-CoV-2–seropositive patients in Delta state, Nigeria are scarce. The aim of this research is to determine TB prevalence among SARS-CoV-2 antibody–positive patients in Delta State, Nigeria. A cross-sectional study enrolled 154 patients with respiratory symptoms from three hospitals. Venous blood was collected for SARS-CoV-2 antibody testing, and sputum samples were analyzed for TB using GeneXpert MTB/RIF. Descriptive statistics summarized participant characteristics, and Chi-square tests assessed associations between TB/SARS-CoV-2 co-infection and age, gender, and study site. SARS-CoV-2 antibodies were detected in 98 participants (63.6%). Among these, 31 (31.6%) had TB co infection. Co-infection was highest in Warri (38.7%), followed by Asaba (33.3%) and Ughelli (25.0%). Adults aged 31–45 years had the highest co-infection rate (15.3%). Females had slightly higher prevalence than males (51.6% vs. No statistically significant associations were observed between co-infection and site, age, or gender (p > 0.05). in conclusion, SARS-CoV-2 exposure is widespread in Delta State, with a substantial proportion of seropositive individuals co-infected with TB. Adults aged 31–45 years and females appear most affected. These findings highlight the urgent need for integrated TB and COVID-19 screening programs in high-burden settings to enable timely diagnosis and improve patient outcomes.

title: Advancing Health Equity In Long Covid: Bioethical Considerations And System-Level Strategies For Post-Acute Care And Recovery
abstract: Abstract: Long COVID has emerged as a continuing public health challenge, with symptoms such as fatigue, cognitive slowing and shortness of breath affecting many people well after the initial SARS-CoV-2 infection. This review synthesizes evidence on prevalence, symptom, risk determinants, health utilization, and the wider social and economic effects of Long COVID, emphasizing prevention and health system preparedness. The analysis highlights differences across regions and population groups, rising pressure on rehabilitation services and notable consequences for employment, education and mental health. The study looks at fairness in resource distribution within overburdened health systems, equity in care access, and the protection of vulnerable groups in research and policy responses from an ethical standpoint. We underline the importance of harmonized diagnostic criteria, inclusive and representative research, and equitable access to chronic care services. We also set out priority policy actions to support earlier identification, team-based models of care and coordinated national strategies. By integrating clinical, economic and social perspectives, this review outlines a policy priorities to support early identification, multidisciplinary care, and coordinated national strategies. We also examine bioethical considerations including equity in care access, resource allocation in strained health systems, and protection of vulnerable populations in research and policy responses.

title: Transitions to Post-Compulsory Education of Foreign and Immigrant Students in Switzerland in Time of the COVID-19 Crisis Übergänge von ausländischen und zugewanderten Schülerinnen und Schülern in die nachobligatorische Bildung in der Schweiz während der COVID-19-Krise Transitions vers la formation post-obligatoire des élèves étrangers et issus de l’immigration en Suisse en période de crise du COVID-19
abstract: This paper examines whether the COVID-19 crisis reshaped the transition to upper secondary education in Switzerland and reinforced migration-related inequalities. Using exhaustive LABB administrative data, we compare three cohorts completing compulsory school before and during the pandemic with sequence analysis and detailed migration indicators. Results show more linear trajectories, higher entry into general education, and stable VET access. Inequalities by nationality and residence permit remain strong, with no clear pandemic exacerbation.

title: Fear of Anti-Asian Hate Crime and Discrimination During the COVID-19 Pandemic: Evidence from Korean Community Members in the United States
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic created a racialized social crisis in which Asians and Asian Americans in the United States faced heightened discrimination and concern about hate crime victimization. Using online survey data collected from Korean community members in the United States during summer 2021, this study examines direct and indirect anti-Asian hate crime/discrimination victimization before and after COVID-19 and identifies factors associated with fear of anti-Asian hate crime/discrimination. Contrary to broader national evidence documenting increased anti-Asian hate during the pandemic, the findings indicate that both direct and indirect victimization experiences decreased after COVID-19 within this sample. Multiple regression results further show that income was negatively associated with fear of anti-Asian hate crime/discrimination, while media exposure was positively associated with fear. The findings suggest that the relatively high-income composition of the sample may have reduced exposure to public victimization opportunities during the pandemic, potentially through greater access to remote work and other protective resources. source_records.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic created a racialized social crisis in which Asians and Asian Americans in the United States faced heightened discrimination and concern about hate crime victimization. Using online survey data collected from Korean community members in the United States during summer 2021, this study examines direct and indirect anti-Asian hate crime/discrimination victimization before and after COVID-19 and identifies factors associated with fear of anti-Asian hate crime/discrimination. title: Distribution, carbapenem resistance and DTR dynamics of ESKAPEEc pathogens from pediatric bloodstream infections in Sichuan Province, 2017-2025: epidemiological characteristics under COVID-19 pandemic and emerging linezolid MIC creep
abstract: To characterize the distribution and antimicrobial resistance evolution of ESKAPEEc pathogens causing pediatric bloodstream infections in Sichuan Province across the COVID-19 era, and to systematically evaluate the epidemiology of carbapenem resistance (CR), difficult-to-treat resistance (DTR), and MIC drift in vancomycin and linezolid, thereby addressing a long-standing gap in longitudinal pediatric multidrug-resistant surveillance in Southwest China. A multicenter retrospective study was conducted using pediatric blood culture data from 134 healthcare institutions in Sichuan Province between 2017 and 2025. A total of 20,018 isolates were included and stratified into pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic periods. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing and DTR classification were interpreted according to CLSI M100 (35th edition) criteria. Statistical analyses were performed using WHONET 5.6 and SPSS 26.0. A total of 5,236 ESKAPEEc isolates were identified, accounting for 26.2% of all bloodstream isolates. Detection rates increased during the pandemic period and declined thereafter. Carbapenem resistance rates in Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae were significantly higher in the post-pandemic period compared with the pre-pandemic baseline. The overall DTR prevalence was 8.6%, with Acinetobacter baumannii exhibiting the highest DTR burden (87.3%) despite a declining temporal trend, whereas DTR in K. pneumoniae increased progressively over time. Reliance on CR criteria alone failed to identify a substantial proportion of DTR-positive E. All Staphylococcus aureus isolates remained susceptible to vancomycin and linezolid in vitro , with stable vancomycin MIC distributions; however, a high-MIC subpopulation among linezolid-treated MRSA isolates increased significantly over time (r=0.767, P = 0.016). Distinct age-stratified differences were observed in both pathogen distribution and resistance profiles. The COVID-19 pandemic exerted a bidirectional and sustained impact on the pediatric ESKAPEEc landscape and resistance ecology in Sichuan Province. Post-pandemic escalation of carbapenem resistance persists. The persistently high DTR burden in A. baumannii and early MIC drift toward linezolid in MRSA represent two critical regional threats in pediatric infectious disease management. Regional surveillance systems should incorporate DTR metrics alongside CR monitoring and implement age-stratified, precision-based antimicrobial stewardship strategies.
journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

title: Impact of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 infection timing on pregnancy outcomes in Jeju, Republic of Korea
abstract: In this study, we investigated whether the gestational timing of maternal severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection was associated with pregnancy and neonatal outcomes. Pregnant women with SARS-CoV-2 infection who subsequently delivered between August 2021 and April 2022 were included. According to the gestational timing of the infection, the participants were categorized into second- and third-trimester infection groups. Maternal characteristics and obstetric and neonatal outcomes were compared between the two groups. A total of 59 women were included in the analysis (12 and 47 in the second and third trimester, respectively). Women in the second-trimester infection group delivered at an earlier gestational age than those in the third-trimester infection group (37.0±3.6 vs. 38.6±1.4 weeks, P=0.020). Birth weight was significantly lower in the second-trimester infection group (2,763±855 vs. 3,201±393 g, P=0.011). Moreover, Apgar scores at 1 and 5 minutes were lower in the second-trimester group (P=0.005 for both). Although neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission rates were similar in the groups, neonates born to mothers in the second-trimester infection group had a significantly longer NICU length of stay (12.5±19.8 vs. 1.6±3.5 days, P=0.001). Therefore, maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection during the second trimester was associated with earlier delivery and longer NICU stay than that during the third trimester. Thus, the timing of maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy is possibly associated with obstetric and neonatal outcomes.

title: COVID-19 modeling and optimal control strategies with vaccination, healthcare management and social intervention
abstract: In this paper, a compartmental COVID-19 model based on the disease symptoms and health conditions of the individuals is proposed and analyzed, taking into account social interventions (such as mask awareness, hand sanitizer use, social distance in extended family or restriction on relatives' visits and media awareness promotion), lockdown policy and vaccination. In addition, an optimal rational intervention strategy is determined in order to control the disease, that is, to minimize the asymptomatic, severe symptomatic and hospitalized cases. The validation of the model is examined by analyzing the behavior of the solutions and fitting the model to the daily new infected cases reported in India from 24 March 2020 to 09 September 2021. The stability criteria is established in terms of the epidemic threshold parameter. Several numerical simulations are performed to investigate the impact of the social intervention factors and vaccination process. The influence of an effective lockdown policy on the epidemic scenario is illustrated. Furthermore, the effects of the disease transmission rates and social intervention measure on the basic reproduction number are numerically demonstrated.

title: Imaginaries of nature in Argentina during and after the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: ResumenLa pandemia de COVID-19 desató discusiones sobre los efectos negativos del dominio antrópico en el entorno.En este artículo se analizan los imaginarios y las representaciones de la sociedad argentina en su vínculo con la naturaleza durante y después de la pandemia, a partir de marcos teóricos sociológicos vinculados con la percepción del tiempo.La hipótesis plantea que las experiencias singulares derivadas de la enfermedad alteraron significaciones y percepciones acerca del entorno y generaron distintas subjetividades, algunas de ellas contrapuestas y condicionadas por la situación de aislamiento social.Para la interpretación de imaginarios y representaciones de la naturaleza, utilizamos dos investigaciones de metodología mixta ya finalizadas que estudiaron la inserción colectiva y la manifestación de creencias, miedos, percepciones y esperanzas en Argentina durante 2020 y 2021.Entre los resultados, se destaca que, en la etapa de mayor cantidad de contagios y muertes, parte de la ciudadanía asoció la pandemia con una especie de venganza de la naturaleza hacia el ser humano.Este hecho generó el deseo de un acercamiento futuro.Luego, al finalizar el aislamiento social, disminuir los contagios y las muertes, y al retornar las prácticas sociales a una nueva "normalidad", la percepción de una mayor sincronía socioambiental se desdibujó y emergieron nuevas representaciones que, nuevamente, tensionaron la relación.

title: Sounding Covid-19: understanding the pandemic through sonic experiences
abstract: The portfolio and research use a multi-method qualitative approach to study a range of Covid-19 sonic experiences through auto-hermeneutics and ethnographic strategies. During the Covid-19 lockdowns in Belfast, Northern Ireland, which started on March 23, 2020. The research began four days later to capture an immediate response to the changes in the urban sonic environment and preserve the experiences encountered with the pandemic. Part of this research extended to a visit to Montreal, Canada, and the continuation of the pandemic in Belfast from 2020-2022. Throughout these times, the material aided in producing and forming the Sounding Covid-19 Repository, which hosts all soundscape compositions. The repository focuses on Belfast’s Lockdowns (1-3 in 2020-2021), Exit Strategies (Summers 2020 and 2021), Lifted Restrictions (2022), and Montreal’s lockdown visit in 2020-2021. In total, there have been 91 soundscape compositions produced across 27 locations. As time passed, several Calls for Work inspired the idea of sharing and distributing the material for others to learn about the restrictions faced. Contributing to online platforms such as soundmaps and other experiences enabled information sharing on a global scale of the current crisis I was experiencing. There is also a focus on the on-site experiences by designing soundwalking activities with mobile apps that allow participants to reflect on past sounds from the repository material in a modern context. In addition, there is a re-exploration of the Sounding Covid-19 Repository focused on creating pandemic-related compositions and collaborative projects, expanding the purposes of only creating a repository and showing how repositories foster other creative initiatives. The projects and creative pieces bring attention to the regulations issued, the isolated moments within the city, and reflections of changes in everyday life impacting areas such as history, socio-cultural lifestyle, politics, and representation of a crisis through sound. There are various methods to understand how audio materials serve as a form of documentation for an event, how they aid in the growth of personal and collective knowledge, and how integrating research strategies can enhance inquiry in times of crisis for both research and portfolio purposes.

title: Depressive symptoms among Swedish older adults during the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Background To determine the prevalence of depressive symptoms and its association with social interaction among Swedish older adults during COVID-19 pandemic. Methods This population-based cross-sectional study included 3,490 participants aged 60 years and older in Stockholm, Sweden. Data was collected in 2021. Depressive symptoms and social interaction were collected through questionnaires. Logistic regression was performed to estimate odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI). Results The prevalence of moderate to severe depressive symptoms was 4.6%. Compared to high availability of social interactions, the odds of moderate to severe depressive symptoms were higher among those with less availability of social integration (OR=2.37, CI=1.92-3.89) and availability of social attachment (OR= 3.20, CI= 2.28-4.45). Conclusions The depressive symptoms were not highly prevalent among Swedish older adults during COVID-19 pandemic. Less availability of social interaction was associated with higher odds of moderate to severe depressive symptoms.

title: Impact of Public Health Interventions on the Co-infection Dynamics of COVID-19 with Tuberculosis
abstract: COVID-19 and tuberculosis (TB) co-infection presents a significant public health challenge by increasing disease burden and complicating disease management, diagnosis, and treatment. To explore the COVID-19-TB co-infection dynamics and evaluate interventions such as public health campaigns, mask wearing, and social distancing, we formulate and analyse a novel ten-compartmental deterministic SEIRS model. The model is unique in the sense that it simultaneously includes separate exposed, infectious, and recovered classes for TB, COVID-19 and co-infected individuals, thus providing a detailed description of the disease progression, immunity loss, and co-infection routes. The analysis proceeds by first examining the reduced sub-models corresponding to COVID-19-only and TB-only dynamics, followed by the complete co-infection model. For each case, both local and global stability properties are rigorously investigated using analytical techniques complemented by numerical verification. Model calibration is performed against cumulative weekly COVID-19 case data from Brazil and South Africa to estimate the best-fit model parameters. Numerical simulations reveal that reduction in contact rates substantially decreases the prevalence of both single infections and co-infections. Furthermore, public health campaigns are particularly effective in reducing TB transmission and levels of co-infection, whereas mask wearing and social distancing suppress COVID-19 spread and its associated co-infections. Our results suggest that implementing disease-specific interventions can help reduce the disease burden and offer evidence-based information for the development of effective public health policies in areas where both diseases are endemic.

title: Serine ubiquitination of the SARS-CoV-2 RdRp by the non-canonical E3 ligase MYCBP2
abstract: ABSTRACT Post-translational modifications, including ubiquitination, have emerged as important regulators of viral infection and the host innate immune response. We screened the proteins of SARS-CoV-2 for ubiquitination and identified the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) NSP12 as being ubiquitinated, which has not previously been reported. Importantly, we confirmed that NSP12 is ubiquitinated during SARS-CoV-2 infection, and the NSP12 proteins of different coronaviruses are differentially associated with ubiquitin chains. SARS-CoV-2 NSP12 was primarily associated with K63-linked polyubiquitin chains, which increased SARS-CoV-2 NSP12 stability relative to OC43 NSP12, which was associated with K48 chains. Additionally, we identify the atypical E3 ubiquitin ligase MYCBP2 as a mediator of serine ubiquitination of SARS-CoV-2 NSP12 on serine-564 and observe that MYCBP2 promotes SARS-CoV-2 replication in cell-based assays. Substitution of this single residue (S564A) in CoV-2 NSP12 prevented recovery of infectious virus in three independent attempts, precluding direct genetic validation of its role in viral replication. To our knowledge, these findings provide the first evidence of serine ubiquitination of a viral protein and suggest a previously unrecognized role for RdRp ubiquitination in coronavirus biology. IMPORTANCE Viruses often hijack host post-translational modification systems, including ubiquitination, to enhance the functions of their proteins and evade host innate immune responses. We screened the viral proteins of SARS-CoV-2 and found that NSP2, NSP5, NSP12, NSP15, and NSP16 are ubiquitinated. Focusing on NSP12, the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp), we found that it is associated with multiple types of ubiquitin modifications, and RdRp proteins from other coronaviruses are differentially ubiquitinated. We also found that SARS-CoV-2 RdRp undergoes ubiquitination on a serine, rather than a canonical lysine residue, mediated by the atypical E3 ubiquitin ligase, MYCBP2. Consistent with this, MYCBP2 promotes efficient SARS-CoV-2 replication in cell-based assays. To our knowledge, this study provides the first evidence of non-lysine ubiquitination of a viral protein and demonstrates the serine selectivity of MYCBP2 for the first time in a cellular context. These findings raise important questions about the regulatory function of serine NSP12 ubiquitination in coronavirus replication and its potential contribution to viral pathogenicity.

These findings raise important questions about the regulatory function of serine NSP12 ubiquitination in coronavirus replication and its potential contribution to viral pathogenicity.

title: Craniofacial trauma: experience in private hospital care during the pandemic provoked by SARS-CoV-2
abstract: Introducción: El inicio de la pandemia provocada por SARS-CoV-2 trajo consigo importantes cambios en los cuidados hospitalarios para todas las enfermedades.De acuerdo con la literatura internacional, desde el comienzo, y a consecuencia del aislamiento, ha existido un impacto en la incidencia, la etiología y la gravedad del trauma craneomaxilofacial.Objetivo: Estudiar las características del trauma craneofacial en los pacientes ingresados a un hospital privado en la Ciudad de México durante la pandemia por SARS-CoV-2.Método: Se revisaron los expedientes clínicos de los pacientes ingresados a Médica Sur, entre marzo de 2020 y junio de 2021.Se analizaron la incidencia, la etiología, la gravedad de las lesiones y el resultado de la prueba de reacción en cadena de la polimerasa para SARS-CoV-2 que se realizó durante la atención hospitalaria.Resultados: En México no existe un estudio semejante al nuestro, pero los resultados fueron similares a los reportados por otros centros hospitalarios en el mundo, presentando un mayor número de casos clasificados como traumatismo craneofacial leve, además de encontrar que el principal grupo de edad afectado fueron los adultos mayores.Conclusiones: La información reportada en nuestro estudio brinda un panorama general sobre las características del trauma craneofacial durante la pandemia por SARS-CoV-2.

title: Rehabilitación respiratoria y funcional temprana tras neumonía asociada a COVID-19 en una persona mayor: estudio de caso con ejercicios progresivos en sedestac
abstract: Functional recovery after COVID-19-associated pneumonia may be limited by dyspnea, muscle weakness, chest pain, deconditioning, and loss of autonomy, particularly in older adults after prolonged hospitalization. This study aimed to describe the application and clinical-functional course of a progressive respiratory and functional exercise system in a woman older than 65 years during the early post-discharge phase. A descriptive single-case design with 30-day follow-up was conducted using clinical-functional observation, analysis of ventilatory mechanics, and graded motor tasks performed in a seated position. The participant had controlled hypertension and hypercholesterolemia and, after approximately 21 days of hospitalization, presented chest pain, occasional cough, fatigue, perceived breathing difficulty, and reduced muscle strength. The intervention comprised four progressive upper-limb tasks intended to promote scapulothoracic mobility, thoracic expansion, postural control, and muscular activation related to ventilatory mechanics. At day 20, an observationally favorable course was documented in movement tolerance and perceived breathing capacity; by day 30, greater functional autonomy and no reported episodes of breathlessness during usual activities were recorded. These observations must be interpreted cautiously because they derive from a single case and were not supported by standardized physiological outcomes. Current evidence supports individualized pulmonary rehabilitation after COVID-19, while emphasizing the need to rule out exertional desaturation, cardiac impairment, and post-exertional symptom exacerbation before exercise training. For future replication, the protocol should include objective monitoring, validated functional tests, symptom scales, and explicit stopping criteria. The case contributes a feasible low-resource sequence for early functional progression while highlighting the methodological and safety requirements necessary for stronger clinical inference.

title: Adding spotlight on the interplay between Covid-19 and the host’s immune system: The case of the HLA partner
abstract: Background: COVID-19 has varying susceptibility, severity, and mortality rates across different patients’ populations. We aim to investigate any possible impact of HLA polymorphisms on disease’s clinical course. Method and Material: One hundred thirty-three previously affected individuals of Greek origin, were tested for anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG and IgA antibody titers and had HLA high resolution typing. Among them, ninety did not require hospitalization (O1), whereas thirty-three were hospitalized (O2). The following parameters were investigated: frequency of occurrence of various HLA alleles, variations between the two groups, correlations between anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG and IgA antibody titers, HLA polymorphisms and disease’s clinical severity. Results: We report higher frequency of expression of HLA - A*24:02 (p=0.0176), A32:01 (p=0.0127), A*68:01 (p =0.0205), DRB1*16:01 (p=0.0067) in the O1 subgroup and higher frequency of expression of HLA-A*03:01 (p=0.0067), A*31:01 (p=0.0082) and B*47:01 (p=0.0265) alleles in the O2 subgroup. Among participants with HLA*A24:02 expression, IgG antibody levels were higher in the O1 subgroup compared to the O2 subgroup (p=0.0000157). Conversely, the average titers of IgG and IgA anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibodies were higher in the O2 compared to the O1 subgroup (p=0.00006 and 0.000341, accordingly). Conclusions: This work brings light to the complex interplay between the virus and host’s immune system, suggesting that genetic defined parameters may play a role on disease’s clinical course. More relevant efforts are required in a global scale level to further investigate this complicated issue.

title: Correlation between Soluble Immunosenescence Biomarkers and Serum Neopterin Levels after COVID-19 Vaccination in a Geriatric Population
abstract: The geriatric population is increasing worldwide, including in Indonesia which has reached 11.01% in 2021 as the leading country in the geriatric population in Southeast Asia. Consequently, there is an increased risk of having severe infection, malignancy, and autoimmunity. Aging of immunity (immunosenescence) is responsible not only for those conditions but also affects the immune response to vaccination. The study's purpose was to analyze the correlation between immunosenescence and a decreased cellular immune response between 6 and 24 weeks after the second dose of CoronaVac vaccination in the geriatric population. This was an observational analytical study with a prospective cohort design. 73 geriatric subjects (≥ 60 years old) who had already received a second dose of CoronaVac were included. All the subjects had blood taken at 6 and 24 weeks after the second dose of CoronaVac. Serum sCD28, sCD80, and sCTLA-4 were used as immunosenescence markers. The decrease in cellular immunity was measured by the decreasing level of serum neopterin between 6 and 24 weeks following vaccine administration. There is a moderate correlation between sCD28, sCD80, and sCTLA-4 with serum neopterin at weeks 6 and 24. We also found a significant correlation between the decrease in neopterin at 6 and 24 weeks with sCD80 (p = 0.016, r = 0.282) but not with sCD28 (p = 0.078, r = 0.207) or sCTLA-4 (p = 0.017, r = 0.279). sCD80 and sCTLA-4 correlated with a more rapid decrease in neopterin level after CoronaVac vaccination in the geriatric population.

title: Cardiovascular Complications of COVID-19: Acute Injury, Post-Acute Sequelae, and Long-Term Cardiovascular Risk
abstract: The virus responsible for the disease COVID-19, which has greatly influenced health care worldwide, is referred to as severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). Although it is clear that this infection impacts the respiratory system, there have been many incidences where coronavirus affects the circulatory system as well. Various studies have identified correlations between coronavirus and different cardiovascular complications. These viruses infect the host cells via ACE2 receptors, which interfere with the renin angiotensin aldosterone systems, causing inflammation and damaging the blood vessels, resulting in damage to cardiac muscle cells. Consequently, heart attack, myocarditis, arrhythmia, thrombosis, heart failure, and ischemic heart disease develop in patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection. People who have cardiac disease before the infection are at increased risk of the impact of the coronavirus infections. Finally, post-COVID syndrome (long COVID) is also associated with cardiovascular complications including chest pain, palpitation, dyspnea, fatigue, tachypnea, tachycardia, and myocardial damage. Numerous studies have found that there are patterns in the relationship between coronavirus and different complications related to heart health.
journal: International Journal of Pharmaceutical Sciences and Drug Research

title: TRIPS Flexibilities and Equitable Access to Medicines in Pandemics: A TWAIL Analysis of HIV/AIDS and COVID-19 Experiences
abstract: During pandemics, States require vaccines and medicines on a mass scale, at affordable cost and without delay, to combat infectious diseases. Vaccines and medicines, however, are subject to twenty-year patent rights. The patent system under the TRIPS Agreement restricts the production and export of low-cost generic versions of new medicines. Most low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) cannot afford expensive patented medicines. They also lack the resources and infrastructure to produce generic medicines and consequently depend heavily on pharmaceutical imports. Yet they are also unable to use compulsory licences to import medicines, because Article 31(f) of the TRIPS Agreement restricts generic-producing nations from exporting to them: it allows those nations to use compulsory licences predominantly for the supply of their own domestic market. Article 31bis, which implements paragraph 6 of the Doha Declaration, permits export and import under strict and complex conditions, and there has been only one successful use of the system it codifies, Rwanda’s import of HIV medicines from Canada under the 2003 waiver. Moreover, the patent system cannot be viewed in isolation: the patent–trade secret duopoly extends protection beyond the twenty-year patent term. TRIPS flexibilities therefore operate as strategies that maintain the disparities in negotiating power between pharmaceutical companies and LMICs, and thus the status quo. HIV/AIDS and COVID-19 are the two principal pandemics to have occurred since the adoption of the TRIPS Agreement. Drawing on a comparative analysis of these two pandemics, this paper examines a central question: why does reliance solely on the public health-related TRIPS flexibilities not appear to be a sufficient means of ensuring fair and equitable access to medicines in pandemics? It argues that the TRIPS flexibilities are not sufficient to ensure fair and equitable access to medicines, particularly in pandemics, and proposes legal mechanisms to mitigate the adverse consequences arising from the limitations of the TRIPS flexibilities in addressing future pandemics.
journal: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities

title: In Silico Variant Analysis Identifies Mutations in TP53 Gene Increasing The Risk of Cancer in COVID-19 Patients
abstract: Introduction: The Coronavirus 2019 (COVID-19) disease caused by SARS-CoV-2 emerged as a global pandemic due to its lethal nature and great potential to spread rapidly. It is predicted that the coronavirus infection can leave detrimental consequences in infected patients even after recovery. Therefore considering the ability of the virus to induce lethal mutations in the host genome, we aimed to identify variants in COVID-19 patients irrespective of their origin. Methods: For the present study, transcriptomic data of patients were retrieved from the GEO dataset of the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) (GSE216811 and GSE197976 (India), GSE174786 (Germany), GSE171052 (Canada), GSE 206264 (Spain) and GSE206677 (Japan)). Each dataset was assessed independently for Single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). After quality check and removing low-quality reads the samples were normalized using Bcf-tools norms. Further, SnpEff eff and SIFT4g annotator was used to identify and annotate variants occurring in each sample. The common variants occurring in all the patients of COVID-19. Were identified through a Venn diagram. The systems biology approach was used to identify hub genes out of common mutated genes. Results and Discussion: CytoHUBBA plug-in of Cytoscape identified TP53 as the hub gene mutated due to COVID- 19 infection. TP53 is a tumor suppressor gene that plays an important role in DNA damage repair, cell cycle regulation, and inducing apoptosis. Conclusion: Therefore, we conclude that mutation in TP53 causes loss of suppression potential of the gene increasing the risk of cancer in such individuals.

title: Future Jobs for People with Disabilities Post-COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Abstract Technology was the driving force behind future employment for people with disabilities and created opportunities, but it posed challenges regarding the gap between PWD and people without disabilities. Driven largely by the expansion of remote and hybrid work, current employment rates for PWD saw remarkable gains, even outpacing those of nondisabled workers in some sectors. The call of post-pandemic RTO mandates could erode the progress in flexibility of work and technology achieved by PWD in term of progress in the labor market during the pandemic in the United Kingdom and United States. In both countries, the legal framework encourages this kind of flexible working as a potential reasonable accommodation/adjustment, though the United Kingdom had implemented more explicit, universal rights to request it. The second half of the chapter examines the role of AI as a potential to enhance future work opportunities for workers with disabilities in both the United Kingdom and the United States through advanced assistive technologies and flexible work options. However, the realization of this potential could heavily be contingent on proactive policy and regulatory frameworks in each country to address inherent biases in AI-powered hiring tools and government systems. The post-pandemic labor market offered some potential for positive change, largely driven by technological shifts. However, despite the opportunities, the economic situation in many LMICs stayed the same or even worsened. In many of these countries the lack of robust, disability-inclusive policies and social safety nets would make individuals with disabilities vulnerable to economic shocks.
journal: Prospects for Employment of Persons with Disabilities in the Post-COVID-19 Era

title: Employment for Persons with Disabilities in the Twenty-First Century Before, During, and After the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Abstract Prior to the pandemic, both the United Kingdom and United States saw increasing employment rates for people with disabilities, driven by policy shifts, strong economies, and rising self-reporting of disabilities. However, significant employment gaps persisted, and workers with disabilities often faced inequality in pay, opportunities, and workplace accommodations. There was a steady increase in the number of people with disabilities who worked in the United Kingdom between 2013 and 2019. However, the gap between disabled and nondisabled people narrowed, but a substantial disparity remained. Despite improvements, workers with disabilities still faced notable inequalities. They were more likely to be in part-time work and lower-skilled occupations. Prior to the pandemic, employees with disabilities were more likely to face discrimination, leading to lower wages, fewer opportunities for advancement, and a lack of necessary accommodation. Employment for people with disabilities in the United Kingdom and United States had seen significant shifts in the twenty-first century, particularly shaped by the COVID-19 pandemic. While pre-pandemic efforts showed some progress, the pandemic temporarily reversed trends before accelerating new opportunities, most notably the expansion of remote work. For workers with disabilities in Low-Middle-Income-Countries (LMICs), the COVID-19 pandemic amplified preexisting systemic disadvantages. While the pandemic caused widespread job loss, workers with disabilities, who were already disproportionately in the informal sector, suffered more severe economic impacts. Post-pandemic, recovery has been uneven, with some progress seen through remote work, but the employment gap persists.

title: The Impacts of the COVID-19 Pandemicon National Economic Welfare: The GenuineProgress Indicator for Iceland
abstract: This study assesses the economic impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic in Iceland using the Genuine Progress Indicator (GPI), an alternative macroeconomic measure that incorporates environmental and social externalities omitted from GDP. It updates Iceland’s GPI from 2000–2023, with primary focus on the pandemic period (2019–2023), based on a methodology comprising 28 sub-indicators. Key findings reveal contrasting trends. While GDP fell by 6.0% in the pandemic’s first year, the GPI showed sustained welfare levels. Government investments in education, healthcare, and infrastructure more than offset rising social costs (mainly from unemployment) and declining environmental costs (notably reduced non-renewable resource use and greenhouse gas emissions). Following the full lifting of travel restrictions in 2022 and the tourism boom, both indicators rebounded strongly in 2022 and 2023. The GPI grew by 12.7% and 6.8%, while GDP increased by 18.7% and 11.0%. The results provide indications of Iceland’s economic resilience during crisis and recovery.

title: Unraveling the Effects of SARS-CoV-2 on Dementia: A Comprehensive Study
abstract: Since late 2019, a pandemic caused by SARS-CoV-2, a highly contagious coronavirus, has jeopardized human and public health. Neurodegeneration and structural brain diseases produce dementia, which is developing rapidly. Strong evidence of COVID-19 brain abnormalities as neurotrophic viruses impair neurological systems. Neuron and glial cell degeneration can affect nerve transmission and brain function. Damage to these brain components raises dementia risk. Multiple studies linked SARS-CoV-2 to dementia. This manuscript contains selective data. This study aims to review the findings and suggest strategies to improve SARS-COVID dementia management. The study makes use of medical research databases like Google Scholar, PubMed, Medline, and Embase. Furthermore, information is also collected by recognized health organizations and government agencies. COVID-19 can produce neuropsychological deficits, agitation, confusion, inattention, and disorientation. Thus, SARS can worsen dementia and neurodegeneration. This article summarizes COVID-19's effects on dementia patients from several sources. The focus on existing treatments for affected patients ties the two.

title: Response to awake prone positioning in ICU patients with COVID-19 differs according to oxygenation interface: a prospective cohort study
abstract: Awake prone positioning (APP) has been widely used in patients with COVID-19-related acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), but its effectiveness may vary depending on the oxygenation interface. This study aimed to compare the response to APP according to different oxygenation interfaces and to identify predictors of response. We conducted a prospective observational study including adult patients admitted to the intensive care unit for severe to critical COVID-19, from March to May 2021. APP sessions of at least 30 min were performed within the first 24 h using conventional oxygen therapy (COT), high-flow nasal oxygen (HFNO), and noninvasive ventilation (NIV), applied sequentially when tolerated. Arterial blood gases were measured before and 20 min after each session. Response was defined as an increase of ≥ 20% in the PaO2/FiO2 ratio. Fifty-six patients were included. Response rates differed across interfaces: 25.5% under COT, 34.4% under HFNO, and 43.9% under NIV. Responders under COT and HFNO had lower intubation rates (p = 0.03 and p = 0.01, respectively), and responders under HFNO had shorter hospital stays (p = 0.018). Mortality was higher among non-responders for all interfaces except NIV (p = 0.6). Higher body mass index (BMI) was associated with response under COT and HFNO, with ROC analysis identifying a predictive cutoff between 27.3 and 28.3 kg/m2. The response to APP differs according to the oxygenation interface. APP response may be associated with improved clinical outcomes, particularly under COT and HFNO. Higher BMI appears to predict a favorable response. These findings should be interpreted cautiously given the observational design and sequential application of interfaces.
journal: Egyptian Journal of Critical Care Medicine

title: Nasal Vaccine: A Special Prominence on SARS-CoV-2
abstract: Nasal administration of mucosal medications and vaccines is an alternate and promising method of drug and vaccine delivery. Mucosal pathways can be used selectively for various disorders due to many benefits. Many initiatives are now being made to yield effective medications and cutting-edge nasal delivery systems. The structure of the nasal cavity and key features were discussed in this review. With a focus on vaccine distribution, the benefits, successes, and difficulties of using the nasal route for medical purposes were examined. The strong result supports the benefits and security, of the safety of nasal medication and vaccination administration. This alternate path may help many unmet medical needs and may also make big vaccination drives or expensive, protracted chronic therapies possible. Today, despite some lingering criticism, the area of nasal medicine and vaccine delivery is expanding quickly, supported by recent advancements in nanotechnology, imaging, and administration devices. The variety of drugs that have been licensed for nasal delivery is expected to increase significantly.

title: The Impact of Extended COVID-19 Lockdowns on Scottish Residents’ Mental Health
abstract: This article will explore Michel Foucault’s ideas with respect to the coronavirus pandemic (COVID-19), focusing on biopolitics and the influence of the surveillance state. The impact of extended and extensive lockdowns on the mental health of Scottish residents is scrutinized from a Foucauldian perspective. A key limitation of using Foucault’s framework for analysing the pandemic must be recognized. While Foucault’s perspective focuses on control mechanisms, it might lead to viewing all public health measures with suspicion. For example, the UK’s vaccination campaign was said to have prevented approximately 100,000 deaths, demonstrating that biopower can be beneficial, not solely oppressive. The framework is most useful not as a comprehensive critique but to challenge uncomfortable assumptions about who wields power, whose lives are valued, and how consent is created. In this way, it remains a vital perspective for understanding not only COVID-19, but also the broader dynamics between governance, bodies, and society.
journal: International Journal of Mental Health Research
