title: Small Area Estimation of Case Growths for Timely COVID-19 Outbreak Detection
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has exerted a profound impact on the global economy and continues to exact a significant toll on human lives. The COVID-19 case growth rate stands as a key epidemiological parameter to estimate and monitor for effective detection and containment of the resurgence of outbreaks. A fundamental challenge in growth rate estimation and hence outbreak detection is balancing the accuracy-speed tradeoff, where accuracy typically degrades with shorter fitting windows. In this paper, we develop a machine learning (ML) algorithm, which we call Transfer Learning Generalized Random Forest (TLGRF), that balances this accuracy-speed tradeoff. Specifically, we estimate the instantaneous COVID-19 exponential growth rate for each U.S. county by using TLGRF that chooses an adaptive fitting window size based on relevant day-level and county-level features affecting the disease spread. Through transfer learning, TLGRF can accurately estimate case growth rates for counties with small sample sizes. Out-of-sample prediction analysis shows that TLGRF outperforms established growth rate estimation methods. Furthermore, we conducted a case study based on outbreak case data from the state of Colorado and showed that the timely detection of outbreaks could have been improved by up to 224% using TLGRF when compared to the decisions made by Colorado's Department of Health and Environment (CDPHE). To facilitate implementation, we have developed a publicly available outbreak detection tool for timely detection of COVID-19 outbreaks in each U.S. county, which received substantial attention from policymakers.

title: Mortality Due to Mental and Behavioral Disorders Before, During, and After the COVID-19 Public Health Emergency in Espírito Santo, Brazil: A Population-Based Ecological Time-Series Study
abstract: Background: Public health crises may disrupt mental health care and alter mortality patterns. We analyzed temporal patterns in mortality from mental and behavioral disorders in Espírito Santo, Brazil, from 2010 to 2024, encompassing the pre-pandemic, COVID-19 emergency, and subsequent periods. Methods: We conducted a population-based ecological time-series study using data from the Brazilian Mortality Information System from 2010 to 2024. We included deaths among residents of Espírito Santo whose underlying cause was coded as F00–F99 in the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th Revision (ICD-10). Monthly mortality rates were analyzed using a continuous segmented Prais–Winsten regression of log10-transformed rates, with prespecified transitions in March 2020 and June 2022 and adjustment for calendar-month seasonality. Segment-specific annual percent changes (APCs) and 95% confidence intervals were estimated. Results: We identified 4256 deaths. Males accounted for 79.0% of deaths, and alcohol dependence syndrome accounted for 68.0% of deaths. Mortality decreased during the pre-pandemic period (APC, −4.99%; 95% CI, −6.63% to −3.32%; p < 0.001), increased markedly during the COVID-19 emergency period (APC, +42.00%; 95% CI, 30.24% to 54.81%; p < 0.001), and decreased during the subsequent period (APC, −29.27%; 95% CI, −36.73% to −20.93%; p < 0.001). Alcohol dependence remained the predominant underlying cause, while disorders related to multiple drug use and cocaine gained relative importance. Conclusions: Mortality from mental and behavioral disorders showed a marked increase during the COVID-19 emergency followed by a subsequent decline. These findings reinforce the importance of continuous mortality surveillance and maintaining access to mental health and substance use disorder care during periods of health-system disruption.
journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health

title: Aerosol transmission and mask guidance in Spain during COVID-19: An analysis of institutional health communication, 2020–2025
abstract: Research background: Institutional health communication during public health emergencies shapes risk understanding, protective behaviour, and public trust. During the COVID-19 pandemic, mask recommendations had direct implications for protection against aerosol transmission, for which scientific evidence increasingly consolidated between 2020 and 2021. High-filtration respirators (FFP2/N95) provide substantially better protection than surgical or hygienic masks, yet official guidance in Spain consistently prioritised the latter. Purpose: To examine how the Spanish Ministry of Health communicated about mask use between January 2020 and December 2025. Methodology: A documentary content analysis was conducted on 2,060 press releases and 143 institutional campaign materials. Findings: Low-filtration masks were referenced substantially more frequently than high-filtration respirators across both sources. Aerosol transmission was not mentioned in any campaign material. A marked dissociation emerged in 2021: the highest proportion of high-filtration references in press releases (58.3%) coincided with a vaccination campaign in which all protagonists wore surgical masks. Influenza campaign materials did not include any reference to high-filtration protection in any annual cycle. Practical implications: These findings document a systematic pattern of limited visibility of high-filtration protection across the communication formats analysed, with important implications for pandemic preparedness and public health messaging. Originality / value: This study offers a novel, longitudinal analysis of Spanish health communication that reveals a persistent omission of high-filtration respirators despite evolving evidence on aerosol transmission. It bridges institutional messaging and scientific consensus with direct implications for pandemic risk communication.

source_records.abstract: Research background: Institutional health communication during public health emergencies shapes risk understanding, protective behaviour, and public trust. During the COVID-19 pandemic, mask recommendations had direct implications for protection against aerosol transmission, for which scientific evidence increasingly consolidated between 2020 and 2021. High-filtration respirators (FFP2/N95) provide substantially better protection than surgical or hygienic masks, yet official guidance in Spain consistently prioritised the latter. Purpose: To examine how the Spanish Ministry of Health communicated about mask use between January 2020 and December 2025. Methodology: A documentary content analysis was conducted on 2,060 press releases and 143 institutional campaign materials. Findings: Low-filtration masks were referenced substantially more frequently than high-filtration respirators across both sources. Aerosol transmission was not mentioned in any campaign material. A marked dissociation emerged in 2021: the highest proportion of high-filtration references in press releases (58.3%) coincided with a vaccination campaign in which all protagonists wore surgical masks. Influenza campaign materials did not include any reference to high-filtration protection in any annual cycle. Practical implications: These findings document a systematic pattern of limited visibility of high-filtration protection across the communication formats analysed, with important implications for pandemic preparedness and public health messaging. Originality / value: This study offers a novel, longitudinal analysis of Spanish health communication that reveals a persistent omission of high-filtration respirators despite evolving evidence on aerosol transmission. It bridges institutional messaging and scientific consensus with direct implications for pandemic risk communication.

title: ATTITUDES AND PRACTICES TOWARDS COVID-19 AND SEASONAL FLU VACCINES AND VACCINATION IN THE GENERAL POPULATION AND AMONG MEDICAL PROFESSIONALS
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has led to the development of several types of vaccines, among which messenger RNA (mRNA)-based vaccines have represented a significant breakthrough. This study aimed to evaluate attitudes towards COVID-19 and seasonal influenza vaccination among the general population and individuals with a medical background. A questionnaire was developed to collect sociodemographic data, personal health information, vaccination status, and information on participants’ attitudes towards and knowledge of vaccines. The profile of the typical participant was an employed woman with tertiary education, living with another person in an urban area and reporting generally good health. The typical participant had received at least two doses of the Sputnik V vaccine. Participants generally expressed favourable attitudes towards regular COVID-19 vaccination. The results showed no apparent differences between participants with and without a medical background regarding vaccine choice, the decision to receive a third dose, or seasonal influenza vaccination. Similarly, no apparent differences were observed in attitudes towards the AstraZeneca vaccine or mandatory COVID-19 vaccination between respondents with and without a medical background.

title: Estimação de Parâmetros e Estados em um Modelo Epidemiológico SIR Aplicado à Evolução da Covid-19 na cidade de Itabuna-BA
abstract: Nos anos recentes, a doença infecciosa Covid-19 causada pelo coronavírus SARS-CoV-2 se tornou uma das epidemias mais mortais na história humana. Este artigo tem como objetivo realizar a estimação dos parâmetros em um modelo epidemiológico SIR envolvendo os dados da Covid-19 para alcançar os parâmetros de infecção e de recuperação que tornem o modelo o mais realístico possível. Além disso, pretende-se realizar a estimação dos estados do modelo SIR quando este está sujeito à ruídos aleatórios. As metodologias utilizadas para realizar a estimação dos parâmetros e dos estados foram o método dos mínimos quadrados o e filtro de Kalman estendido. As simulações computacionais foram realizadas via software Scilab. Como resultado foi alcançado um modelo epidemiológico aproximado com a realidade dos dados da doença da Covid-19 no período determinado em Itabuna-BA.

title: LINKING SUSTAINABILITY PERFORMANCE TO STOCK RESILIENCE DURING AND AFTER COVID-19 CRISIS: EVIDENCE FROM SOUTHEAST ASIA
abstract: Background: The COVID-19 pandemic severely disrupted markets. While sustainability performance measured by ESG scores theoretically buffers against shocks, its efficacy in emerging markets with nascent sustainability frameworks remains underexplored. Method: We analyze a balanced panel of 1,395 observations from 279 non-financial Southeast Asian firms (2020–2024). Using OLS, lagged, and fixed effects models, we compare the impact of sustainability performance on stock resilience during the 2020–2022 and post-pandemic (2023–2024) periods. Findings: Sustainability performance (ESG scores) significantly enhanced stock resilience during the pandemic. However, this protective effect dissipated post-pandemic. Results confirm a statistically significant improvement in overall resilience following the crisis, as investors redirected their focus toward traditional financial fundamentals such as profitability and leverage. Conclusion: Sustainability performance acts as situational crisis insurance. Its risk-mitigation value is highly salient during systemic uncertainty but diminishes under stable market conditions. Novelty/Originality of this article: Unlike prior single-phase studies in developed economies, this research provides longitudinal evidence on the dynamic, state-dependent nature of sustainability performance across crisis and recovery phases within Southeast Asia’s early-stage ESG landscape.

title: Investor attention and GCC stock market connectedness during the first wave of COVID-19: evidence using Google trends and VIX
abstract: This study investigates the behavioral determinants of financial market connectedness in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) during the first wave of COVID-19. It examines whether the Chicago Board Options Exchange Volatility Index (VIX), regional investor attention measured via Google Trends, and their interaction are associated with changes in connectedness. Time-varying parameter vector autoregression (TVP-VAR) is used to estimate the Total Connectedness Index (TCI) across GCC stock markets from (2018–2022). Moreover, behavioral regressions over the first wave (January–August 2020) assess the role of VIX, Google Trends-based regional attention (GTR), and their interaction. TCI nearly doubled from 31.94% during the pre-COVID period to 64.25% throughout the crisis. After controlling for oil volatility, neither VIX nor GTR was significant. Notwithstanding, their interaction is positive and statistically significant, nearly doubling the model's explanatory power. Given fundamental controls, Granger causality tests show unidirectional precedence from GTR to TCI in bivariate specifications. Results hold despite the exclusion of March 2020 and the addition of COVID-19 case growth. This study integrates TVP-VAR connectedness with behavioral finance theory in GCC markets. Crucially, it introduces Google Trends as a regional attention measure, and documents an attention–uncertainty interaction consistent with behavioral amplification through which connectedness intensifies when both channels are simultaneously elevated.

title: Mortality Surveillance Learning Module: Durán et al (2026), Multiple causes of death data to track trends of mortality from chronic diseases: Insights from the COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland.
abstract: Educational Engagement Modules (EEMs) are teaching materials for educators and students that facilitate a deeper understanding of key epidemiological methods and concepts. Each EEM poses a series of questions using a recently published paper in Annals to further understanding of a specific study design or epidemiological concept and to encourage critical thinking and careful evaluation. This EEM focuses on mortality surveillance featuring the following article: Durán N D, Kaufman JS, Chiolero A, Carmeli C. Multiple causes of death data to track trends of mortality from chronic diseases: Insights from the COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland. doi: 10.1016/j.annepidem.2025.12.002.

title: Effects of COVID-19 on Food Supply: A Systematic Review
abstract: Objective: The COVID-19 outbreak has had a significant influence on several critical industries, including agriculture, education, and the economy. This essay investigates these processes, with a focus on agriculture, where the repercussions have been particularly harsh for poor groups dealing with unpredictable food supplies and food safety. Methods: Along with a critical examination of the shift to digital education systems, the report highlights the major obstacles that lie ahead for regions lacking adequate digital infrastructure and digital literacy. There have been notable disruptions in the economy as well. Manufacturing, the financial markets, and tourism have all seen major downturns. Results and Discussion: The study emphasizes the crucial part that following safety measures and boosting immunization campaigns play in mitigating these negative consequences while supporting economic recovery. Also, new technical solutions have emerged throughout this time. The application of drone technology to contactless food delivery is a notable illustration of how creativity can overcome the challenges posed by the pandemic. Conclusion: Finally, the report recommends the development of specific and rigorous methods to strengthen recovery efforts in these critical areas.

title: COVID-19 and psychiatric inpatient admissions at a Saudi tertiary hospital, 2017-2024: an interrupted time-series study
abstract: Psychiatric inpatient admissions decreased in many countries during the COVID-19 pandemic. Most studies used a year or less of pre-pandemic data and compared the two periods directly, which cannot separate a pandemic effect from the increase that predated it, and evidence from the Middle East is limited. This study examined changes in psychiatric admission volume across the COVID-19 pandemic, with diagnostic case-mix and length of stay (LOS) examined as secondary outcomes. This interrupted time-series analysis used eight years of inpatient records from Prince Sultan Military Medical City, a tertiary hospital in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. All 1551 adult psychiatric admissions between January 2017 and November 2024 were assigned to pre-COVID (January 2017 to February 2020), during-COVID (March 2020 to December 2021), and post-COVID (January 2022 to November 2024) periods. Monthly admission counts were modeled by segmented Poisson regression. Diagnostic case-mix was assessed by chi-square tests and length of stay by a linear mixed-effects model. Before the pandemic, admissions were increasing by 1.7% per month (IRR 1.017; 95% CI 1.009-1.024), a trend concentrated in the first recording year (2017). With the baseline restricted to 2018 onward, this trend was flat. At onset admissions decreased by 31.5% (IRR 0.685; 95% CI 0.564-0.831), a reduction that persisted across baseline specifications. Monthly volume then remained near the pre-pandemic mean of 16 to 17 through 2024. Diagnostic composition differed across periods. Admissions for substance use disorders increased from 9.0% to 14.3% in the post-COVID period (absolute difference 5.3 percentage points; 95% CI 1.6-9.0), and admissions for mood disorders decreased from 37.4% to 30.5%. Length of stay showed no significant change. At this single center, admissions fell at onset and then remained near their pre-pandemic level through 2024. The diagnostic and sociodemographic differences were small and should be regarded as exploratory. Multicenter studies are needed to confirm these findings and to inform mental health service planning for future public health emergencies.

title: From COVID-19-Associated Acute Kidney Injury to Long-Term Kidney Dysfunction: Recovery Phenotypes, Risk Stratification, and Post-COVID Renal Surveillance
abstract: Background: COVID-19-associated acute kidney injury (AKI) is common in severe disease, but its long-term kidney implications are heterogeneous and incompletely defined. Objective: To synthesize recovery phenotypes and longitudinal outcomes, reconcile conflicting evidence on whether COVID-associated AKI differs from other-cause AKI, and set out implications for surveillance and management. Methods: The evidence base was assembled through a targeted PubMed/MEDLINE search for COVID-19 and kidney dysfunction (January 2020 to August 2026), hand-searching of reference lists, and direct retrieval of pivotal longitudinal cohorts and clinical practice guidelines. Longitudinal cohorts and comparative studies were prioritized. Findings: AKI severity, duration, kidney replacement therapy, lower baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and incomplete early recovery consistently identify patients at greatest risk. Longitudinal studies disagree on whether COVID-AKI confers more risk than AKI from other illnesses: early cohorts reported steeper eGFR loss, whereas a later 9624-patient cohort found lower adjusted major adverse kidney events. This divergence reflects differences in kidney reference point, outcome construction, ascertainment, and handling of competing death rather than genuine contradiction. Population studies show long-term kidney failure is concentrated after hospitalization and severe disease. Candidate biomarkers remain investigational. Conclusions: Post-COVID kidney risk is severity- and phenotype-dependent rather than universal. Follow-up is most defensible after hospitalized AKI, incomplete recovery, advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD), dialysis, or transplantation and applies existing post-AKI guidance rather than a COVID-specific schedule. Survivors who meet Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria for CKD at three months, namely a GFR below 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 or a persistent marker of kidney damage, become eligible for guideline-directed therapy, though no trial has enrolled on recent AKI. Prospective studies should test whether structured follow-up improves outcomes.

title: REPERCUSSÕES DA PANDEMIA DA COVID-19 NA QUALIDADE DE VIDA DOS PROFESSORES REPERCUSSIONS OF THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC ON TEACHERS' QUALITY OF LIFE REPERCUSIONES DE LA PANDEMIA DE COVID-19 EN LA CALIDAD DE VIDA DE LOS PROFESORES
abstract: O estudo analisa a literatura científica publicada entre 2020 e 2024 acerca das demandas de trabalho vivenciadas por professores no contexto da pandemia de covid-19, do ensino remoto e do retorno às atividades presenciais, considerando suas repercussões na qualidade de vida docente. Trata-se de uma revisão de literatura, de abordagem qualitativa e caráter descritivo-analítico, fundamentada na concepção multidimensional de qualidade de vida da Organização Mundial da Saúde e nos domínios contemplados pelo Whoqol-Bref. As buscas foram realizadas em maio de 2026, no Portal de Periódicos da Coordenação de Aperfeiçoamento de Pessoal de Nível Superior (CAPES) e na base Education Resources Information Center (ERIC), utilizando termos relacionados à qualidade de vida, à saúde docente, à pandemia, ao ensino remoto e ao retorno às atividades presenciais. Foram identificados 781 registros, sendo 167 na CAPES e 614 na ERIC. Após a aplicação dos critérios de inclusão e exclusão e a leitura dos estudos potencialmente elegíveis, 16 artigos compuseram a análise. Os achados foram organizados em dois eixos temáticos: repercussões da pandemia e do retorno às atividades presenciais; e qualidade de vida dos professores. Os estudos analisados evidenciaram necessidade de adaptação pedagógica, reorganização curricular, diagnóstico e recomposição das aprendizagens, além de estresse, redução do tempo de descanso e sobreposição entre trabalho e vida pessoal dos docentes. Conclui-se que as demandas de trabalho e as condições de exercício da docência, no período analisado, envolveram aspectos relacionados à atuação individual dos professores, às condições institucionais e às dimensões físicas, psicológicas e sociais da qualidade de vida.

Os estudos analisados evidenciaram necessidade de adaptação pedagógica, reorganização curricular, diagnóstico e recomposição das aprendizagens, além de estresse, redução do tempo de descanso e sobreposição entre trabalho e vida pessoal dos docentes. Conclui-se que as demandas de trabalho e as condições de exercício da docência, no período analisado, envolveram aspectos relacionados à atuação individual dos professores, às condições institucionais e às dimensões físicas, psicológicas e sociais da qualidade de vida.

title: Dexmedetomidine: A Promising Agent to Enhance Tolerance of Non-invasive Ventilation in COVID-19 Patients: A Narrative Review
abstract: COVID-19 patients can exhibit a hyperinflammatory response, which may result in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and hypoxemic respiratory failure. While the effectiveness of non-invasive ventilation (NIV) for treating COVID-19 patients with ARDS is not well established, many clinicians still opt for this treatment. Patient intolerance is the primary factor limiting the use of NIV, highlighting the need for sedative agents. Dexmedetomidine (Dex), an α2 adrenergic receptor agonist, is used as a sedative and anxiolytic medication. Unlike other sedatives, Dex does not act through the GABA pathway, so it does not depress the patient's respiratory drive. This drug also exhibits antioxidant effects and modulates the inflammatory system, making it potentially more appropriate for hyper-inflammatory states in COVID-19 patients. Despite the studies, our knowledge about the choice of sedative agents in this condition remains limited. This narrative review aims to provide information about the role of sedative agents, particularly Dex, in COVID-19 patients undergoing NIV. We conducted a literature search to examine the mechanisms of the human immune response to COVID-19, the immunomodulatory effects of Dex, and how this agent can enhance the acceptance of NIV among COVID-19 patients. The beneficial effect of Dex with antioxidant and immunomodulatory mechanisms has been shown in various studies. While there is a significant amount of research regarding the role of Dex in non-COVID patients undergoing NIV, studies focusing on COVID-19 patients are limited and primarily consist of case reports and retrospective observational studies. Nevertheless, the findings suggest that Dex may help improve the tolerability of NIV. Dex not only reduces agitation and delirium but also enhances the acceptance of NIV treatment. Due to its immunomodulatory and antioxidant effects, it can be considered a viable option for improving patients' respiratory status. However, future interventional studies are essential to understand better the efficacy and safety of Dex in severe COVID-19 patients.

title: Libraries’ responses during the COVID-19 pandemic : A case study of Kuwait libraries
abstract: Public and specialized libraries, for example, can learn from the national and academic libraries’ experiences and how they dealt with the crisis to improve their services and overcome all the obstacles mentioned by the public library participants in this study. Objective: This study aims to examine the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on libraries in Kuwait, with particular emphasis on the role of national, public, specialized, and academic libraries during the pandemic. Method: An online survey was employed to collect both qualitative and quantitative data. A sample of 11 libraries was surveyed, representing all types of libraries in Kuwait, four academic libraries from both public and private universities, five public libraries, one specialized library, and the National Library of Kuwait. Results: The findings revealed a noticeable role for the academic and national libraries, in contrast to the limited roles of specialized libraries and the complete absence of activity in public libraries. Recommendations: The results and recommendations of this study are expected to be beneficial to governmental and private libraries in Kuwait and for all types (national, academic, and public), in terms of enhancing their services and resources that support individuals and society, in addition to the preparedness for any similar crisis in the future.

title: A experiência da gravidez na adolescencia no México durante a COVID-19
abstract: This article analyzes the educational and health experiences of Mexican women who experienced teenage pregnancy during and after the pandemic, aiming to identify relevant aspects for the prevention of unplanned pregnancies in future health emergencies. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with six women who became pregnant between 2019 and 2023. Their testimonies revealed significant difficulties in accessing and participating in online classes, as well as a perception of insufficient support and interest from the educational community. In the health field, participants expressed fear of attending medical appointments during pregnancy due to the risk of COVID-19 infection. They also indicated that the mandatory use of masks during childbirth made breathing and labor difficult. The results highlight educational and health barriers relevant to the care and prevention of teenage pregnancy in the context of health emergencies.

title: Thrombocytopenia and Other Hematological Features in COVID-19 Patients Referred to Shahid Mostafa Khomeini Hospital
abstract: Introduction: COVID-19 is a deadly virus, but there is still no appropriate cure for it. Hence, the target of this study was to estimate the clinical value of thrombocytopenia and other blood parameters in COVID-19 patients referred to Ilam Shahid Mostafa Khomeini Hospital from April and September 2020. Materials and Methods: In this cross-sectional study, patients with thrombocytopenia, associated with COVID-19, diagnosed at the Shahid Mostafa Khomeini Hospital in Ilam City during the spring and summer of 2020 were included. A checklist was used to record the hematological indicators of the patients. Further, an analysis of data using SPSS V20 software was performed. Results and Discussion: Overall, 66 thrombocytopenic patients were studied. Among patients who succumbed to the disease complications, 40 (67.8%) were male, and 19 (32.2%) were female. Mortality and survival rates were 90% and 10%, respectively. Conclusion: Due to the high mortality rate of COVID-19 patients with thrombocytopenia, platelet count can be considered a major risk factor, as well as a prognostic and diagnostic indicator in these patients.

title: Revealing the Unseen: Post COVID-19 Biomarkers, Severity, and Outcome Mysteries
abstract: Background: Although the COVID-19 pandemic has passed, some patients still experience post-COVID-19 symptoms. It has been reported that COVID-19 symptoms can persist for more than three months after recovery. Objective: This study aims to analyze biomarkers, severity, and outcome factors associated with post-COVID-19 symptoms. Methods: This prospective cohort study involves hospitalised COVID-19 patients who were followed for up to 3 months after discharge. Clinical examinations and laboratory tests for MMP-9, TIMP-1, and IL-6 were conducted during hospitalisation and after three months. Results: We enrolled 76 COVID-19 patients, with a mortality rate of 30.26%. Among them, 55 individuals (30.91%) had no residual symptoms, 54.5% had acute COVID-19, 9.09% had ongoing COVID-19, and 5.45% had long-term COVID-19. Symptomatic post-COVID-19 had oxygen demand and respiratory rates higher than no-symptoms groups. Early IL-6, IL-10, MMP-9, and TIMP- 1 were lower in symptomatic post-COVID-19 compared to dead and asymptomatic post-COVID-19 groups. IL-6 and MMP-9 decrease, and TIMP-1 increases after cure. IL-6 significantly still increases in post-COVID-19 symptoms compared to no-symptoms (p=0.01). Patients more than 50 years old and critically ventilated patients are prone to have symptoms post-COVID-19. Conclusions: More than half of patients suffer from post-COVID-19 symptoms with various related factors. Even though IL-6 decreases after recovery, IL-6 levels are still higher in symptomatic post- COVID-19 patients.

title: CÔNG NGHỆ mRNA HẬU COVID-19: ỨNG DỤNG MỚI, RÀO CẢN KỸ THUẬT VÀ HÀM Ý ĐỐI VỚI VIỆT NAM
abstract: Sau đại dịch COVID-19, công nghệ mRNA đã mở rộng từ nền tảng chủ yếu phục vụ vaccine phòng bệnh truyền nhiễm thành một nền tảng dược phẩm sinh học đa mục tiêu, với các hướng phát triển nổi bật gồm vaccine thế hệ mới, vaccine ung thư cá thể hóa và liệu pháp thay thế protein. Bài viết thực hiện tổng quan tường thuật có cấu trúc đối với các công bố trên PubMed/Medline, Scopus và Web of Science từ năm 2005 đến ngày 25 tháng 8 năm 2026; thư viện Y học Quốc gia Hoa Kỳ và tài liệu quản lý được đối chiếu khi cần cập nhật tình trạng lâm sàng và pháp lý. Từ 185 tài liệu xác định ban đầu, 22 công bố khoa học được lựa chọn cho tổng hợp chính. Kết quả cho thấy mRNA có ưu thế về tốc độ thiết kế, khả năng chuẩn hóa một số công đoạn sản xuất và tính linh hoạt đối với y học chính xác. Bằng chứng hậu COVID-19 đã mở rộng sang RSV, cúm mùa, vaccine phối hợp, ung thư và một số bệnh chuyển hóa di truyền. Tuy nhiên, độ ổn định của RNA, hiệu quả và độ an toàn của lipid nanoparticles (LNP), khả năng hướng mô đích, yêu cầu dùng lặp lại, kiểm soát chất lượng và chi phí sản xuất vẫn là những thách thức đáng kể. Đối với Việt Nam, bài viết đề xuất lộ trình phát triển theo từng nhóm năng lực, từ thiết kế mRNA-tin sinh học và LNP-kiểm nghiệm đến tiền lâm sàng, lâm sàng và sản xuất. Đây là các hàm ý từ bằng chứng quốc tế và bối cảnh chính sách hiện hành, không thay thế cho một đánh giá chuyên biệt về năng lực quốc gia.
journal: Tạp chí Nghiên cứu Khoa học và Phát triển

title: The impact of COVID-19 on investors’ behavior: the case of anchoring and 52 week high
abstract: This paper aims to examine how the COVID-19 pandemic influenced investor behavior in Kuwait’s emerging market, focusing on changes in anchoring patterns tied to the 52-week high/low strategy. Using daily stock data from 2012 to 2024, the author find that investors typically favored momentum strategies anchored to 52-week highs. During the pandemic, however, a marked shift occurred in which investors gravitated toward stocks near their 52-week lows, likely perceiving them as undervalued or safer amid increased uncertainty. This contrarian shift proved profitable, with the 52-week low strategy outperforming during the crisis. Postpandemic, investor behavior largely reverted to momentum-based preferences. These findings highlight the temporary adaptability of anchoring heuristics under crisis conditions and offer novel insights into behavioral finance within the GCC context. The study underscores the importance of dynamic investor psychology in shaping market behavior during periods of systemic stress.

title: Polymorphisms in SARS-CoV-2 entry pathway genes are associated with COVID-19 severity : analysis of ACE1, ACE2, and TMPRSS2 polymorphisms in a Slovenian cohort
abstract: Raziskava je proučevala povezavo med genetskimi različicami v genih, ki sodelujejo pri vstopu virusa SARS-CoV-2 v gostiteljsko celico, in težo bolezni covid-19 v slovenski populaciji. Vključenih je bilo 240 odraslih bolnikov z različno težkim potekom bolezni covida-19. Analizirani so bili izbrani polimorfizmi v genih ACE1, ACE2 in TMPRSS2, njihova povezanost s kliničnimi značilnostmi bolezni pa je bila ovrednotena z univariatnimi in multivariatnimi statističnimi modeli. Polimorfizem TMPRSS2 rs12329760 je bil povezan z blažjim potekom bolezni, medtem ko so bile posamezne različice v genih ACE1 in ACE2 povezane s trajanjem hospitalizacije in drugimi kazalniki težjega poteka bolezni. Rezultati kažejo, da lahko genetska variabilnost v poteh vstopa virusa prispeva k razlikam v kliničnem poteku covida-19. Podatkovna zbirka vsebuje psevdonimizirane demografske in genotipske podatke preiskovancev. Zaradi varovanja osebnih podatkov je dostop do zbirke omejen in je mogoč le na podlagi utemeljene zahteve ter po odobritvi skrbnika podatkov.
journal: Repository of the University of Ljubljana (University of Ljubljana)

title: From Intubation to Tracheal Resection: Navigating Severe Airway Complications in a Post-COVID-19 Patient with Comorbidities
abstract: Laryngotracheal stenosis (LTS) is a significant complication post-intubation in COVID-19 patients, with incidence rates between 12.7% and 40%, exacerbated by comorbidities like diabetes and obesity. We report a 44-year-old female with type II obesity (BMI=39.8 kg/m2), diabetes mellitus, and hypertension, who developed LTS after 8 days of intubation for severe COVID-19. Her condition rapidly progressed from grade 3 to grade 4 LTS, requiring emergency tracheostomy, Shian-Yann-Lee procedure, and tracheal resection with anastomosis (TRA). Complications included anastomotic dehiscence, sepsis, and deep venous thrombosis. Serial dilatations and intralesional steroid injections (SILSI) were needed to manage restenosis. title: Presence, Severity and Evolution of Long COVID Dyspnea Correlate with Functional Capacity Measured with the Six-Minutes Walking Test (6MWT): Data from a Multicenter Cohort from Italy
abstract: The present national observational cohort study investigated in patients followed for long COVID—mostly hospitalized during acute infection—the presence, severity and evolution of dyspnea and its functional correlates. Dyspnea was assessed with the modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) dyspnea scale and its functional correlates via six-minutes walking distance (6MWD). A total of 217 individuals were evaluated. The mean difference in 6MWD between patients with and without dyspnea (mMRC score ≥ 1) was 87 m (95%CI 56–117, p < 0.001). Significant declines were observed between four and eight months from COVID-19 in prevalence of dyspnea (from 56.7% to 36.4%, p < 0.001), mean mMRC score (from 0.95 to 0.63, p < 0.001), and proportion of patients with 6MWD ˂ 65% of predicted value (from 15.5% to 9.4%, p = 0.035). Each additional point in mMRC score corresponded to −56.3 m walked at first assessment and to −47.7 m walked at second assessment. In the longitudinal analysis, each unitary mMRC score increase between the two assessments corresponded to a concurrent 6MWD reduction of 22.5 m (95%CI −40.1 to −4.8 m, p = 0.013). Although the prevalence of dyspnea reduced significantly over time, roughly one-third of patients remained affected eight months after COVID-19. The 6MWD was a sensitive measure in capturing the functional correlates of presence, severity and evolution of dyspnea.

title: Restructuring Global Supply Chains: Navigating Challenges of the COVID-19 Pandemic and Beyond
abstract: Problem definition: The COVID-19 pandemic imposed unprecedented stresses on global supply chains (GSCs), compelling companies to reassess their supply chain structures and strategies. This crisis has also heightened awareness among businesses, consumers, and policymakers about the critical importance and far-reaching implications of GSC design and management. This unique moment presents a generational opportunity for Operations Management (OM) researchers to document and understand the ongoing restructuring of GSCs. Methodology/results: By analyzing microlevel data on U.S. customs import shipments (2019–2021), we uncover shifts in GSC strategies during the COVID-19 pandemic. Firms diversified suppliers within existing sourcing locations and reallocated volumes among them. Whereas dependence on China decreased, imports from other Asian nations like India and Vietnam, as well as North American countries like Canada and Mexico, increased. Industry-specific differences were pronounced, and a notable shift toward lower-frequency, higher-quantity shipments was also observed. Managerial implications: Beyond the challenges of COVID-19, recent years have witnessed other major supply chain disruptions, due to causes such as geopolitical tensions, natural disasters, and port worker strikes. We offer actionable insights for executives designing supply chain strategies to prepare for similar disruptions as they increase in frequency and severity. We identify future research avenues aimed at enhancing the resilience and adaptability of GSCs in a continuously evolving environment. Supplemental Material: The online appendix is available at https://doi.org/10.1287/msom.2024.0879 .

title: Mindfulness and anxiety in postnatal women during the COVID-19 pandemic: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Women experience many stressful events during the pregnancy and after birth, due to bio-physiological changes, Postnatal women are a group whose mental health was affected by the coronavirus (Covid-19) pandemic. Increased stress, together with the restrictive measures that many governments implemented to contain the pandemic posed mental health risks for women and infants and indicated the need for robust psychosocial therapy to support postnatal women. Mindfulness is a way to self-regulate one’s internal and external experiences moment by moment non— judgmentally with a focus attention on the present in a way which helps improve mental health and wellbeing. This study aimed to determine whether mindfulness practices led to lower anxiety levels in postnatal women during the Covid-19 pandemic.

title: Next-Gen COVID-19 Diagnosis: Integrating SegFormer, MaxViT, and Explainable AI for Advanced Lung CT Imaging
abstract: Introduction: The COVID-19 pandemic underscored the critical role of medical imaging, particularly lung CT scans, for diagnosing and monitoring the disease. Despite the importance of CT in detecting COVID-19, challenges remain in achieving high accuracy and robustness in diverse clinical settings, especially with varying image quality and presentation. This study introduces a deep learning framework combining SegFormer for segmentation and MaxViT for classification, aimed at improving the accuracy of COVID-19 diagnosis from lung CT scans using four diverse datasets. Materials and Methods: This work utilized four publicly available CT scan datasets: SARS-COV2- CTScan (Brazil), COVID-CTset (Iran), MosMedData (Russia), and BIMCV-COVID19+ (Spain), totaling 77,050 CT images from over 2,100 patients. The datasets were processed through various preprocessing and augmentation techniques, including CLAHE, noise filtering, and 3D transformations. The model’s segmentation was evaluated using the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), while classification accuracy was measured using standard metrics like precision, recall, and F1-score. Results: The proposed model achieved an average DSC of 0.91 across the datasets, with classification accuracy reaching 95.2%, 92.5%, 93.4%, and 94.1% for each dataset, respectively. Precision for COVID-19 detection was 96.4% on the SARS-COV2-CTScan dataset, with corresponding recall and F1-scores of 94.8% and 95.6%. Cross-dataset evaluations maintained consistency with an overall accuracy of 95.0% and a DSC of 0.90. Key novel metrics like the COVID-19 Severity Grading Index (97%) and Temporal Progression Index (96%) demonstrated the clinical relevance of the model. Discussion: The model demonstrated exceptional generalization ability across diverse datasets and imaging conditions. Augmentation techniques, such as MixUp and CutMix, significantly improved model robustness, with a 14% reduction in Dice loss and a 7% improvement in classification accuracy for rare cases. The explainability of the model, through attention heatmaps and feature attribution, further enhanced its clinical applicability by providing transparency and aiding decision-making. Conclusion: This study presents a robust deep-learning framework for COVID-19 detection from lung CT scans, demonstrating high accuracy, reliability, and interpretability across multiple datasets. Despite strong performance, there is room for refinement, particularly in handling noisy or atypical cases. The model is poised for clinical deployment, providing an effective tool for automated COVID-19 diagnosis and monitoring, with the potential for further improvement in real-world applications.

title: The well-being of small-scale farmers post-Covid-19 pandemic: A mediation-effect approach
abstract: Small-scale farmers are vulnerable to unpredictable threats, including climate disasters, price volatility, and health shocks. While the first two hazards occur frequently, farmers experienced both health crisis and market shock simultaneously during and post COVID-19 pandemic. Leveraging unique information of 461 rural households collected in the Vietnamese Mekong Delta in 2023, this research investigates the extent to which the COVID-19 pandemic hit farming household welfare as measured by income. Hence, the impacts of COVID-19 infection were analysed through two alternative proxies: (1) households with at least one infected member before vaccination; and (2) households’ perceptions of COVID-19 seriousness. The findings reveal that household income was largely negated by the COVID-19 pandemic irrespective of the proxies used. Quantile regression models uncover that the COVID-19 infection hit wealthier households harder than those in lower income groups, whereas the perception of COVID-19 seriousness had more negative influences on the lower tail of the income distribution. Further, the mediation analysis model exhibits that the pandemic directly reduced household welfare and hampered on-farm diversification in household income as a mediator. Hence, this study provides useful insight into the effectiveness of the recovery policies and the preparedness for future inevitable dangers, especially in rural communities.

title: The Impact of COVID-19 on Cyber Attack Trends
abstract: This study investigates the influence of the COVID-19 pandemic on cyberattack trends between 2018 and 2023, with a particular emphasis on the healthcare, government, and education sectors. These businesses experienced increased cyber threats during the pandemic as a result of fast digital transformation, a shift to remote employment, and reliance on personal devices without corporate-grade protection. The study uses a curated dataset from sources such as Hackmageddon and Kaggle to evaluate notable cyber occurrences, assessing shifts in both attack frequency and types, with a focus on ransomware, phishing, and DDoS attacks. The study aims to answer two main questions: did the frequency of cyberattacks rise during the pandemic, and what kinds of attacks become more common? The results show that phishing and ransomware attacks, which took advantage of pandemic-related vulnerabilities and the rise in digital communication, were very successful during this time. The study's distinctive comparison methodology covers pre-, during-, and post-pandemic periods and provides data-supported insights that highlight cybersecurity weaknesses caused by crises in important industries. Aware of the persistent cybersecurity issues brought up by the move to remote work, this study highlights the necessity of scalable, flexible security frameworks that can endure comparable future changes. It not only identifies vulnerabilities unique to a given industry, but it also offers businesses practical suggestions for enhancing their resistance to cyberthreats associated to crises. By advancing our knowledge of the dynamics of cyberattacks in the pandemic era, this research helps organizations plan for and predict dangers during international emergencies.

title: Multilingual academic publishing in Kazakhstan: language shifts during and after the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: This study aims to examine changes in the distribution of Kazakh-, Russian-, and English-language publications during and after the COVID-19 pandemic using the Eurasian Journal of Philology: Science and Education as a case study. The corpus comprises 535 articles published in Kazakh, Russian, and English between 2020 and 2025, including 278 articles from the pandemic period (2020–2022) and 257 from the post-pandemic period (2023–2025). The corpus was analysed using quantitative methods, keyword analysis, and scientometric techniques. Publication patterns were compared across the periods 2020–2022 and 2023–2025, with particular attention to the interplay between language choice, thematic focus, and the journal's disciplinary sections, including linguistics, literary studies, language teaching methodology, and translation studies. The findings reveal a statistically significant shift in the distribution of publication languages between the pandemic and post-pandemic periods, although the magnitude of the association was small. This shift was characterized by an increase in Kazakh-language publications from 38.1% to 47.1%, a decline in Russian-language publications from 30.2% to 21.0%, and a stable proportion of English-language publications (31.7% vs. The findings suggest changing patterns of language choice that may reflect shifting perceptions of linguistic prestige and the evolving roles of Kazakh, Russian, and English in academic communication. These trends reflect broader sociolinguistic transformations in the multilingual context of Kazakhstan, illustrating the interaction between internationalization of academic discourse, local language policy, and individual language use in multilingual settings.

title: Experiencias, percepciones y prácticas de personas con enfermedad renal crónica durante la pandemia de COVID-19
abstract: Objective: To understand the experiences, perceptions and practices of people with chronic kidney disease receiving haemodialysis treatment during the COVID-19 pandemic. Material and Method: A qualitative study was conducted involving 14 people with chronic kidney disease on haemodialysis treatment and residing in the Guadalajara Metropolitan Area. Semi-structured interviews were conducted, and the data were analysed using thematic content analysis. Results: Based on the participants’ narratives, the findings were organised into 5 themes: self-care practices during the pandemic; health-related dilemmas and forced decisions; clinical care and reorganisation of the health care system; emotional and social experiences; and experiences of COVID-19 infection. Chronic kidney disease was experienced as a condition that extends beyond the biomedical sphere and reshapes everyday life and care practices. The pandemic intensified vulnerability and uncertainty, highlighting structural inequalities within the health care system. Self-care emerged as a central component, mediated by socioeconomic resources, health education and family support, while hospital reorganisation and the suspension of transplantation programmes affected continuity of treatment. Conclusions: The pandemic exacerbated structural inequalities and shifted the burden of care towards patients and their families. Comprehensive care should be strengthened through multidisciplinary teams, continuity of treatment during emergencies should be ensured, and policies incorporating patients’ voices and experiences should be promoted.

title: Corporate Investment Property Holdings and Changes in Firm Performance Before and After the COVID-19 Pandemic: Heterogeneity by Financial Constraints
abstract: This study examines the relationship between corporate investment property holdings and changes in firm performance before and after the COVID-19 pandemic, with particular attention to heterogeneity by financial constraints. Using panel data on Korean listed firms from 2015 to 2024, the study defines treatment status using the average investment property ratio observed during 2015–2019. Entropy balancing is used to improve comparability between firms with high and low investment property holdings, followed by difference-in-differences and triple-difference models with firm and industry-year fixed effects. The results show that firms with higher pre-pandemic investment property holdings experienced a limited relative improvement in ROA during 2020–2024, whereas their Tobin’s Q declined relative to comparison firms. Year-specific estimates indicate that the negative relationship with Tobin’s Q was concentrated in 2020 and 2023, while annual ROA estimates were not statistically significant. The triple-difference estimates do not provide evidence that these relationships differ systematically by financial constraints. The findings suggest that investment property may be associated with medium-term changes in profitability but should not be regarded as a universal asset that enhances market value during periods of economic adjustment.

title: Analysis Of Effect of Dynamic Link Among Oil, Gold and Stock Markets of South Asian Economies During and After Covid-19
abstract: This research study investigates the dynamic connectedness among gold, oil and selected South Asian Stock markets, during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. The study collected data of gold from World gold council oil data from West Texas intermediate and stock market from Yahoo finance on daily bases for time period 2020 to 2023.we adopted the recent DCC-GARCH CONNECTEDNESS approach proposed by Gabauer (2020) to conduct a time-varying analysis that investigates the dynamic connectedness among crude oil, gold and stock markets. Unlike traditional rolling-window analysis, the DCC-GARCH offers advantages in capturing time-varying transmission mechanisms without the loss of observations. Findings show stronger connectedness between oil, gold, and stock market indices during COVID-19 than after the COVID-19 pandemic. The findings highlight gold as a potential safe haven asset during economic slumps. This suggests that investors may consider allocating a portion of their portfolios to gold to hedge against market volatility and uncertainty. We also find that during pandemic both gold and oil are receiver of shocks from the five stock markets whereas the oil and gold become net transmitter of shocks after pandemic subsidies. The empirical results show a moderate connectedness between gold, oil and south Asian stock markets which is helpful for investors and portfolio managers in the construction and reallocation of their portfolios under crises period. Policymakers to monitor and analyze volatility in oil and gold prices, and measures to address disruptions in oil demand and supply chains during pandemics. For instance, policymakers should be aware of the links between oil and gold and their effect on financial markets when preparing strategies to reduce connectedness between stock markets during pandemics and crises.

We also find that during pandemic both gold and oil are receiver of shocks from the five stock markets whereas the oil and gold become net transmitter of shocks after pandemic subsidies. The empirical results show a moderate connectedness between gold, oil and south Asian stock markets which is helpful for investors and portfolio managers in the construction and reallocation of their portfolios under crises period. Policymakers to monitor and analyze volatility in oil and gold prices, and measures to address disruptions in oil demand and supply chains during pandemics. For instance, policymakers should be aware of the links between oil and gold and their effect on financial markets when preparing strategies to reduce connectedness between stock markets during pandemics and crises.

title: Alterations in Liver Function Biomarkers Among Moderately Severe COVID‐19 Patients in southeastern Serbia: A Retrospective Single‐Center Study
abstract: Liver biochemical abnormalities have been reported in nearly half of patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection. Aim of the study was to determine the prevalence of altered liver biomarkers (ALT, AST, LDH, GGT, and albumin) in COVID-19 patients with a moderately severe clinical picture at hospital admission, and to assess the presence of altered liver-related biomarkers in the absence of a severe clinical presentation. Research material consisted of medical histories of patients with moderately severe clinical picture of COVID-19 who were hospitalised at the Clinic for Infectious Diseases of the University Clinical Centre in Niš. The study included 655 patients (425 male and 230 female) that were divided into three groups: patients without comorbidities (NC), patients with arterial hypertension (HTA), and patients previously diagnosed with diabetes mellitus (DM). Additionally, within each research group, patients were divided into three age subgroups: patients aged 20-40 years, 40-60 years, and over 60 years. AST, ALT, and LDH showed statistically significant differences across the defined groups, while GGT did not. Logistic regression confirmed increased odds for elevated AST and LDH values ​​in all older and comorbid groups, with the most pronounced effects for LDH. For ALT, significantly increased odds were observed among patients with HTA (40–60 years) and DM (40–60 years). The most pronounced changes were observed in elderly patients and those with hypertension and diabetes, with LDH emerging as the most sensitive, although non-specific, biomarker, likely reflecting systemic inflammation and disease severity in addition to possible hepatic involvement.

title: Pneumomediastinum and air leaks secondary to COVID-19: expectant vs. invasive management of a rare complication
abstract: ResumenDiversas alteraciones que, por su fisiopatología, son clasificadas en conjunto como «fugas de aire», han sido complicaciones raras de la neumonía por COVID-19.Respecto a la infección por SARS-CoV-2, se plantea el debate de si estas se clasifican como espontáneas o secundarias, ya que los múltiples mecanismos de daño estructural pulmonar que conlleva la COVID-19 condicionan fragilidad pulmonar en corto lapso.Por lo anterior, se expone el caso de una paciente de 36 años con COVID-19 complicada con neumomediastino y enfisema subcutáneo con el objetivo de ilustrar y discutir dichas complicaciones.

title: Applying the Frameworks to the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Offering a concise yet comprehensive overview, this textbook explains the fundamental concepts and frameworks that underpin the field of public health. Chapters define key terms and cover topics such as measuring health, technology, equity, leadership, health systems and reform. Real-world health issues, including COVID-19, obesity, HIV/AIDS and climate change, are used to make abstract ideas more easily digestible. Designed for students and professionals interested in public health, it includes learning objectives, illustrative examples, summaries of key takeaways, and comprehension and discussion questions to aid navigation and learning. An instructor manual and test bank are available as supplementary resources.

title: Temporal dynamics of working capital management: evidence from the Indian textile sector across COVID-19 eras
abstract: This study examines the impact of firm-specific drivers on working capital management (WCM) across distinct economic conditions among BSE-traded textile firms in India, particularly against the backdrop of the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic. This study employs static panel regression analysis on a sample of 116 textile firms by segmenting the study period into three distinct economic eras: pre-pandemic (2015–2019), during pandemic (2020–2021), and post-pandemic (2022–2024). The cash conversion cycle and working capital requirements are used as representative measures of WCM. The findings reveal that operational cash flow and leverage are consistent drivers of WCM, irrespective of the economic era. The effects of other firm-specific drivers vary by economic context, suggesting a dynamic and era-sensitive association between firm attributes and WCM. Analysts, prospective investors, and other stakeholders should emphasize crucial firm-specific drivers not only in determining liquidity management policy but also as a strategic tool for safeguarding firm's operational resilience, irrespective of the economic era. Effective management of WCM enhances workforce employment opportunities. This study enriches the existing literature by providing a longitudinal perspective on WCM in India, an emerging economy. By conducting a segment-based analysis, this study provides valuable insights into how firms adapt their WCM strategies to dynamic business contexts. This is a pioneering study that explores segment-based analysis in the Indian context.

title: IMPACTO DEL COVID-19 EN LAS FAMILIAS DE PACIENTES QUE ACUDEN AL HOSPITAL PEDIÁTRICO NIÑOS DE ACOSTA ÑU
abstract: Introduction: The pandemic caused by the coronavirus had a negative impact on multiple aspects of human life, including physical, psychological, economic, and social aspects. Objective: To describe the impact of Covid-19 on family members of patients who sought care at the Niños de Acosta Ñu Pediatric Hospital. Methods: An observational, descriptive, prospective, cross-sectional study was conducted. Family members of patients who sought care at the Niños de Acosta Ñu General Pediatric Hospital in January and February 2023 were included. The variables analyzed were age, sex, place of origin, contact with positive cases, hospitalized family member, admission to an intensive care unit, deceased family member, job loss, loss of health insurance, interruption of education, household relocation, and canceled events. Data were analyzed using SPSS through descriptive statistics. The protocol was approved by the Ethics Committee. Results: A total of 150 family members were included, with a median age of 29 years; 92.7% were female. All participants (100%) were from the Central Department. Education was interrupted in 98.7% of cases. Difficulties in obtaining medical care were reported by 71.3%. Household income decreased in 84.7%, and leisure activities were canceled in 84.7%. Exposure to coronavirus was reported by 72.3% of participants; 8% were hospitalized, and 4.7% reported the death of a family member. Parenting was considered difficult in 56% of cases. Physical well-being worsened in 82.6% of participants. Anxiety was experienced by 83.3%, and 83.3% experienced moderate psychological distress. Conclusion: According to the perception of family members of children attending a pediatric hospital, the Covid-19 pandemic caused significant psychosocial and economic repercussions, including household shortages, difficulties accessing essential services, financial hardship, job loss, interruption of education, cancellation of leisure activities, difficulties with parenting, increased anxiety, fear of infection, emotional lability, depression, insomnia, and stress among family members and children. All participants were from the Central Department, and the majority were female.
journal: Revista Ibero-Americana de Humanidades, Ciências e Educação

title: Cause-specific mortality and its rural–urban patterning across 1,890 Japanese municipalities before (2017–2019) and during (2020–2022) the COVID-19 pandemic: a nationwide small-area ecological study of rurality and deprivation
abstract: National and regional mortality summaries can conceal local inequalities. We compared cause-specific mortality and its associations with rurality and area deprivation across Japanese municipalities before and during the COVID-19 pandemic. This nationwide ecological study compared 2017–2019 with 2020–2022 across 1,890 municipalities. Expected deaths applied common pre-pandemic national age-, sex-, and cause-specific mortality rates to municipal populations estimated by interpolation to 2018.5 and extrapolation to 2021.5 from the 2015 and 2020 censuses. We calculated Empirical Bayes-smoothed standardised mortality ratios (EB-SMRs) and fitted period-specific Besag–York–Mollié 2 spatial models for 34 causes and all-cause mortality, with and without area deprivation adjustment. Pooled models with period-specific spatial fields tested period × rurality interactions. Multiplicity was assessed using Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment. Observed deaths increased by 7.3%, while the median municipal all-cause EB-SMR changed little (100.1 to 99.5). The largest decreases in median EB-SMR occurred for asthma (− 38.2), pneumonia (− 28.5), traffic accidents (− 24.4), and tuberculosis (− 21.8). Increases occurred for senility (+ 21.2), pancreatic cancer (+ 4.7), and suicide (+ 4.6; +13.5 in women), with smaller increases for liver disease, leukaemia, and renal failure. Pandemic-period deprivation-adjusted rurality rate ratios were 1.103 (95% credible interval 1.062–1.146) for traffic accidents, 1.029 (1.012–1.046) for unintentional injuries, and 1.026 (1.008–1.045) for suicide; these associations survived multiplicity adjustment. Senility showed a positive adjusted association (1.027, 1.003–1.051) that did not survive multiplicity adjustment. No period × rurality interaction identified a detectable between-period change. Under common pre-pandemic rates and period-appropriate populations, median all-cause relative mortality remained stable, while cause-specific changes varied and rural excesses persisted for external causes and, less robustly, for senility. The two-period comparison does not isolate pandemic effects from secular trends. Municipal monitoring can inform geographically targeted transport, emergency care, long-term care, and suicide-prevention planning.

title: Pseudoangiomatosis eruptiva en el embarazo asociada a COVID-19: reporte de un caso
abstract: INTRODUCCIÓN: La pseudoangiomatosis eruptiva es una dermatosis vascular infrecuente, benigna y autolimitada, caracterizada por la aparición súbita de máculo-pápulas eritematosas pequeñas con halo blanquecino periférico, de distribución predominante en cara y extremidades. Aunque es más común en la población pediátrica, también se ha descrito en adultos y, de forma excepcional, durante el embarazo. Su etiopatogenia no está completamente esclarecida, pero se ha asociado con infecciones virales y bacterianas, incluida la enfermedad por COVID-19. CASO CLÍNICO: Presentamos el caso de una mujer de 40 años, primigesta, con embarazo de 20 semanas, que desarrolló lesiones pápulo-purpúricas asintomáticas tras una infección de vías urinarias. La presentación clínica simuló vasculitis leucocitoclástica y púrpuras pigmentarias, lo que representó un reto diagnóstico. El estudio histopatológico mostró dilatación capilar y edema endotelial sin inflamación vascular, confirmando el diagnóstico de pseudoangiomatosis eruptiva. Posteriormente, durante la infección por SARS-CoV-2 confirmada por PCR, se observó exacerbación transitoria de las lesiones, con resolución espontánea aproximada del 80%. La paciente presentaba además hipotiroidismo con sustitución hormonal insuficiente. DISCUSIÓN: En el tercer trimestre se documentó restricción del crecimiento intrauterino, sin poder establecer una relación causal con la dermatosis cutánea. El embarazo culminó por cesárea a las 37 semanas de gestación, con recién nacido vivo de 2.420 gramos, sin otras complicaciones neonatales inmediatas. CONCLUSIÓN: Este caso resalta la importancia de reconocer esta entidad durante el embarazo, considerar infecciones intercurrentes como posibles desencadenantes y evitar diagnósticos y tratamientos innecesarios, reafirmando su comportamiento benigno y autolimitado desde el punto de vista cutáneo.

title: Short-term recovery of outdoor exercise after the lifting of COVID-19 restrictions in Beijing: a GPS-based study of urban environmental differences
abstract: Large infection waves can disrupt health-related physical activity even when outdoor spaces remain accessible. However, little is known about how outdoor activity recovers across different urban environments immediately after public health restrictions are lifted. This study examined short-term changes in outdoor exercise in Beijing after the lifting of COVID-19 restrictions, with particular attention to temporal phases, spatial heterogeneity and differences among urban environmental settings. We analysed 196,524 anonymised walking, running and cycling trajectories recorded by the Keep app from 13 December 2022 to 31 March 2023. Activity in January 2022 was used as a reference period. Daily trajectory counts were modelled as time series to identify recovery phases. Spatial clustering, hotspot statistics and trajectory-based counts were used to compare changes across urban green spaces, active transportation corridors and localised sports facilities, and between central and suburban areas. Outdoor exercise did not show a simple linear recovery. Four short-term phases were identified: initial stability, brief disruption, rapid rebound and later stabilisation. The main decline occurred after the infection peak, indicating a delayed behavioural response rather than an immediate reduction when restrictions were lifted. Recovery varied markedly by urban setting. After accounting for differences in spatial extent, urban green spaces showed the most stable activity intensity across phases. Active transportation corridors exhibited the largest relative increase during the rapid recovery phase, particularly in central urban areas, whereas localised sports facilities showed a later increase in activity intensity. These patterns describe differences in observed trajectory activity across exercise-space typologies rather than behavioural preferences of population groups. Spatial differences were also evident, central and suburban areas exhibited different recovery patterns in observed exercise trajectories, with variation in the timing and magnitude of activity changes. Outdoor exercise recovery after the lifting of COVID-19 restrictions was phased, delayed and spatially uneven. Analysis of spatially normalized activity intensity and trajectory changes revealed differentiated recovery patterns across exercise-space typologies: urban green spaces showed the greatest stability, active transportation corridors showed the strongest increase during early recovery, and localised sports facilities showed higher activity intensity during later recovery. These findings highlight that different exercise-space typologies exhibited distinct recovery patterns after a major public health shock.

title: Multicenter validation of longitudinal SOFA-based prognostic models for ICU triage during scarcity in mechanically ventilated COVID-19 patients
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has highlighted the need for evidence-based allocation of scarce intensive care unit (ICU) resources during periods of extreme capacity strain. Although age-based criteria have been proposed as a last resort non-medical allocation strategy in crises, incorporating longitudinal changes in a patient's clinical condition may improve medical triage. We therefore evaluated whether longitudinal sequential organ failure assessment (SOFA) trajectories could improve prognostic assessment and theoretical ICU resource utilization compared with an age-based approach. We developed and externally validated three logistic regression models using three Dutch ICU cohorts of mechanically ventilated COVID-19 patients admitted during the first waves of the pandemic: (1) SOFA score on day 1, (2) SOFA trajectory up to day 3, and (3) SOFA trajectory up to day 6 after initiation of mechanical ventilation. The models were trained on the development cohort (Maastricht University Medical Center, n = 143) and validated in two hospitals of comparable ICU size, Rijnstate Hospital, Arnhem (n = 216) and St. Antonius Hospital, Nieuwegein (n = 221). Model performance was compared with age-based triage on the date of intubation and assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), calibration plots, and decision matrices that evaluated the trade-offs between percentage of bed days gained and false positives (patients predicted to die, but who survived). Incorporating longitudinal SOFA data improved discrimination, with AUROC increasing from 0.71 (day 1 model) to 0.78 (day 3) and 0.89 (day 6) in the development cohort, with similar results in the external validation cohorts (AUROC up to 0.82 for the day 6 model). Age-based triage yielded the greatest theoretical capacity gains, but was associated with substantially more false positives. In contrast, longitudinal SOFA assessment up to day 6 resulted in fewer false positives, while preserving clinically relevant theoretical ICU capacity gains. The longitudinal SOFA-based trajectory model improved prognostic discrimination compared with the age-based triage model in critically ill COVID-19 patients. These findings suggest that longitudinal SOFA-assessment up to six days after intubation may improve prognostic support during prolonged ICU scarcity and warrant further evaluation of longitudinal SOFA trajectories as a potential component of ICU triage protocols during future healthcare crises.

title: Exploring the Role of SARS-CoV-2 in Neuroinflammation: Impact on P2X7 Receptor and Neurodegenerative Diseases
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases primarily affect the brain, leading to loss of attention, awareness, and alertness in humans. COVID-19, caused by SARS-CoV-2, has raised concerns among researchers and medical professionals due to its potential to induce neurodegenerative disorders. Despite global reports of neurological symptoms, the long-term effects of SARS-CoV-2 on the nervous system remain unclear. Complications from COVID-19 are linked to intensified immuneinflammatory reactions to the virus. SARS-CoV-2 can enter the brain via the olfactory nerve, disruption of the blood-brain barrier, or trafficking of infected immune cells across this barrier. This invasion triggers a "cytokine storm", releasing pro-inflammatory molecules into the bloodstream. Neuropsychiatric disorders and neurodegenerative diseases are often associated with neurological inflammation, blood loss, and neuron destruction caused by inflammatory mediators and viruses crossing the blood-brain barrier into the central nervous system. Consequently, SARS-CoV-2 infection may cause or worsen brain issues. Patients with conditions related to neuroimmune activation, such as Parkinson's and Alzheimer's diseases, may experience severe symptoms following SARS-CoV-2 infection. A significant factor in neuro-invasion and subsequent neuroinflammatory processes in psychiatric and neurodegenerative diseases is the stimulation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, potentially triggered by elevated extracellular ATP levels from SARS-CoV-2 infection. P2X7 receptors (P2X7Rs) in immune cells play a critical role in neuroinflammation by promoting the release of proinflammatory cytokines and ATP. These receptors contribute to the severe respiratory and neurological symptoms in COVID-19 patients, suggesting that P2X7R antagonists could be crucial in treating or preventing neurological side effects in these patients.

title: Prenatal incarceration exposure and adverse COVID-19 related experiences during pregnancy
abstract: This study examines the relationship between exposure to incarceration and stressful experiences endured during the initial months of the COVID-19 pandemic (June-December 2020). Using data from the 2020 Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (PRAMS), multiple Poisson and logistic regression models were used to assess the association between incarceration of a woman or her partner in the year before birth and the likelihood of experiencing 13 different types of adverse experiences due to the COVID-19 pandemic between June and December 2020. Results indicate that women’s incarceration exposure – either personally or vicariously through a partner – was associated with more total COVID-19 experiences. Additionally, women with incarceration exposure encountered several adverse experiences, including problems paying rent, mortgage, or bills, worried food would run out, felt more anxious, felt more depressed, had more verbal augments or conflicts with husband/partner, and husband/partner was more physically, sexually, or emotionally aggressive, than their non-incarceration-exposed counterparts. Implications of the findings for theory and public policy are discussed.

title: Policy narratives and digital compliance: comparative governance during COVID-19 in Indonesia, Japan, and China
abstract: Why do governments using broadly comparable digital governance technologies during the COVID-19 pandemic exhibit markedly different levels of observable digital compliance? Institutional capacity, technological capability, and regime characteristics help account for this variation, but they do not fully explain why similar interventions generated different trajectories as implementation unfolded. This article examines that puzzle through a qualitative comparison of Indonesia, Japan, and China, using a Most-Different Systems Design (MDSD) and a purposively constructed corpus of 45 government documents, media reports, civil society publications, and academic sources. Divergence was shaped less by the technologies themselves than by the ways official policy narratives evolved during implementation. Indonesia experienced increasing narrative fragmentation; Japan retained a relatively coherent narrative but showed limited adaptation; China combined centralized coordination with sustained narrative adaptation and consistently high observable administrative compliance. The findings suggest that institutional capability alone is insufficient to explain variation in observable compliance. What also matters is whether governing institutions can revise policy narratives as conditions change without losing sufficient coherence to sustain legitimacy. Governance legitimacy is treated here as an interpretive and institutional condition through which compliance may become durable or fragile, not as a directly measured behavioural outcome. The article extends the Narrative Policy Framework (NPF) through the concept of Narrative Velocity, which captures the capacity of governing institutions to adapt official narratives while maintaining sufficient coherence to sustain legitimacy. Bringing temporal narrative dynamics into the implementation stage expands the explanatory reach of NPF in digitally mediated governance.

title: Pattern And Distribution of Lung Findings on Chest CT and Severity Score in COVID-19 Patients Attended at National Referral Hospital in Tanzaniaia
abstract: Background: Chest computed tomography is an important imaging modality for assessing pulmonary involvement and disease severity in COVID-19, particularly where access to reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction testing is limited. Data on chest CT findings among COVID-19 patients in Tanzania, however, remain scarce. Objective: The objective of this study was to describe the pattern and distribution of pulmonary abnormalities on chest CT in adults with COVID-19, quantify disease severity using a CT severity score, and examine relationships with clinical and laboratory parameters. Methods: This was a hospital-based study of 158 adult COVID-19 patients (aged ≥18 years) referred for chest CT at Muhimbili National Hospital, Tanzania, from December 2019 to June 2022. CT images were acquired on 64- or 128-slice multi-detector scanners using a standard non-contrast protocol. CT severity scores, assigned out of 25 based on the percentage area involved in each lobe, were graded as mild (0–10), moderate (11–15), or severe (16–25). Associations between clinical and laboratory variables and CTSS were analyzed using chi-square tests; p<0.05 was considered significant. Results: The mean age was 53.67 ± 19.98 years (range 18–95); 63.92% were male and 43.03% were aged 60 years or older. Dyspnoea was the commonest presenting symptom (85.44%). All patients had abnormal scans. Bilateral involvement was seen in 91%, ground-glass opacities in 89%, peripheral distribution in 73%, and multilobar disease in 74%. Severe CTSS predominated (56.33%). Oxygen saturation below 95% was strongly related with severe findings (87.34%, p<0.001). RT-PCR was positive in 101 patients (63.92%). Notably, those without available RT-PCR results more often had severe CTSS than RT-PCR-positive patients (73.68% vs. No significant relationship was found between CTSS and inflammatory markers. Conclusion: COVID-19 was frequent in older, male patients presenting clinically with difficulty in breathing. Most patients had severe CTSS. The distribution Pulmonary involvement in COVID-19 was predominantly bilateral, peripheral, and multilobar, with ground-glass opacities the most frequent finding. Moreover, CTSS showed a positive relationship with difficulty in breathing and abnormal oxygen saturation. Chest CT is a valuable adjunct for diagnosis and severity stratification, particularly where RT-PCR testing is constrained Keywords: COVID-19; chest computed tomography; CT severity score; ground-glass opacity; pneumonia.
