title: Age, period and cohort effects in alcohol-related liver disease mortality in the United States, 1968 to 2023.
abstract: AIMS Over the past two decades, mortality from alcohol-related liver disease has rapidly increased in the United States. We aimed to describe age, period and cohort contributions to alcohol-related liver disease mortality to better understand the possible drivers of recent worsening trends. DESIGN Sex-stratified age-period-cohort analysis using national mortality data. SETTING AND CASES The United States from 1968 to 2023 (846 008 alcohol-related liver disease deaths: 246 040 for females and 599 968 for males). MEASUREMENTS We grouped sex-specific alcohol-related liver disease deaths and population estimates into 5-year age and period groups, with a top coded 85+ age group and one 6-year period from 2018 to 2023. RESULTS Alcohol-related liver disease deaths for females and males declined from approximately the years 1980 to 2000, reaching lows of 3.00 per 100 000 population for females in 2003 and 8.70 per 100 000 for males in 2006, before steadily increasing and peaking in 2021 at 7.86 per 100 000 and 17.04 per 100 000, respectively. Mortality rates remained historically elevated through 2023. Age-period-cohort models showed the highest mortality rates among females ages 50-64 and males ages 50-69. Period effects declined from 1973-1977 to 1998-2002, then steadily increased, peaking in 2018-2023. Compared with the 2008-2012 period, females had a mortality rate ratio of 1.80 [95% confidence Interval (CI) = 1.78-1.82] in 2018-2023. Model-sensitive cohort effects have increased among the youngest birth cohorts; for example, compared with the 1958-1962 cohort, males born from 1998 to 2003 had a mortality rate ratio of 2.03 (95% CI = 1.92-2.14). SUMMARY Alcohol-related liver disease deaths in the United States declined from the mid-1970s until the late 1990s before reversing, with period effects accelerating during the COVID-19 pandemic and suggestive cohort effects indicating increasing mortality risk for people born since the late 1980s. Females face disproportionate risk, consistent with their heightened susceptibility to alcohol-related liver disease and the narrowing gender gap in alcohol consumption.

title: A Qualitative Study of Awareness, Perceptions and Acceptance of Human PapillomavirusVBaccination among Female Healthcare Students in Pakistan
abstract: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination coverage remains critically low in Pakistan despite a high burden of cervical cancer. Understanding attitudes and barriers among female healthcare students is essential for designing effective interventions. This qualitative study explored knowledge, attitudes, hesitancy drivers, and recommended strategies for HPV vaccination among female healthcare students in Pakistan. This qualitative study used face-to-face semi-structured interviews with 20 female medical students from public and private institutions in Islamabad and Rawalpindi, Pakistan. Data were collected from December 2025 to February 2026. Inductive thematic analysis was performed following Braun and Clarke’s framework. Participants were generally aware that HPV vaccination prevents cervical cancer; however, in-depth scientific understanding was limited. While most trusted the vaccine’s effectiveness, many remained skeptical of government-led vaccination programs, reflecting lingering distrust following the COVID-19 pandemic. Healthcare practitioners, particularly gynecologists, were regarded as the most reliable sources of vaccination recommendations. Misconceptions linking HPV vaccination to infertility were identified as the primary cultural obstacle, impacting perceptions even among participants who rejected the notion. Protecting adolescent girls from cervical cancer was one of the strongest motivators for vaccination acceptance. Participants favored informed choices over compulsory vaccination and advocated for culturally tailored, multi-channel awareness campaigns, involvement of religious scholars, large-scale public education, and healthcare practitioners’ visible endorsement, such as vaccinating their own children. Among this sample of female medical students in Pakistan, awareness of HPV vaccination was often superficial and accompanied by institutional distrust and perpetual infertility-related misconceptions. Enhancing HPV vaccination acceptance requires multifaceted strategies that extend beyond awareness alone, emphasizing trusted healthcare practitioners, open communication, and culturally sensitive, research-based messaging to promote public confidence in immunization programs. Additional qualitative and quantitative studies including more diverse populations are warranted to validate and extend the generalizability of these findings.

title: A Data-Driven Econometric Analysis of the Time-Varying Hedge and Safe Haven Properties of Gold and Silver in Emerging
abstract: Precious metals play an important role in portfolio diversification and financial risk management, particularly during periods of economic uncertainty and stock market instability. However, their defensive properties may vary depending on market conditions and the intensity of financial shocks. This study aims to examine the time-varying hedging and safe-haven properties of gold and silver in the Indian stock market, with particular attention to their capacity to protect investors during periods of financial stress. The research employs daily price data for the BSE SENSEX, gold, and silver covering January 2003 to December 2023. The methodological framework combines descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, Dynamic Conditional Correlation Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity (DCC-GARCH) modelling, and quantile regression to assess asset dependence under normal and extreme market conditions. The results reveal substantial differences in the defensive characteristics of the two metals. Gold exhibits a weak negative average correlation with the BSE SENSEX (-0.08), which becomes more pronounced during the Global Financial Crisis (-0.21) and the COVID-19 pandemic (-0.18). Quantile regression produces negative coefficients for gold at the 0.05 (-0.28) and 0.10 (-0.21) quantiles, indicating potential safe-haven properties during severe equity market downturns. Conversely, silver demonstrates a weak positive average correlation with stock returns (0.12) and positive coefficients across all examined quantiles, suggesting limited protective capacity during extreme market conditions. The findings indicate that gold exhibits more consistent defensive characteristics than silver, while its protective properties remain dependent on market conditions. The study contributes to understanding the dynamic relationships between precious metals and equity markets and provides insights relevant to portfolio diversification and financial risk management in emerging economies. Further research should incorporate additional emerging markets, alternative safe-haven assets, structural break models, and volatility spillover analysis to examine the robustness of these relationships across different financial environments.

title: Trends in mortality involving chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and obesity in the United States, 1999-2023: A population-based observational study.
abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and obesity are major US public health conditions that frequently coexist. Despite adverse respiratory and cardiometabolic effects of obesity, an apparent "obesity paradox," whereby obesity has been associated with lower mortality in some patients with COPD, has been described. National mortality trends involving concurrent COPD and obesity remain poorly characterized. We examined temporal, demographic, and geographic patterns from 1999 to 2023. We conducted a retrospective, population-based analysis of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Wide-ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research Multiple Cause of Death database. Deaths among adults aged ≥25 years listing COPD (International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision: J40-J44) and obesity (International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision: E66) were identified. Age-adjusted mortality rates per 100,000 were calculated using direct standardization to the 2000 US population. Joinpoint Regression Program version 5.3.0.0 estimated annual percent changes (APCs) and average annual percent changes with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Analyses were stratified by age, sex, race/ethnicity, region, urbanization, and state. Among 1,30,958 deaths, the age-adjusted mortality rate increased from 0.78 (95% CI: 0.74-0.82) in 1999 to 2.63 (95% CI: 2.57-2.68) in 2023 (average annual percent change: +5.14%; 95% CI: 4.09-6.21; P < .001). After increasing significantly through 2013, mortality increased nonsignificantly during 2013 to 2018 (APC: +2.11%; 95% CI: -0.39 to 4.67), rose markedly during 2018 to 2021 (APC: +17.45%; 95% CI: 10.18-25.19), and declined significantly through 2023 (APC: -13.47%; 95% CI: -18.32 to -8.34). Males and adults aged ≥65 years had higher mortality burdens, with variation across racial/ethnic groups, urbanization levels, regions, and states. Interpretation is limited by unavailable individual-level factors, including smoking, COPD severity, comorbidities, and socioeconomic characteristics. Mortality involving concurrent COPD and obesity increased substantially from 1999 to 2023, with marked demographic and geographic variation and an increase during the COVID-19 pandemic. These population-level associations do not establish causality. Integrated pulmonary and metabolic care, targeted prevention, and improved access in underserved communities may help address observed disparities.

title: Immune-effector and infection-associated reporting patterns of CD20×CD3 bispecific antibodies in B-cell lymphoma: a label-anchored FAERS analysis with descriptive JADER contextualization
abstract: CD20×CD3 bispecific antibodies are associated with acute immune-effector toxicities and infections, but drug-specific postmarketing co-reporting and report-level onset patterns remain incompletely characterized in B-cell lymphoma. We performed a label-anchored FAERS pharmacovigilance analysis with descriptive JADER contextualization. Deduplicated FAERS reports from 2022 Q4 through 2026 Q1 were restricted to primary-suspect epcoritamab, glofitamab, or mosunetuzumab reports in B-cell lymphoma, yielding 2,879 exposed reports. Prespecified MedDRA endpoints were evaluated against a disease-restricted comparator. Primary adjusted reporting odds ratios (aRORs) accounted for demographics, disease subgroup, reporting region, and calendar year. We mapped report-level phenotype intersections, summarized time to onset (TTO), and performed model-specification, restriction, comparator-exclusion, and TTO-completeness analyses. The cohort included 1,463 epcoritamab, 944 glofitamab, and 472 mosunetuzumab reports. CRS had higher primary adjusted reporting odds for epcoritamab (aROR 4.70, 95% CI 4.15 to 5.32), glofitamab (3.43, 2.94 to 4.00), and mosunetuzumab (6.23, 4.97 to 7.81). ICANS had higher reporting odds for epcoritamab (2.28, 1.87 to 2.80); the glofitamab estimate crossed 1 in the primary model (1.26, 0.93 to 1.70) and varied with covariate specification, while mosunetuzumab ICANS was sparse. Epcoritamab had higher reporting odds for CMV (4.54, 3.66 to 5.62) and narrow opportunistic infection (2.20, 1.84 to 2.63). Mosunetuzumab had higher reporting odds for pneumonia/lower respiratory infection (1.74, 1.32 to 2.31) and COVID-19 (1.66, 1.25 to 2.21), although these infection-specific patterns attenuated in some geographic and calendar restrictions. Immune-effector and infectious phenotypes co-occurred in reports containing serious outcomes. TTO was calculable for 33.7%–61.2% of reports and suggested earlier CRS than infection-associated reporting, but report characteristics differed by TTO completeness. CRS was the clearest shared reporting pattern across the three CD20×CD3 antibodies. Neurotoxicity and infection-associated findings were more drug- and analysis-dependent. Report-level co-reporting supports concurrent consideration of inflammatory toxicity and infection when presentations overlap, while later infection-associated TTO distributions support continued awareness beyond step-up dosing. Spontaneous-reporting data cannot estimate incidence, causality, or comparative treatment risk.

title: DNA and RNA Helices as Antennae for Sonic and Electromagnetic Communication
abstract: In addition to the electrogenic microorganisms, e.g., bacteria, that can be found in communities that are wired together in circuits carrying electrons in and out of biological cells, strong evidence exists that there are wireless connections between micro-organisms that pass information to one another at a distance in virtue of electromagnetic signals. One needs electromagnetic antennae to send or receive signals as they pass information back and forth between living microorganisms. We here discuss the properties of DNA and RNA long polymer molecules regarding their utility as antennae. As well as emitting or absorbing radiation photons, these antennae also emit and absorb phonons, i.e., acoustic signals. The coupling between sound waves and electromagnetic waves is very appreciable and is described by biological piezoelectricity. Biological phases of condensed matter also exhibit chiral symmetry breaking, i.e., “handedness” symmetry breaking, between right- and left-handed electronic states. Describing two spin components (say up and down) times two chirality components (say left and right) ultimately requires four-component electron wave functions as discovered by Dirac even if the electrons are moving at velocities much less than light speed. Coupled with the quasi-one-dimensional nature of long polymer molecules, this yields bound Bose-condensed particle-hole pairs constituting a Tomonaga–Luttinger liquid similar in some ways to the Bardeen–Cooper–Schriefer Bose-condensed bound electron pairs found in superconductors. One similarity is that transport weak links in the Bose condensate fluid flow yield Josephson effects described by a quantum pendulum, e.g., a sine-Gordon field theory. The coherent phase in the Tomonaga–Luttinger liquid is the difference between the right- and left-handed electronic phases, as first demonstrated by Coleman via the conversion of the massive Thirring model into a Josephson-type pendulum model. The complete theory of wireless communication between biological organisms is only beginning to be developed. The basic DNA and RNA microbe antennae must be wired in nature as a coherent phased antenna array for appreciable communication bit rates radiated through large distances. Finally, acoustic and/or radio frequency electromagnetic radiation carrying sufficient communication information should be of use medically as a possible alternative to chemical medicines and/or vaccines in the treatment of illness; for a most recent example in the COVID-19 virus with its RNA internal antenna.

title: Evaluation of Educational and Occupational Determinants on Societal Compliance with Health Protocols During the Pandemic Period in Indonesia
abstract: While non-pharmaceutical interventions are critical for pandemic mitigation, empirical evidence regarding the structural and socioeconomic determinants of public compliance during epidemic transitions remains fragmented in developing economies. Existing literature primarily focuses on broad epidemiological trends without identifying how specific demographic strata navigate behavioral adherence during the pandemic transition phase. To bridge this literature gap, this study investigates the demographic and occupational determinants of health protocol compliance in Indonesia, establishing an analytical framework to differentiate between self-directed preventive behaviors and institutionally enforced adherence. A quantitative cross-sectional study was conducted using a digital convenience sampling strategy across Indonesian provinces. Data were collected from 506 validated respondents via a structured 35-item instrument evaluating behavioral adherence, implementation process, and environmental readiness. Bivariate inferential analyses were conducted using Pearson’s Chi-Square tests at a significance threshold of p 0.05), and physical distancing remained uniform across occupations (p = 0.195). These findings demonstrate that public compliance is bifurcated into institutionally enforced adherence and cognition-driven adherence. Effective epidemic containment requires dual-track intervention strategies, maintaining administrative enforcement in formal workplaces while deploying targeted educational outreach for informal and independent workforces.Keywords: COVID-19, Public Health Compliance, Health Behavior, Occupational Health, Health Literacy.

title: Post-pandemic inflation: A look through the lens of modern monetary theory (MMT) and mainstream economics
abstract: Inflation management in developed countries in the post‐COVID‐19 period. To critically assess the effectiveness of traditional monetary instruments (interest rate hikes) versus alternative fiscal approaches under Modern Monetary Theory (MMT) in the context of post‐pandemic inflation. A comparative historical and economic analysis is applied, using empirical data from the USA, Europe, and Japan, along with a decomposition of inflationary factors according to A. Shapiro’s methodology. It was found that traditional monetary instruments proved to be largely ineffective against inflation driven by supply‐side shocks (supply chain disruptions, energy crisis). Despite rate hikes, central banks were unable to quickly bring inflation back to target levels. The MMT‐oriented approach, focused on fiscal measures — targeted subsidies, investment in capacity, and cost compensation — demonstrated effectiveness, as illustrated by the case of Japan. Policy instruments need to be adapted to the nature of inflationary shocks: in the case of supply‐driven inflation, fiscal measures may be more effective and less detrimental than monetary tightening. The study contributes to the discussion on the role of central banks and substantiates the potential for synergy between monetary and fiscal instruments for macroeconomic stabilization in the post‐pandemic period.

Shapiro’s methodology. It was found that traditional monetary instruments proved to be largely ineffective against inflation driven by supply‐side shocks (supply chain disruptions, energy crisis). Despite rate hikes, central banks were unable to quickly bring inflation back to target levels. The MMT‐oriented approach, focused on fiscal measures — targeted subsidies, investment in capacity, and cost compensation — demonstrated effectiveness, as illustrated by the case of Japan. Policy instruments need to be adapted to the nature of inflationary shocks: in the case of supply‐driven inflation, fiscal measures may be more effective and less detrimental than monetary tightening. The study contributes to the discussion on the role of central banks and substantiates the potential for synergy between monetary and fiscal instruments for macroeconomic stabilization in the post‐pandemic period.

title: An atlas of sarbecovirus infectivity across diverse ACE2 orthologs
abstract: Sarbecoviruses pose a substantial zoonotic threat, yet the determinants governing their host range remain incompletely defined. To systematically investigate host entry mechanisms, we generated a panel of vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) pseudoviruses representing 46 sarbecoviruses and assessed their infectivity across 66 angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) orthologs. This analysis produced a high-resolution host-entry landscape with direct implications for cross-species transmission risk. We found that all severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 1 (SARS-CoV-1) isolates, WIV1, and pangolin-derived sarbecoviruses demonstrated broad ACE2 usage, whereas no sarbecovirus utilized alternative entry factors including neuropilin-1, CD147, AXL, or TMEM106B. Notably, ACE2 orthologs from Rhinolophus affinis and Miniopterus schreibersii supported infection by nearly all clade 1 sarbecoviruses, identifying highly permissive host receptors. We also identified residues 27 and 42 of ACE2 as critical determinants of sarbecovirus host tropism. Together, these findings define host entry constraints relevant to receptor-based risk assessment and inform surveillance and pandemic preparedness.

title: การศกษายอนหลงการตดเชอไวรสอะดโนในโรงพยาบาลรามาธบด (พ.ศ. 2555-2565): การวเคราะหปจจยเสยงผานวธการตรวจวนจฉย ดวยการเพมปรมาณกรดนวคลอกในหองปฏบตการไวรสวทยา
abstract: Human adenovirus (HAdV) has been identified as a significant causative agent of infection, affecting patients of all age demographics. The present retrospective study was conducted with the objective of investigating the association of risk factors with adenovirus infection. An analysis was conducted on data from the Virology Laboratory, Department of Pathology, Faculty of Medicine, Ramathibodi Hospital, from 2012 to 2022. The study included a total of 46,128 individuals. The study identified 2,348 infections (5.09%), with the highest number of infections (436, 9.86%) recorded in 2013. In particular, the infection rate was found to be higher in children under 12 years. The former group included toddlers (8.46%), preschoolers (9.17%), and school-aged children (6.11%), with the infection rate greather than for the newborn and infant being 3.92%. Correlation analysis was performed Multivariable logistic regression analysis revealed that toddlers (Adjusted OR=2.12, 95% CI=1.74-2.57), preschoolers (Adjusted OR=2.41, 95% CI=1.95-2.97), and school-aged children (Adjusted OR=1.63, 95% CI=1.26-2.12) had a significantly higher risk of adenovirus infection than newborns and young children, respectively. There was no significant difference in infection risk between males and females. The sample with the highest incidence of adenovirus infection was nasal rinse fluid (Adjusted OR=1.82, 95% CI=1.28-2.59), followed by throat swabs (Adjusted OR=1.70, 95% CI=1.25-2.32). The findings reported herein pertain to adenovirus infection in the period preceding the advent of the pandemic caused by the severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS)-coronavirus (CoV-2). The levels were found to be significantly higher than during the post-pandemic period, with an observed increase of 1.93 times (Adjusted OR=1.93, 95% CI=1.52-2.44). These findings have the potential to inform the enhancement of medical and public health preparedness in anticipation of future adenovirus outbreaks, thereby facilitating more effective responses.

title: The Role of T1 and T2 Mapping in the Diagnosis of Different Types of Myocarditis
abstract: Myocarditis is a heterogeneous inflammatory disease of the myocardium with a wide etiologic spectrum and highly variable clinical course, ranging from subclinical forms to severe heart failure and sudden cardiac death. Its diagnosis is particularly challenging in subacute, chronic and post-COVID presentations.Aim. To evaluate the diagnostic and clinical value of T1 and T2 mapping and extracellular volume quantification in patients with acute, healed, post-COVID and chronic myocarditis, as well as in the recovery phase, in comparison with established reference values.Materials and methods. Between January 2023 and October 2025, 166 patients (42 children, 124 adults) with suspected myocarditis underwent CMR at 1.5 T using a standardised protocol including native T1 and T2 mapping, post-contrast T1 mapping for extracellular volume calculation.Results. Acute myocarditis was confirmed in 31 patients, who showed markedly reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (40.4±12.8 %) and significantly increased native T1 mapping (1131±82 ms), T2 (54.7±5.6 ms) and extracellular volume (33.1±5.8 %; all p<0.0001). In 116 patients with healed myocarditis, including 67 (57.8 %) with prior COVID-19, left ventricular ejection fraction was moderately reduced (49.3±13.8 %), T2 mapping values were near-normal, whereas T1 mapping (1035.8±100.7 ms) and extracellular volume (28.6±4.2 %) remained elevated. No significant differences in T1, T2 mapping or extracellular volume were found between post-COVID and non-COVID subgroups. In seven patients in the recovery phase, T2 nearly normalized while T1 mapping and extracellular volume remained mildly increased, whereas six patients with chronic myocarditis exhibited the lowest left ventricular ejection fraction (27.2±3.9 %) and the highest T1 mapping and extracellular volume values, consistent with advanced fibrotic remodelling. Serial CMR in six patients confirmed a pronounced decrease in T2 with relatively stable or slightly elevated extracellular volume over time.Conclusions. These findings underscore the pivotal role of T1, T2 mapping and extracellular volume as quantitative biomarkers for phase differentiation, detection of post-COVID myocardial involvement and longitudinal monitoring in myocarditis.

title: The Impact of Best Practice Meetings on Outcomes of Esophageal Cancer Surgery in the Netherlands.
abstract: BACKGROUND National best practice meetings, combining transparent hospital-level benchmarking and peer-to-peer learning, were introduced in the Netherlands in 2018 to improve outcomes after esophagectomy. This study aimed to investigate the impact of these meetings on national outcomes following esophageal cancer surgery. METHODS This nationwide population-based cohort study included patients who underwent esophagectomy for cancer registered in the Dutch Upper Gastrointestinal Cancer Audit between 2011 and 2023. Best practice meetings were organized annually from 2018 onwards, except in 2020 because of the COVID-19 pandemic. The primary outcome was the national anastomotic leakage rate. Secondary outcomes included qualitative outcomes and actions after the meetings, assessed using a structured questionnaire. Multilevel multivariable logistic regression compared outcomes 2 years before and after the meetings held in 2018, 2019, and 2021. RESULTS A total of 9166 patients were included. Anastomotic leakage increased from 18.6% in 2011 to 20.3% in 2017, then decreased to 14.0% in 2023. Significant overall reductions were observed after the meetings of 2019 (odds ratio 0.65; 95% confidence interval 0.52-0.82) and 2021 (odds ratio 0.78; 95% confidence interval 0.62-0.99). Declines were observed in both cervical and intrathoracic anastomoses. All centers reported implementing improvement actions after the meetings, with 71% rating the meetings as positive and 29% as very positive. Actions included structured site visits and adjustments to surgical techniques, protocols, and care pathways, with key focus areas including anastomotic leakage, lymphadenectomy, and length of hospital stay. CONCLUSIONS Annual best practice meetings were associated with outcome-oriented actions and significant reductions in national anastomotic leakage rates, suggesting that transparent peer-to-peer sharing of hospital-level outcome data may improve outcomes of esophageal cancer surgery.

title: Generalized Ordered Rough Set Models via Minimal and Maximal Neighborhoods Induced by Binary Relations
abstract: Classical Pawlak rough set theory is fundamentally based on equivalence relations, which limits its ability to represent uncertainty arising from non-equivalent and ordered information. This paper develops a generalized ordered rough set framework in which binary relations are combined with partial order structures to construct minimal and maximal neighborhood systems. Based on these neighborhoods, generalized increasing and decreasing approximation operators are introduced and systematically related to the corresponding right-neighborhood model. The proposed framework establishes fundamental inclusion, boundary, and accuracy relationships between the minimal and maximal models, showing in particular that minimal neighborhoods generally yield tighter approximations, whereas maximal neighborhoods produce wider uncertainty regions. Six associated nano-topological structures, together with their basis representations, are constructed for the right, minimal, and maximal neighborhood systems, providing a unified topological setting for the analysis of ordered uncertainty. The theoretical developments are further connected with several established rough set models, demonstrating the generality of the proposed constructions. A topological attribute-reduction procedure is then developed to identify dispensable and indispensable attributes through changes in the induced structural patterns. In addition, the proposed m-Nano Flou measure is employed as a complementary structural-sensitivity criterion for quantitatively characterizing the effects of attribute removal. A COVID-19 medical information system adopted from a published study is used to illustrate the applicability of the framework to ordered medical information. The obtained rankings are interpreted exclusively in terms of structural influence within the proposed approximation framework and do not represent clinical importance or diagnostic performance. The proposed approach therefore provides a flexible mathematical framework for modeling and analyzing uncertainty in ordered information systems beyond the restrictive equivalence-relation setting of classical rough sets.

title: NGHIÊN CỨU MARKETING ĐỊA ĐIỂM THÀNH PHỐ DU LỊCH THÔNG QUA TỔ CHỨC SỰ KIỆN THỂ THAO
abstract: Nghiên cứu này khảo sát các hiệu ứng Marketing địa điểm của Sự kiện Thể thao tại Việt Nam. Trường hợp thực nghiệm là SEA Games 31 - Đại hội Thể thao Đông Nam Á lần thứ 31 được tổ chức tại Hà Nội và các tỉnh thành phía Bắc Việt Nam vào năm 2022. Thông qua việc phân tích các chiến lược Marketing địa điểm của các tỉnh/thành phố đăng cai (Host Cities), nghiên cứu điều tra cơ chế tạo ra hình ảnh điểm đến thông qua nghi lễ thể thao, sự kiện văn hóa bổ sung và hiệu ứng lan tỏa kinh tế. Bài báo cũng đề cập đến vai trò của truyền thông trong việc thần thoại hóa các địa điểm thi đấu. Tác giả nhận thấy, SEA Games 31 với tư cách là Sự kiện Thể thao đa địa điểm, hoạt động như một bộ phát sinh Lễ hội có hệ thống tại Việt Nam, đồng thời là cú hích quan trọng cho sự phục hồi du lịch sau đại dịch COVID-19.

title: Respiratory panel detections, inflammatory biomarkers, and length of stay in children hospitalized with acute respiratory tract infections: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Qualitative respiratory-panel detections and inflammatory markers are often considered together in hospitalized children, but neither identifies the cause of illness on its own. We examined associations between panel detections and routinely recorded biomarkers, radiographic findings, and length of stay (LOS). This retrospective study included children aged ≤ 18 years hospitalized with acute respiratory tract infections at Hangzhou Children’s Hospital, China, between 5 January 2023 and 17 June 2025. A 13-target pharyngeal-swab assay was summarized as 11 analytical groups. Primary outcomes were high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) ≥20 mg/L, procalcitonin (PCT) ≥0.5 ng/mL, and LOS ≥ 7 days. Complete-case logistic models adjusted for age group, sex, testing year, and season. Sensitivity analyses assessed continuous biomarkers, multiple-target detections, recorded severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) positivity, and sampling within 24 or 48 hours of admission using source records and chart-reviewed intervals. Among 6093 children, 2076 were panel-negative, 3343 had single-target detection, and 674 had multiple-target detection. Compared with panel-negative children, human adenovirus detection was associated with hsCRP ≥ 20 mg/L (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.19; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.63–2.96) and PCT ≥ 0.5 ng/mL (aOR, 1.93; 95% CI, 1.34–2.77). Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP) detection was associated with LOS ≥ 7 days (aOR, 2.57; 95% CI, 1.99–3.31) and lower odds of PCT ≥ 0.5 ng/mL (aOR, 0.22; 95% CI, 0.13–0.37). The MP–LOS aORs were 2.50 (1.82–3.44) and 2.76 (2.12–3.59) in the 24-hour and 48-hour subsets. Multiple-target detection was also associated with LOS ≥ 7 days (aOR, 2.21; 95% CI, 1.73–2.82). Detection groups differed in recorded biomarker and hospitalization measures. Early-sampling restrictions supported the persistence of the MP–LOS association but did not establish causation. Unmeasured bacterial infection, treatment, illness severity, and clinical selection preclude pathogen-causal or prognostic interpretation.

title: Spatial compartmentalization shapes distinct germinal center states during respiratory viral infection
abstract: Germinal centers (GCs) typically arise within the lymph node cortex, where follicular dendritic cell (FDC) networks and follicular helper T cells coordinate B-cell expansion, affinity maturation, and durable immunity. Whether proliferating B-cell aggregates in the medulla engage bona fide GC programs or instead represent a distinct GC-like differentiation state remains unresolved. In this study, using mediastinal lymph nodes from SARS-CoV-2-infected cynomolgus macaques, we combined immunofluorescence with Xenium spatial transcriptomics to identify LYVE1+ sinus-associated medullary GC structures (mGCs) alongside conventional cortical GCs (cGCs). mGCs shared core GC-associated modules with cGCs but showed niche-divergent features, including increased expression of PRDM1, MZB1, and VWF and decreased expression of IRF8, CD27, and CD86. mGCs retained organized follicular architecture but showed lower CD4+ T and GC B cell densities, greater plasma cell representation, and enrichment of pDCs, NK cells, and stromal populations. Compared with cGCs, mGCs lacked polarized CD35+ FDC and CD3+ T cell network topology, exhibited reduced CXCL12 availability, and showed a higher IgM/IgG ratio. During early reinfection, medullary secondary follicles contracted sharply and were associated with higher Foxp3+ cell density. These findings support a model in which lymph node microanatomy imprints a distinct mGC state, diversifying humoral immune architecture during respiratory viral infection.

In this study, using mediastinal lymph nodes from SARS-CoV-2-infected cynomolgus macaques, we combined immunofluorescence with Xenium spatial transcriptomics to identify LYVE1+ sinus-associated medullary GC structures (mGCs) alongside conventional cortical GCs (cGCs). mGCs shared core GC-associated modules with cGCs but showed niche-divergent features, including increased expression of PRDM1, MZB1, and VWF and decreased expression of IRF8, CD27, and CD86. mGCs retained organized follicular architecture but showed lower CD4+ T and GC B cell densities, greater plasma cell representation, and enrichment of pDCs, NK cells, and stromal populations. Compared with cGCs, mGCs lacked polarized CD35+ FDC and CD3+ T cell network topology, exhibited reduced CXCL12 availability, and showed a higher IgM/IgG ratio. During early reinfection, medullary secondary follicles contracted sharply and were associated with higher Foxp3+ cell density. These findings support a model in which lymph node microanatomy imprints a distinct mGC state, diversifying humoral immune architecture during respiratory viral infection.

title: Global ve Ülke Bazlı Risklerin Turizm Sektörüne Etkileri Türkiye Örneği
abstract: Bu çalışma, 2012–2024 döneminde global ve ülke bazlı risklerin Türkiye turizm sektörünün finansal piyasa performansı üzerindeki etkisini incelemektedir. BIST Turizm Endeksi getirisi ve anormal getirisi bağımlı değişken olarak kullanılmış; ülke bazlı turizm göstergeleri, makroekonomik değişkenler ve küresel risk göstergeleri açıklayıcı değişkenler olarak ele alınmıştır. Analizlerde birim kök, değişen varyans ve otokorelasyon testleri uygulanmış, Newey-West HAC standart hataları ve COVID-19 kukla değişkeni kullanılmıştır. Bulgular turist sayısı, turizm geliri ve döviz kurunun pozitif; enflasyon, faiz, ABD tahvil faizi, VIX ve jeopolitik riskin negatif ilişkili olduğunu göstermektedir. Sonuçlar, turizm sektörünün çok boyutlu risk yapısı içinde değerlendirilmesi ve finansal açıdan izlenmesi gerektiğini ortaya koymaktadır.

title: LE DISCOURS MARTIAL DE MACRON: AVATARS DU TERME « GUERRE »
abstract: Our study focuses on the martial language used by the French President Emmanuel Macron in two of his recent speeches. The purpose of our approach is to identify the linguistic and rhetorical means on which the President’s discourse is built and the communicational aim envisaged. The first speech, dating from the 16th of March 2020, is centered on the term “guerre” (“war”) used in a metaphorical sense to designate the fight against the SARS-CoV-2 virus, whereas the second message, delivered on the 31st of December 2023, is based on the concept of “réarmement” (“rearmament”), employed in various contexts of public life. The analysis of the French president’s discourse shows that martial language is resorted to with the purpose of strengthening social cohesion and general compliance, but also of building a meliorative image of the speaker in the eyes of the French people.

title: An Examination of Psychosocial Processes Related to Quality of Life in Pregnancy
abstract: Perinatal anxiety and potential protective processes are often poorly understood compared to other types of perinatal distress. The present study investigated the relationship between perinatal anxiety and quality of life or life satisfaction in a pregnant sample. Psychological flexibility and self-compassion were examined as moderators of these associations. COVID-19 and other external factors were examined on an exploratory basis. Results indicate significant correlations between perinatal anxiety and satisfaction with life, as well as psychological flexibility and perinatal anxiety; proposed interaction effects were not significant. This study may enhance understanding of these processes and contribute to the growing field of reproductive psychology.
journal: Journal of prenatal & perinatal psychology & health

title: Extensão universitária como meio para obtenção de etanol a partir de bebidas apreendidas
abstract: A Receita Federal do Brasil realiza operações ostensivas de apreensão de bebidas alcoólicas, principalmente em regiões de fronteira. Depois de aprendidas, as bebidas passam a ser um resíduo com potencial de impacto ambiental, que deve ser processado para a destinação final correta. Este trabalho advém de um projeto de extensão universitária surgido durante a pandemia da COVID-19, voltado à produção de álcool e sabão líquido para higienização, a partir da transformação destas bebidas enviadas à UFPR, em parceria com a Receita Federal do Brasil. Passada a crise na saúde, foi dada continuidade nas ações, todavia, com um novo direcionamento, estudar a viabilidade do processo de destilação para produzir etanol hidratado combustível (EHC) visando sua utilização nos veículos do campus universitário da UFPR, Setor Palotina. Foram realizadas análises físico-químicas de rotina em amostras antes e após a destilação desta bebida, seguindo os parâmetros da Resolução No 907/2022 da Agência Nacional do Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis - ANP. Os testes incluíram avaliação da cor, aspecto, condutividade elétrica, massa específica, potencial hidrogeniônico (pH), teor alcoólico e acidez total. As bebidas analisadas apresentaram características semelhantes a bebidas do tipo vinho, enquanto o etanol produzido no processo de destilação atendeu, em grande parte, aos limites estabelecidos pela normativa vigente. A amostra de etanol E3 obtida a partir da amostra de bebida B3 destacou-se por estar próxima da especificação, necessitando de ajustes mínimos. O trabalho ganha importância ao propor uma solução para um problema real, considerando especialmente, os casos de contrabando de bebidas e os casos de bebidas contendo metanol veiculadas no Brasil recentemente, no ano de 2025. Utilizando princípios de economia circular e sustentabilidade, este trabalho apresenta resultados concretos a respeito de um simples processamento de um resíduo com potencial poluidor, de maneira a promover sua transformação em um produto de valor agregado, aproveitando internamente em uma instituição pública.

title: Persistent Borrelia burgdorferi protein antigen in CD16+ monocytes is associated with monocyte-skewed immune dysregulation in post-treatment Lyme disease syndrome (PTLDS)
abstract: Post-treatment Lyme disease syndrome (PTLDS) is characterized by persistent symptoms after antibiotic therapy for Borrelia burgdorferi infection. The mechanisms underlying these symptoms remain incompletely understood and have been attributed to ongoing low-level infection, autoimmunity, or immune dysregulation driven by residual bacterial antigens. We investigated whether Borrelia burgdorferi protein antigen persists in long-lived monocyte subsets in PTLDS patients and is associated with broader immune dysregulation. CD14CD16 monocytes from 10 patients with PTLDS were analyzed by mass spectrometry; plasma from all 10 was profiled on a 14-plex cytokine panel against 50 healthy donors; PBMCs from 6 patients (3 antigen-positive and 3 antigen-negative) underwent RT-qPCR and bulk RNA-seq with immune-compartment profiling. FlaB and OspC were detected in CD14CD16 monocytes months to years after treatment, whereas Borrelia burgdorferi transcript was not detected. Plasma IFN-{gamma} exceeded the healthy donor median in all 10 participants. Antigen-positive samples showed an antigen-associated inflammatory transcriptional profile, including increased TNFSF14/LIGHT, GSDMD, GBP5, and KCNJ2 expression, together with a compartment-level pattern of monocyte-skewed myeloid reconfiguration, higher neutrophil-related features, and selective T-cell-state changes. These findings link residual Borrelia burgdorferi protein in CD14CD16 monocytes to monocyte-skewed immune remodeling in PTLDS, paralleling observations in long COVID and supporting a model in which post-infectious syndromes are sustained by antigen-fueled immune remodeling rather than ongoing infection.
